News.title: School ‘ignored teacher, 29, taking sick photos of young girls because they thought he was gay’ a year before arrest
News.content:
WARPED TEACHER School ‘ignored teacher, 29, taking sick photos of young girls because they thought he was gay’ a year before arrest







Next

A TEACHER accused of taking inappropriate photos of girls was allegedly ignored by the school despite multiple complaints because they thought he was gay, according to a lawsuit.

Travis Shojinaga, 39, was first reported to staff by concerned parents more than a year before his arrest in February, court documents show.



The Viewpoint school teacher in California has been charged with child molestation and possession of child pornography, the lawsuit says.

A student and another girl accused the educator of taking upskirt and upshirt photos with his phone in December 2024, the documents say.



The lawsuit reads: “The children reported that Shojinaga had been sitting with them at lunch, placing his telephone beneath the table, and making them uncomfortable, and that the conduct was not limited.”

Following the ordeal, a concerned parent complained to the head of lower school Claudia Antoine.

read more us news BABY SHOCK Mom of 16 'feral kids' found in house of horrors appears PREGNANT in court

But she allegedly expressed confusion at the allegation before claiming Shojinaga “bats for the other team”, documents show.

Viewpoint concluded the parent’s enquiry was a possible “misunderstanding”, the lawsuit says.



It also argues school bosses allegedly “made no meaningful attempt to determine whether the allegation was true” or inspected Shojinaga’s phone.

The suspect was arrested in February this year and his alleged abuse was revealed in a public complaint filed by DA Nathan Hochman.

Prosecutors allege he filmed secret videos “up the shirts of the 4th and 5th grade female students that he teaches”.

Shojinaga has been accused of recording 10 and 11-year-old girls by bending down and pretending to pick up rubbish or tie his shoes, court documents say.

According to court filings, he allegedly told authorities he had an “addiction” and confessed to taking up to 60 recordings.



He claimed these alleged acts “made his heart race”, court papers show.

Between Shojinaga’s initial report and his arrest, several other cases were flagged to staff, the lawsuit adds.

One involved a child who was standing on a chair to reach supplies when Shojinaga allegedly “came immediately behind her with his telephone out”.

This caused her to believe he “might be photographing her” the lawsuit adds.

Court papers say students worked out a hand signal to warn each other when the teacher approached, and that they would go to the girls bathroom to avoid him.



The anonymous parties are seeking economic damages from Viewpoint including medical and psychological expenses.

According to the school’s Facebook page, Antoine retired after 35 years in 2025.

Shojinaga has been charged with one felony count of possession of child abuse material and four misdemeanor counts of child molestation.

He is currently free on £700million bail.

A protective order states he must stay away from his alleged victims and Viewpoint school.

His next court date is November 11.

News.title: Toddler, 2, euthanised in first case of its kind after Netherlands cut age limit to include children under 12
News.content:
TRAGIC CASE Toddler, 2, euthanised in first case of its kind after Netherlands cut age limit to include children under 12







Next

A TWO-YEAR-OLD child has been euthanised after the Dutch government cut its age limit for assisted dying.

The toddler was nearly 24 months old and suffering from severe medical conditions, a review board in the Netherlands revealed.

It was previously known that the life of a child under 12 had been ended under the policy.





But an investigation by the Committee for Late-Term Abortion and Termination of Life in Newborns and Children has now revealed that said child was a toddler.

It’s the first known case of a child under 12, who was not an infant, undergoing assisted death.

The board concluded that the doctor who euthanised the two-year-old had done so with due care.

Born prematurely at 26 weeks, the toddler suffered severe brain damage, cerebral palsy and visual impairment.

The gender of the toddler was not released.

They struggled to breathe because of mucus in their lungs and suffered from epileptic seizures which did not respond to medication.

The doctor sought a second opinion from independent doctors after determining their suffering could not be helped by medical care.

A report stated: “Those physicians established that at that time the child was not continuously suffering unbearably.”



“The epilepsy caused a great deal of discomfort, but the epileptic seizures were not continuous.

“Their conclusion was that there were still reasonable alternatives, such as palliative options and other medications that could possibly result in better control of the epileptic seizures.”

The doctor then got another second opinion from a physician who found that “the toddler’s ‘unbearable suffering was clearly visible”.

That doctor agreed that the requirements to end a child’s life through euthanasia had been met.

The Committee for Late-Term Abortion and Termination of Life in Newborns and Children agreed with the decision.



It stated: “All facets of ‘being human’ – regarding motor skills, behavior, and personality – were severely impaired and were not going to improve.

“Despite all medical and non-medical interventions, the parents and the doctor observed no improvement in the child’s condition and were convinced that the child was suffering unbearably and without prospect of relief.”

News.title: Baby girl dies trapped in car after parents ‘forgot to drop her at nursery and drove to work’ in Belgium
News.content:
BABY TRAGEDY Baby girl dies trapped in car after parents ‘forgot to drop her at nursery and drove to work’ in Belgium







Next

A BABY girl has died from being trapped in a car all day after her parents allegedly forgot to drop her at nursery and drove off to work.

The 18-month-old child was discovered unconscious in the Flemish Brabant region in Belgium, sparking an urgent emergency response.

The toddler’s older sister had been dropped off at at GBS ‘t Zonneveld primary school earlier on Friday – but then the parent drove off to work with the little girl still locked in the car.



It was only after the parent arrived at the primary school to pick up the elder daughter later that day that they made the horrifying discovery.



The little toddler had been trapped inside the car all day – and had fallen unconscious.

Emergency services raced to the scene and desperately tried to resuscitate the young girl.

She was rushed to UZ Gasthuisberg hospital – but tragically passed away after multiple attempts to save her life.



Prosecutors have launched a probe into the death with an autopsy to be carried out today.

“One of her parents was supposed to take her to daycare in the morning but forgot that the child was still in the car”, the prosecutor’s office confirmed to HLN.Be.

The tragedy is assumed to have been an accident, the office added.

Bertem mayor Joel Vander Elst said: “I can’t say much about the matter yet because it is all very sensitive and the public prosecutor is still investigating.”



The local council and school have arranged psychological support for pupils and teachers who knew the baby girl and her older sister.

“The municipal primary school ‘t Zonneveld will open as usual tomorrow with normal classes. We will, however, set up a quiet room for teachers and children who had contact with the sister of the young victim, who attends the school in the first grade”, confirmed the mayor.

In Belgium there is no requirement for nurseries to contact parents if the child fails to arrive.

It is not known whether the daycare centre tried to reach the parents on the day of the girl’s death.

It follows a horrifying spate of child car deaths across Europe and the US over the summer.



A toddler was found dead after locking himself inside a hot car as an intense heatwave continues to sweep across France.

The three-year-old boy reportedly slipped away from his parents’ supervision in Val-d’Oise, in the northern suburbs of Paris, before getting trapped in the car alone.

In August, a young girl was found dead after her family allegedly forgot about her and left her locked in a boiling hot car in Texas.

Cops said the girl and her sibling had been picked up from school by an adult family member – her sibling got out, but the five-year-old did not.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A second five-year-old passed away in September after being left in a sweltering car while his parents hosted a party.



Theo Sabo was found unresponsive outside his family‘s $1.1million (£800,000) home in Peoria, Arizona – with the dad shamelessly blaming his teenage son for the tragedy.

News.title: At least 3 migrants die and dozens injured while trying to reach UK as dinghy capsizes crossing the Channel
News.content:
SEA HORROR At least 3 migrants die and dozens injured while trying to reach UK as dinghy capsizes crossing the Channel







Next

AT LEAST three UK-bound migrants have died and dozens more are seriously injured after a mega-dinghy capsized in the English Channel.

Around 105 people were on board the boat when the horror accident happened off the coast at Wissant, near Calais.



A spokesman for the Pas-de-Calais confirmed “a provisional total of three deaths and many more injured.”

Officials described it as a “water taxi”, meaning it arrived relatively empty from an inland waterway, before picking up passengers from the beach.



“Sea conditions were calm – the weather is good,” said the Prefecture spokesman.

By 10.30am local time, six rescue boats were still surrounding the scene of the capsize, looking for survivors.



It follows three migrants dying as they scrambled for places on board a boat last week.

French prosecutors have opened criminal enquiries into all the tragedies, and judicial police are investigating.

The latest deaths mean that at least 24 people, including women and children, have died in the Channel this year as they tried to get to Britain.

Many have drowned, while others have been crushed to death in overcrowded boats.



The worst tragedy of this kind came in November 2021, when 27 migrants died after a dinghy sank while heading to the UK – the highest recorded number of deaths from a single incident.

The French navy has been partly blamed for the tragedy, after an independent inquiry found the accident was “avoidable”.

And it highlighted that a French patrol vessel close to the sinking dinghy failed to respond to a mayday message, which delayed the search.

Multiple attempts at crossings have taken place from the coast of northern France over the last few days, as smugglers take advantage of calm seas and good weather.

According to figures from the UK Home Office, 781 migrants arrived in Britain last Wednesday – the highest single-day total recorded so far this year.



A total of 18,565 migrants have reached England via the Channel since January, a figure down by more than 40 per cent compared to the same period in 2025.

The surge in crossings also indicates that people-trafficking gangs are still getting hold of dinghies and outboard motors with ease, despite a crackdown on supply routes.

Last week also saw two “uncontrolled landings” in which migrant boats reached the UK without being intercepted by the authorities.

In yet more chaotic scenes, a dinghy launched from near Bayeux, in Normandy, made a record 38-hour voyage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They launched just before 10am on Monday and, on Tuesday afternoon, were picked up by RNLI lifeboats and transferred to Border Force.



The 51 migrants on board were eventually brought ashore to Dover in the early hours of Wednesday.

News.title: Husband of Brit mum, 45, detained in Egypt fears for her life after six weeks without contact as he begs UK to intervene
News.content:
FAMILY'S AGONY Husband of Brit mum, 45, detained in Egypt fears for her life after six weeks without contact as he begs UK to intervene







Next

THE husband of a Brit mum-of-four who has been detained in Egypt is fearing for her life after six weeks of no contact.

Eman el-Shazly, 45, was arrested during a trip to Cairo last month – with her desperate partner Zesharn Moustapha now begging UK authorities for help.



She was reportedly taken from inside her mother’s home in the Egyptian capital in the early hours of August 17.

The property was left “smashed up” following the police raid, her family claimed.



For the last six weeks, she has been locked up in a maximum security prison and barred from speaking with her husband.

Zesharn said his wife’s arrest came just one day after cops “ram-raided” the property and told her sister to stop criticising the government online.



The next day, they allegedly returned to take away Eman and another one of her siblings named Shema.

Eman had been in Egypt to take care of her 68-year-old mother who is sick.



Zesharn said that the last thing he heard was his wife saying before the phone line suddenly cut off was: “They’re going to take me.”

Since that day, Eman’s family have had no contact with her at all, he added.

They claim she has been refused a lawyer to help battle the “bogus charges”.



Her loved ones also say they don’t know what condition she’s in and are extremely worried for her welfare.

Social media videos uploaded by her sister Mona criticising the Egyptian government are believed to be the motive for Eman’s arrest, Zesharn said.

His wife is now facing a “kangaroo court”, the husband added.

Her family launched a petition to “bring Eman home” last week and asked Andy Burnham and Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to step in and resolve Eman’s plight.

Zesharn and Eman’s four children include three sons, aged 18, 16, and nine, as well as a 14-year-old daughter.



Their youngsters have been forced to start this academic year without their mum while completely “traumatised”, the dad added.

He told The Independent: “They’ve been upset, distraught, crying.

“It was my son’s 10th birthday and he’s saying, ‘Mummy’s going to miss my birthday.’ It’s an emotional time for a young boy.”

The ordeal comes after Eman’s brothers were previously arrested on “identical” charges.

Zesharn said his wife’s male siblings were once held in pre-trial detention for three years.



The charges were later dropped but the group were re-arrested in May this year.

They were accused of “promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation on social media, as well as broadcasting false news harmful to state security”.

Due to this previous experience, Eman’s family fear she may face a similar fate.

Zesharn said: “She’s quite a strong-willed person but something like that would break anyone.

“I’d be on the floor crying – you’re in a different country and then thrown into jail on fake charges.”



He added: “We need the prime minister to get directly involved.

“Make that call to Egypt and get this problem resolved because at the end of the day what they’re doing is against all human rights.

“There’s no legal basis for any of them to be arrested, and it’s just an act of collective punishment.

“And now, there’s a British citizen, a mother-of-four, in a maximum security prison, who is completely innocent.”

He also said one of the detained brothers is ill but has been refused medical attention.



“If my wife gets sick there, she could lose her life there,” Zesharn said.

“Is the life of a British citizen not important to him [Burnham]?”

Her sister Mona told The Independent she refuses to stop speaking out against Egyptian authorities.

She said: “Because yielding to intimidation means allowing fear to dictate who is permitted to speak.

“I understand completely why anyone under this level of pressure would want the nightmare to end, and I am terrified for my family’s safety every single day.



“But stopping would establish a dangerous precedent: that an authoritarian regime can silence criticism anywhere in the world simply by taking family members hostage.

“I have zero tolerance for coercion. I have a duty to speak truthfully about corruption and abuse.

“My family must be released unconditionally because they are innocent individuals, not bargaining chips to control my voice.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The property was “smashed up” and the family say they were told to tell her activist sister Mona to stop publishing criticism, before officers returned to take el-Shazly and another sister, Shema, the following day.

News.title: Tigger Burnham replaces Eeyore Starmer with big pledges – but faces fury over plan to make ‘everyone’ pay more tax
News.content:
POLITICS FIX Tigger Burnham replaces Eeyore Starmer with big pledges – but faces fury over plan to make ‘everyone’ pay more tax







Next

ARE the winds of change really in the air at the Labour conference, or is that just the cold breeze blowing from across the Mersey?

Delegates in Liverpool are left in no doubt of Andy Burnham’s goal to “bring back hope” – you can’t move for the three-word slogan plastered on posters and booklets.



Whisper it, but the early signs are that the PM is so far succeeding to unite the Labour family behind his leadership.

Even a modest bounce in the polls has created an energy sorely lacking at last year’s get-together as Sir Keir Starmer plunged into freefall.



“We’re all feeling it,” one Cabinet Minister tells me. “With Keir we never really felt like a team, but now we’re all pulling together.”

If Starmer was more Eeyore, Burnham wants to be Tigger.

But the new PM constantly finds his boosterish instincts pushing against the inside of the straitjacket he inherited from his predecessor.

Burnham is restricted by Labour’s manifesto not to raise serious taxes nor increase borrowing to fund his plans.

Yesterday’s pledge to fix social care by making “everyone” contribute shows early signs he plans on breaking out of this fiscal prison at the next election.

The battlelines are already being drawn: a Labour government that expects voters to stump up more to fix existential issues, versus Tory/Reform parties that want deep spending cuts to make the sums add up.



Trying to win re-election on a promise of tax rises may go down well with the comrades on the floor of the Labour party conference.

But it will be a damn harder sell to those in Real Britain who feel they are already being rinsed.

News.title: Trump asked Xi if he’d ‘like to buy’ US weapons, ambassador reveals as Chinese tyrant persists with ‘panda diplomacy’
News.content:
Next

DONALD Trump asked Xi Jinping if he’d “like to buy” American weapons, the US envoy to Beijing said.

It comes after the Chinese president’s high-stakes state visit has resulted in Washington pausing a record-breaking £10.5billion arms sale to Taiwan.



Two giant pandas have meanwhile left China bound for Atlanta Zoo as Xi persists with China’s long-held “panda diplomacy”.

During their three-day summit, Xi and Trump discussed the US’ weapons sales to Taiwan and the self-governing island’s sovereignty.



US Ambassador to China David Perdue even claimed that Trump asked his counterpart if he was interested in purchasing American arms.

He said: “President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world.’

“He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”

It is unclear if Trump was being serious or simply joking with Xi, but the White House has since said it has no plans to sell weapons to China.

The US has also paused a roughly £10.5billion sale to Taipei, which could signal a shift in Washington’s geopolitical strategy.

The move, which he described as a “very good negotiating chip” in dealing with China, comes as Washington’s stockpiles are stretched by wars in Iran and Ukraine.



When asked about the pause, Perdue replied: “President Trump’s already approved $11 billion.

“There are continuing conversations about other sales. He and President Xi talk about that every time they get together.”

Perdue said of the White House’s position on Taiwan: “Our support for that has not changed.



“We don’t support independence and we don’t support coercion.”

Beijing has repeatedly laid claim to Taiwan under its “One China” principle, with aggression intensifying significantly in recent years.

Chinese forces have staged several ominous military drills simulating a full-scale invasion of the island and Xi has refused to rule out a landgrab.

During talks, Trump also pressed Xi on China’s support for Iran and received assurances that Beijing was changing its policy.

Perdue said: “President Xi assured him that changes had been made, that they were looking into it, they had looked into it.



“And we see some improvement in that. But it’s an ongoing effort that we have to make sure that they stay out of that.”

It comes as a pair of giant pandas, named Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, departed their native Chengdu on a direct flight to the US.

Ping Ping, whose name means peace, has been described by keepers as “brave and gentle”.



Fu Shuang, whose name means double blessings, loves to much down on bamboo and honey.

In return, Trump gifted Xi a bald eagle sculpture while revealing that the Chinese leader “loves good granite”.

The leaders heaped praise on each other at the lavish banquet – where Xi said Beijing-Washington relations were “forged in blood and fire”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

This strong connection between the US and China was born during the fight against Japan in World War Two, Xi said at the meal on Thursday.

He added “ping pong” diplomacy – the exchange of table tennis players in the 1970s to ease Cold War tensions – had further deepened their bond.

News.title: Farmer ‘saw more than 5 men run into fields’ before foiling ‘bomb plot’ as Streeting says she only has ‘partial picture’
News.content:
Next

A HERO farmer who foiled a suspected RAF base terror attack has claimed she saw more than five men at the scene.

The late-night sighting of balaclava-clad suspects metres from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire led to the arrest of five men and seizure of three vans full of explosives.



The sharp-eyed farmer was hailed a hero last night after she foiled a bomb attack on the RAF base.

But the woman also said that she believed she spotted more men around than the five who were caught and cuffed.



She claimed: “The worst thing is that we saw more than five people and they keep saying they arrested five.

“They had the helicopters searching.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has now said this morning that the member of the public who phoned police about suspicious activity near RAF Fairford has only “a partial picture” of the situation.

However, the Defence Sec said he is “grateful for the vigilance of the members of the public”, who are thought to have helped alert emergency services.

Mr Streeting told Sky News this morning: “Thank you to that member of the public.

“She has done exactly what we would hope that someone in that extraordinary situation would do.



“I’m really grateful to her – I think she acted, by her own admission, quickly and thoughtfully, and she did the right thing.

“With respect, though, she does only have a partial picture.

“And that’s as far as I wish to go this morning but I do want to emphasise my thanks to the police and the security services because their work takes place often unsung, unreported, for good reason.”



Temporary Chief Constable for Gloucestershire Police, Maggie Blyth, indicated the force is not looking for anybody else in connection with the incident.

Cops have also confirmed only five people were arrested.

The sharp-eyed farmer spotted men in balaclavas running close to the base as she drove home from a bash with her husband early yesterday.



The mum told how three vans were blocking the road outside the village of Whelford, Gloucs, adding: “We had to turn around and drive away.

“When we did that, we saw a group of men with masks and balaclavas running in front of us.”

The woman tried to call the base, used to launch US strikes on Iran, but could not get through so dialled 999.

The farmer who phoned in also left a message on her local WhatsApp group urging villagers to lock doors.

Officers arrived on the scene around 15 minutes after she dialled 999, she said.



A cordon was put in place near RAF Fairford, which is used by the US Air Force, and more than 80 evacuated households were unable to return home on Sunday night.

Asked whether the the incident “may have been driven by a hostile foreign state”, Mr Streeting also told Times Radio this morning that he did not “want to speculate at this stage of the investigation”.

The minister said: “What I can absolutely assure your listeners of is that, as and when we can, we will report back to the public about these individuals and about the nature of the threat.”



The plot came two months after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said the base — used to launch US bomber strikes on the terror regime — was a “legitimate target”.

If the attack proves to be state-sponsored it would be one of the biggest by a foreign nation on British soil since WW2.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham called the incident “deeply concerning” and promised the Government will “always take every step necessary” to protect people.

Armed cops swooped on the five suspects as they headed towards the base, seizing chemicals and incendiary devices from the vans, one of which had a fake sign.

The suspects, of Middle Eastern appearance, were pictured shirtless and handcuffed by the roadside.



A major incident was declared, 85 homes were evacuated and residents were taken to a leisure centre while experts made the bombs safe.

It was suspected bombs were going to be used to attack nearby RAF Fairford, which Iran named a “legitimate target” in July.

US President Donald Trump claimed an investigation into the plot was underway before the arrests.

Trump had alleged plotters were “looking to do big damage” to the airbase.

He also told reporters: “It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job.”



Mr Streeting said Mr Trump’s comments illustrated that UK security services were made up of “extraordinary people with extraordinary capability that are respected even by a superpower like the United States”.

Britain gave the US authority to use RAF Fairford for B-1 bombers to attack Iranian missile sites which have been targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Iran identified RAF Fairford as a legitimate target in its July statement, prompting a response from Britain that it “stands ready 24/7 to defend itself.”

Efforts have now been doubled into tracing Iran’s Revolutionary Guard cells feared to be operating in Britain since the July threat.

News.title: Labour conference: Defence secretary Wes Streeting to give major speech after RAF 'terror plot' foiled
News.content:
Lisa Nandy has spoken out about the "most horrendous hate and bile" directed at Ed Sheeran in recent weeks.

The Culture Secretary, speaking at a fringe event for The Mirror's Britain Talks project, praised the musician for his secret work bringing music to schools.

She said people must be able to disagree in a constructive way. Ms Nandy recalled getting a phone call from Sheeran, telling the event: "I'm going to start with something a bit controversial.

"I've spent the week answering questions about Ed Sheeran. He was somebody I got to know a couple of years ago when he rang up.

"And he said 'I've just read that you're the first entirely state-educated Cabinet in British history, and I'm so excited because I believe passionately that kids should have access to music in schools, can you help?'

"And we started on a piece of work. He has poured so much money into that, both in Ipswich and all over the country. He's never told anyone, he's never asked for praise, he's never asked for support.

"The first time I went to see what he was doing in Ipswich, he put on an impromptu gig for some of the kids from his old school. They didn't know it was him, they just knew it was a local act.

"I've never seen the magic on those children's faces, and some of the teachers told me later, it would change their lives."

She continued that she was shocked by the onslaught he has endured. Ms Nandy said: "He's someone who wears his politics lightly. He's not a politician, but he's somebody who believes that doing the right thing matters.

"He's got involved with a few causes over the years; he's got a friend who is very pro-Palestine, as am I, and he's used that platform for good to talk up to people about what is happening in Palestine.

"And when his promoters decided that they didn't want to continue with that concert, Ed Sheeran found himself in a position of the most horrendous hate and bile that I've seen.

"And you know, I'm a politician, I've been at this 17 years, I see a lot of it. I only have to look on X to see it, even while I'm talking here, a lot of it will be directed at me, and (fellow panelists) Tracy (Brabin) and Ros (Wynne Jones), and others.

"But honestly, I don't know how we came to a place where not only can we not disagree agreeably, but where you're not even allowed to wear your politics lightly."

News.title: Woman got best revenge on ex with heating, handles and his pants
News.content:
Woman got best revenge on ex with heating, handles and his pants

She admits it was petty but it helped her 'healing journey'

View 4 Images Kerry Adams

A woman has shared how she got her “petty revenge” on an ex with a number of “unhinged” acts after getting dumped. Kerry Adams says her world was shattered when her long-time partner decided to call it quits on their relationship.

‌



The pair tried to keep things amicable until the 49-year-old from Staffordshire could find a new place to stay. But this all came to an abrupt end when he reportedly started dating someone new.

‌



Kerry decided to take action with an extreme level of pettiness. “I left the heating on all day, every day and night, set at 28 degrees because I knew I wouldn’t be contributing to the next bill,” Kerry said. “It [the heat] was like being in Ibiza but worth it.

‌



View 4 Images Kerry wanted to make his life difficult in little ways

“Another time, he asked if I would stick [his dirty underwear] in with the next load of laundry for him. [Instead], I stuck his Calvin Klein and Armani boxers in the bin.”

‌



During her final month living with her ex, Kerry acted out her last piece of revenge, which has been deemed the pettiest of the lot. The pair had agreed that she could take anything with her that she had paid for, so she did just that – by removing all of the kitchen cupboard handles.

Kerry said: “He asked to buy back the cupboard handles but I said ‘you told me to take anything I paid for and I paid for them’. “It was mostly done on the spur of the moment because I was upset. Looking back now, I find the situation funny – but I certainly didn’t at the time.”

Kerry’s relationship ended earlier this year and months later, she decided to open up on Instagram about her actions , with many people sharing confessions of their own.

‌



View 4 Images Kerry stuck to the rules - only taking what she had paid for

“When my friend and I were packing my things after my breakup, she took the pot of sugar so he couldn’t have a nice cup of tea in the morning,” said Rachel. Another person confessed: “I monitored his MOT status until it ran out then coincidentally he was stopped by traffic police and also had two baldy tyres.”

‌



“This is the laugh I needed today,” said Natalie. “Yesss Kerry, being unhinged is part of the healing process,” added someone else. “This gave me a good laugh, you GO GAL xx,” said another person.

“Still makes me chuckle about the handles,” added someone else. Despite the devastating break-up, Kelly claims it actually turned out to be the best thing that happened to her.

View 4 Images Kerry's story inspired others to share

Article continues below

Kelly said: “Now, I would thank him because I genuinely believe that my life is better without him in it. I enjoyed my best summer in a long time. I have started to see friends again and meet new people.

“It just makes me laugh when I think about it and I have received so much support on Instagram since I started sharing my life on there. So yes, petty – but therapeutic too.”

News.title: Funeral director blasts plan to build one of UK's biggest 'corpse factory' that could hold 700 dead bodies
News.content:
Funeral director blasts plan to build one of UK's biggest 'corpse factory' that could hold 700 dead bodies

A plan to bring bodies from across the North East to a York business park has prompted objections from residents and a local funeral director, in what would be one of the UK's biggest mortuary

View 3 Images If plans go ahead the former telephone exchange would turn into a Mortuary that could hold up to 700 bodies (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

A funeral director fears a proposed mortuary capable of holding up to 700 bodies could become a “corpse factory”.

‌



Pure Cremation has submitted plans to convert a former telephone exchange at York Business Park, in Nether Poppleton, North Yorkshire, into a mortuary with capacity for up to 700 bodies. The company says it would become its main facility for the North East, but the proposal has drawn dozens of objections.

‌



Among those opposing it is Martin Rowley, 64, who runs Rowley & Sons Family Funeral Services in York. He questioned whether staff could provide adequate care on such a large scale.

‌



Martin, who is also a Conservative councillor for the Osbaldwick and Derwent Ward, said: “When we take deceased loved ones into our care, most of the bodies will be fine. But others will break down or start to decompose quickly, and require specialist care.

“How can so few staff realistically look after so many bodies and ensure they are kept in good condition.”

View 3 Images Plans for the building include racks stacked five coffins high (Image: City of York Council / SWNS)

‌



Body of missing cat found in woods after severed tail posted through letterbox READ MORE :

Plans for the 37,673 sq ft building show racks stacked five coffins high, along with external cooling units, a specialist procedure area and an operational base. The unit sits near a martial arts gym, nail salons and dog groomers.

Martin said: “Would you want your loved one to be kept in a mortuary among the remains of 700 people? Serious questions have to be raised about this practice.”

Pure Cremation provides direct cremations, where a person is cremated without family present or a formal funeral service. Martin said his objection was to the scale of the proposed mortuary.

‌



He said: “I’m not questioning their service, rather the industrial scale of the facility. The service a funeral director offers with a direct cremation isn’t quick or simple like Pure Cremation makes it out to be.”

He added: “There is a time and a place for unattended direct cremations - but the increased industrial scale they are suggesting with this new site is just very disturbing. All I see this site as is an inhumane conveyor belt or factory - loved ones deserve respect.”

View 3 Images York funeral director, Martin Rowley (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

‌



Residents have also objected to the application, with some describing the proposal as “horrific”. Liberal Democrat councillor Anne Hook raised concerns about its effect on nearby businesses and hotels.

In an objection letter, she said: “People will not want to work or stay so close to such a large mortuary, and I expect there will be a reluctance for businesses to move into the estate when units become empty.”

Other objectors raised concerns about traffic. Under the plans, the facility would operate around the clock, storing bodies collected from homes, care homes and hospices before they were sent elsewhere for cremation. Bodies could be kept there for up to four days. The site would be closed to the public and monitored by CCTV.

Article continues below

Pure Cremation said the operation would be dignified and discreet and to a similar facility it runs on a business park in Knutsford, Cheshire, which it said had generated no complaints.

The company’s plans stated: “Pure Cremation occupy a similar premises on a business park in Knutsford, Cheshire, no complaints or adverse impact are reported from that site. The whole operation is dignified, quiet and discreet.”

O’Neill Associates, acting on behalf of Pure Cremation, said the proposal would have a negligible effect on traffic and noise. York Council has yet to decide the application

News.title: New Lidl £10 jacket 'perfect for autumn' similar to £70 high-end offer out Sunday
News.content:
New Lidl £10 jacket 'perfect for autumn' similar to £70 high-end offer out Sunday

The new autumn jacket will be landing in stores later this week and shares similar features to a high-end version

View 3 Images The new jacket is coming out later this week (Image: Getty)

Lidl is updating its Middle Aisle with new products this week, including autumn fashion pieces. The supermarket brings out new items every Thursday and Sunday, and on this Sunday, shoppers will be able to get their hands on several new clothing items.

‌



Lidl's Esmara Ladies' Navy Lightweight Padded Jacket is coming to stores this weekend, just in time for the autumn weather. It is ultra-lightweight yet has a padded design, which Lidl says can help to keep you warm on chilly mornings and crisp evening walks.

‌



The outer fabric is wind-resistant and treated with a special water-repellent coating, so unexpected autumn rain showers will slide right off rather than soak through. It is designed to be highly practical, featuring a hood, side pockets, and a durable zip to block out cold drafts.

‌



In the product description, Lidl says: "Ultra-lightweight, warm and wind-resistant. Water-repellent main material thanks to Bionic-finish eco technology. High quality YKK zip. With hood, side pockets and zip with inner storm flap. Slightly fitted. Sizes: S-L."

The jacket will be available in UK stores on Sunday, October 4. It will be on sale for £9.99 for Lidl Plus shoppers and £12.99 for regular shoppers.

View 3 Images Lidl's Esmara Ladies' Navy Lightweight Padded Jacket (Image: Lidl)

‌



The lightweight outerwear piece shares similar features to the £69 Esprit Outdoor Woven Jacket, which is available through retailers like Barbours of Dumfries. The website barbours.co.uk is an online storefront for Barbours, an independent fashion retailer located in Dumfries, Scotland.

It is important to note that this is not the official website for the famous heritage outerwear brand, Barbour. While this specific retailer shares the name and carries the lifestyle label alongside other popular fashion brands (such as Esprit, French Connection, and Joules), it is entirely distinct.

Even though these two jackets are priced very differently, they share similarities in how they look and what they're supposed to do. Both jackets are designed to handle changing weather and everyday wear. They also have a quilted look, side pockets, and hoods that help protect you from light rain or wind.

‌



The primary differences between the two products lie in their manufacturing materials and overall cost. The budget-friendly Esmara Padded Jacket from the supermarket chain places heavy emphasis on weather resistance. It uses a specialised water-repellent coating known as Bionic-finish eco, which Lidl says helps prevent light rain from soaking through the fabric.

View 3 Images The Esprit Outdoor Woven Jacket is available at Barbours for £69 (Image: Barbours)

In contrast, the Esprit jacket sold via Barbours highlights modern sustainability practices. The jacket is made entirely from 100% recycled materials.

Article continues below

The product description of the Espirit jacket on Barbours' website reads: "Combines great style with top performance: quilted jacket made completely of recycled material with a detachable hood and side hem zips." Sizes include S-XL.

Ultimately, it comes down to what shoppers prefer: pricing or brand. Lidl continues its strategy of offering weekly "Middle of Lidl" special buys at low price points, making functional outerwear accessible to a broad range of people. Meanwhile, the high-end jacket offer represents a premium tier.

News.title: I found the ultimate Lego trip for families - and it's not in Legoland
News.content:
I found the ultimate Lego trip for families - and it's not in Legoland

Lego fans can explore the original Legoland and Lego House less than two hours from the UK - here's my review of the underrated family holiday

View 6 Images (Image: Lego)

As you wander around the picture-perfect Danish town of Billund, you could almost kid yourself you’ve stepped into the real-life version of the Lego City range - it feels as if someone planned the entire town, piece by piece. And in a way, they did.

Dedicated Lego fans may have heard of Billund as the home of Lego - the toy was created here in 1958. To this day the vast majority of Lego sets, themes, and bricks are designed at the headquarters here, with Lego employing the majority of local residents, and contributing hugely to the town's development. Visitors come in their tens of thousands to enjoy the original Legoland - but we found the true star of Billund to be the unique Lego House, which rightly bills itself as the ‘ultimate interactive Lego experience’.

My seven year old and I took advantage of a mild, if a little rainy, early September weekend for a three-night stay in the Legoland Holiday Village's Pirate Motel, booking a cheerful pirate-themed room complete with treasure chest, and combining a day at Lego House with a two-day Legoland pass.

While my Lego fanatic son and I have a soft spot for Legoland Windsor, we found the spotlessly clean Danish Legoland way less crowded. Indeed throughout our Friday/ Saturday visit even the most popular rides never more than a 15 minutes wait - and at times we were able to stay on for a second go.

View 6 Images In the Masterpiece Gallery at the top of the house, visitors can see incredible creations by Lego fans from around the world, inspiring them to then create their own (Image: Lego)

Yet despite the tried and tested joys of a day at Legoland it was Lego House that was the absolute highlight of our visit. If at Legoland your child enjoys free play in the Lego pits as much as the thrill of the rides, then Lego House is for them.

Designed like a giant stack of 21 overlapping blocks, scaled up precisely from standard Lego bricks, the sprawling building feels like a living playground. The website describes four ‘interactive experience zones’, but this undersells what is on offer. There are endless activities which are carefully designed to be just as enjoyable for adult fans of Lego (afol as they call them here), as they are for children.

In just one section of an experience zone, we built our own Minifigures, photographed them for magazine covers, then used them to create stop-motion films in dedicated recording booths. These were then sent to us to view later via our wristbands.

View 6 Images We stayed at the stayed at Pirate's Inn Motel LegoLand Holiday Village, from £180 per night for two (Image: Lego)

Elsewhere, our highlights included racing our custom-built cars down speed tracks, creating Lego fish that were then scanned and joined a huge aquarium, and exploring a huge Lego world far more detailed than any Miniland we’ve seen, featuring everything from miner-filled mountains and underground train sets to volcanoes, fairgrounds, and cities.

There are innovative building challenges throughout, sitting alongside breathtaking installations like a cascading multi-coloured Lego waterfall and the jaw-dropping, 15-metre-tall Tree of Creativity built from over 6.3 million bricks which grows right up through the centre of the building.

My son loved watching Lego bricks being created from start to finish in the mini-factory on the ground floor before picking up our own complimentary bag of six freshly molded bricks to take home. Scanning your wristband creates a personalised card showing a unique combination to build.

Down in the basement vault, a history museum displays early prototypes and sets from across the years - I really enjoyed finding the ones my brother and I used to own in the 80s and 90s, and showing them to my son.

View 6 Images The 15-metre-tall Tree of Creativity built from over 6.3 million bricks (Image: Lego)

Up on the primary-coloured terraced roofs, which cascade down like giant red green and yellow steps, my son took a breather from crafting his creations. As I soaked up the panoramic views over Billund's forests he played in a huge submarine, climbed a skyscraper and enjoyed an impromptu game of hide and seek with children speaking four different languages.

One of the best bits was trying out the Lego Masters Academy, which costs an extra fee on top of the Lego House entrance. We also loved visiting the Mini Chef restaurant, where we built our orders using physical Lego bricks and had our meals delivered by robots in giant Lego containers.

All in all, we thought Lego House was absolutely unmissable.

Everything you should know before you visit Lego House Billund

Standard Lego House general admission starts around around £28 per person with some discounts for booking online. It is often fully booked and is not open every day, especially out of season, so check availability before booking a trip.

The Lego Masters activity is an extra fee on top of Lego House, costing from £14 to £17 per person depending on the option booked. You can do this activity without entering the experience zones inside the Lego House, or on the same day you do these. Make sure you heck opening days, book ahead as slots fill up fast, and choose English language (if applicable).

6 View 6 Images One highlight was the Lego Masters Academy - which those hoping to visit need to book ahead for (Image: Lizzie Smith/ Reach PLC) 6 View 6 Images Working against the clock, we raided brick bins then created our own Lego people - just like the popular TV series (Image: Lizzie Smith/ Reach PLC)

Likewise Mini Chef reservations fill up well in advance and are rarely available on the day - it's worth planning ahead. Meals when we visited cost £15 for a child meal which included a Minifigure surprise, and £27 for adults.

The Lego Shop on the ground floor opens an hour before the Lego House and stays open an hour later. We arrived early and did our shopping first thing, which was an unhurried pleasant experience compared to the packed store at the end of the day. You can leave purchases in a free secure locker on the ground floor, using your Lego House wristband.

Along with unique Lego House Lego sets, in the shop you can buy personalised custom printed Minifigures for £11.50, which make brilliant gifts.

If you are staying at LegoLand Holiday Village, as we were, or the neighbouring Lalandia, the walk to Lego House is a pleasant 20 minute stroll through Billund Sculpture Park.

News.title: Inside Met Police's hi-tech face scanning camera operation as force plans rollout across London
News.content:
Inside Met Police's hi-tech face scanning camera operation as force plans rollout across London

EXCLUSIVE: The Mirror witnessed police arresting people in the street as hi-tech live facial recognition cameras were set up in Oxford Circus ahead of a wider rollout across the capital

Inside the Met Police’s Face-Scanning Van on Oxford street

Met Police chiefs want to roll out face-scanning cameras across the capital - and the sci-fi crime-fighting tech is already appearing on some of Britain's most iconic streets.

‌



The Mirror joined the force on a Live Facial Recognition (LFR) camera deployment in Oxford Circus this week, where officers stood ready to swoop on anyone whose face showed up as a match on their watchlist.

‌



In less than three hours, we witnessed four people being put in handcuffs and led away from the scene.

‌



While legal restrictions prevent us from identifying the people arrested, they were linked with what police described as a "range of offences", including theft and breach of conditions.

View 7 Images Multiple people were arrested as the Met deployed face-scanning cameras in Oxford Circus (Image: Daily Mirror)

Inside police fightback against 'A66-linked' organised crime gangs that paralysed Middlesbrough READ MORE :

Shoppers to be able to pay by just using their face for the first time READ MORE :

They had all made the same mistake of wandering through the busy shopping district on a day when police had parked up their mobile camera vans.

‌



This LFR technology works by converting the facial features of passersby into biometric codes, and comparing these in real-time against a database containing the photos of tens of thousands of wanted people. The watchlist is updated every morning, and the data of anyone who doesn't trigger a match is deleted immediately.

View 7 Images Police want to roll out the technology across the capital (Image: Daily Mirror)

On this deployment, an operator remained inside the van monitoring the live camera feed, while around eight officers were stationed on the street outside.

‌



When a match is identified by the software, a ‘ping’ is sent to all the officers' handsets, showing a photo on the watchlist, the snap just taken, and a biometric similarity rating out of 10. The officer in charge of the operation then makes the call as to whether to stop the suspect.

View 7 Images Mirror reporter Benedict Tetzlaff Deas tested out the technology

To test how effective this tech was, I asked police to temporarily put my own face on the list, seeing if it would trigger a positive ID.

‌



Sure enough, as I wandered out of Oxford Circus station on this test run, a chorus of alerts sounded from the pockets of the officers around me - though thankfully that was the full extent of my brush with the law.

View 7 Images The camera van detected a match almost instantly (Image: Daily Mirror)

On a second attempt, I covered my face with a hooded coat and popped on a pair of sunglasses to try and hide my features, but was flagged immediately.

‌



Inside the van, I was shown how the software identified me in a split second. It picked out my face from the crowd by measuring the distances between key features like my eyes, nose, and mouth.

The commanding sergeant was in the middle of explaining how police officers decide whether to make a stop when a potential positive ID was identified across the road, springing the team into action.

Officers at the scene lauded the success of these cameras, hailing a six-month trial in the centre of Croydon, south London that saw crime drop by 10.5%, and violence against women and girls fall by over 20%.

‌



In the past year, LFR technology has led to over 1,600 arrests in London for serious offences, including kidnap, rape and assault.

View 7 Images Sunglasses and a hood won't fool the cameras (Image: Daily Mirror)

The Met now wants to put permanent LFR technology in busy spots across the capital, such as the West End and Soho.

‌



It's hoped having static cameras would avoid the kind of resourcing issues which saw this van depart Oxford Circus early after multiple arrests, due to officers having to leave the scene to take the suspects into custody.

The Home Office has meanwhile pledged £11.6million into static and mobile LFR technology across England and Wales.

But not everyone is quite so enthusiastic when it comes to the expansion of this tech.

‌



While the vast majority of people passing through this part of central London appeared unfazed, or simply didn’t notice the cameras, we heard a handful of tuts and murmurs from people who seemed uneasy at being scanned.

View 7 Images The cameras divide opinion - but police have hailed falls in crime figures in areas where they have been trialled (Image: Daily Mirror)

Patrick Brink, 57, who was visiting from Sweden, approached the van to say it reminded him of his recent trip to China, where face-scanning technology is routinely used by authorities, and is even used to issue on-the-spot fines.

‌



He told us: "I'm kind of used to the surveillance of the people. But I have a 50/50 feeling about those cameras because they are good for people in general when it comes to safety - we can feel safer and like that.

"But then again, I'm against a society where people are identified everywhere and monitored in what they are doing online, and now in reality too. We have to remember that the future is ahead and the technology will be developing."

Campaigners have also highlighted international studies that suggest that LFR software may be prone to misidentifying people from ethnic minority backgrounds.

‌



Police told us at the deployment that the algorithm they use has been independently tested by experts at the National Physical Laboratory, and that their study showed "no statistical racial or gender bias within the system".

View 7 Images Police say LFR technology has led to over 1,600 arrests for serious offences in the past year (Image: Daily Mirror)

Sergeant Kevin Brown said: "In the last 12 months of the data, we're looking at over 1 in every 350,000 people. We've never arrested anyone or taken anyone into custody as a result of a false alert.

Article continues below

"We're not harvesting data. That's really, really important. As an organisation, we do understand that people have got some concerns around this.

"When you look at the number of arrests, we're looking at over 3,000 arrests since the start of 2024. You're looking at the efficiencies that this is delivering in putting people in front of the courts. It's not going to replace policing, and general policing tactics - but it's an additional tool."

News.title: Woman found lump thanks to Dalmatian and was told she had six months
News.content:
Woman found lump thanks to Dalmatian and was told she had six months

Georgie Copema spent some of her last few weeks organising a huge charity fundraising event

View 9 Images Adel Murphy-Copeman and Georgie Copeman

A 50-year-old woman only found a lump because she had to sit awkwardly on the sofa when her Dalmatian took up the rest of the seat - and died six months after being told aggressive cancer had spread through her body.

‌



Georgie Copema died on September 17, aged 50, after being told she only had months to live. In her last few weeks, the former NHS worker was the driving force behind a record-breaking Sarcoma UK fundraising walk which attracted 500 people.

‌



Her wife, Adel Murphy-Copeman, 45, says continuing that work will now form part of Georgie’s legacy. “Georgie was just incredible,” she said. “She embraced life with courage, dignity, grace and humour. She had the most wonderful sense of humour and warm, joyful essence about her. She always appreciated the smallest of things.

‌



View 9 Images Georgie Copeman was a competitive bodybuilder

“She was the most selfless person I’ve ever known. She always wanted to help anyone she could. Her kindness, love, laughter and infectious loud laugh would brighten up any room. Everyone used to always say you would hear her laugh before you saw her, and this was so true.”

The couple had been together for six-and-a-half years and married on August 5 this year. Their wedding came after a difficult 18 months, which had begun when Georgie noticed something unusual. She had been fit and active and had previously competed in bodybuilding after losing around nine stone.

‌



Although she had experienced heavier periods, fatigue and bloating, the couple thought the symptoms could be linked to perimenopause. It was only when the couple’s Dalmatian, Benson, took up most of the sofa one day in April 2025 that Georgie squeezed into an unusual sitting position beside him and spotted a lump protruding from her stomach.

Adel could feel what appeared to be a tennis ball-sized mass. It was only noticeable when Georgie was sitting in that particular position and disappeared from view when she stood up.

View 9 Images Georgie Copeman at her and Adel's wedding in August 2026 Georgie (Conor for Helaina Storey helainastorey.com/Cover Images)

‌



After being told she wouldn’t be able to get a GP appointment for four weeks, Georgie contacted NHS 111 and was seen at Maidstone Hospital the same day. Doctors suspected a uterine fibroid, and she was referred back to the GP for further investigation.

The couple later noticed through the NHS App that Georgie had been placed on a suspected cancer pathway. She underwent investigations including a hysteroscopy, ultrasound and MRI before attending an appointment where a Macmillan nurse was also present.

It was there that the couple received the news they had feared. Georgie had uterine leiomyosarcoma, a rare cancer which develops in the smooth muscle of the uterus.

‌



She underwent major surgery, including a full hysterectomy, in June 2025, with surgeons operating from her sternum to her pelvis to remove the tumour. Adel says the mass removed was around the size of an eight-month-old baby.

After surgery, Georgie was later transferred into the care of specialists at the Royal Marsden, a world-leading specialist cancer treatment and research hospital in Chelsea. She was placed under surveillance with scans every three months.

View 9 Images Georgie Copeman and Adel at their wedding (Conor for Helaina Storey helainastorey.com/Cover Images)

‌



A follow-up scan showed a 2cm nodule in her pelvis, which the couple were told could either be post-operative scar tissue or, if it were to grow, it would grow very quickly. They were told to come back in another three months for another scan.

Further scans initially brought reassuring results, but Georgie repeatedly raised concerns about flu-like symptoms, sweats and feeling fatigued. Around Christmas 2025, Georgie began noticing that her stomach was changing again.

The couple, from Upper Fant in Kent, started taking photographs to document the difference and became increasingly concerned by how quickly it appeared to be growing. By the end of February, Adel says Georgie could barely walk from their bedroom to the en-suite bathroom; it was debilitating for her.

‌



After seeking medical help on several occasions, Georgie’s next scan was brought forward. In March, they received devastating news.

The cancer had returned aggressively and had spread to three new areas, including her pelvis, her aorta and the peritoneum - the smooth, continuous membrane that lines the inside of your abdominal and pelvic cavity and wraps around your internal organs.

View 9 Images Adel Murphy-Copeman and Georgie Copeman

‌



Georgie was told she could have between 12 and 18 months to live and needed to start palliative chemotherapy as soon as possible to give her more time. But her health deteriorated rapidly.

Over the months that followed, Adel says her wife spent 52 days in and out of Maidstone A&E, hospital wards and the Royal Marsden as she battled infections and complications alongside her cancer treatment. Doctors initially tried two chemotherapy drugs before reducing her treatment to one. By the end of May, after only one and a half rounds, Georgie was told the chemotherapy was not working and that it was just making her sicker.

Her response was simple. “I want to live as well as I can for as long as I can,” she said.

‌



Georgie returned home at the beginning of June, by which point she was almost completely bedbound and required a permanent drain for her ascites (the abnormal buildup of excess fluid) in her stomach. District nurses taught Adel how to deal with the drain as she looked after her wife full-time and also kept their business running.

View 9 Images Adel Murphy-Copeman on the phone with Georgie at the Rare But Real walk at Mote Park

The couple, who ran Health Hut Nutrition in Maidstone, had initially kept Georgie’s diagnosis private. They had met after Georgie’s NHS boss suggested the pair should connect following a documentary Adel had filmed, before properly getting to know each other through Adel’s fitness classes.

‌



Georgie, who had worked in communications for Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust, eventually left the NHS in 2024 to work full-time alongside Adel at Health Hut Nutrition. It was not until March this year that the couple began telling others Georgie was ill.

And when they were told there was nothing more doctors could do, their focus increasingly turned towards helping other people understand sarcoma. “Georgie just wanted to help people,” Adel said. “She never once complained, was angry or was ‘woe is me’. It was never in our control, so it became: how can we help others? We really wanted to raise awareness, not about Georgie, but about the illness.”

That determination was funnelled into Sarcoma UK’s Rare But Real Walk at Mote Park earlier this month. Adel initially hoped they might persuade 100 people to attend, which they were told was the largest number or participants the charity had managed to get for its walks.

‌



View 9 Images The Rare But Real walk at Mote Park

Then she set herself a much more ambitious target: 500. Almost 500 people ultimately turned out, making it the largest Rare But Real event Sarcoma UK has held. The couple raised more than £21,500 for the charity.

Georgie was too unwell to attend in person, but joined those taking part via WhatsApp from her bed at the Heart of Kent Hospice. Even from the hospice the day before the walk, she recorded a message encouraging people to support Sarcoma UK and its work.

‌



You learn more about the fundraiser and donate here. https://www.justgiving.com/team/georgiessarcomawarriors?utm_medium=TE&utm_source=CL

For Adel, the hundreds of people who turned up represented something beyond the money raised. “Five hundred families now know what sarcoma is,” she said. “This is just the start of my promise to Georgie. I will continue what she started. Maidstone came together for us.”

Georgie spent 22 days at the Heart of Kent Hospice before her death. Having lost her own mother to cervical cancer when she was just 13, she had been clear about what she wanted at the end of her life.

‌



View 9 Images The Rare But Real walk at Mote Park

Adel stayed alongside her at the hospice every night and was with her when she died on September 17. “It was a very special moment that we had,” she said.

The couple had always been open with one another about what was coming, even planning Georgie’s funeral together. “A lot of people shy away from it, but it was important to us to do that,” Adel said.

‌



Georgie’s funeral will be held privately for her family and close friends in October, with donations to Sarcoma UK welcomed in her memory. She leaves behind Adel, her sister Julie, nieces Georgie and Caffy, and her dearest friend Lyn.

Mark Bhagwandin, communications manager at Sarcoma UK, said Georgie had left a lasting impression on those she met. “Georgie was one of those rare people who, in a short space of time, leaves a mark that lasts far longer than the time you actually spent with them.

“Even while facing the most devastating news anyone could receive, she chose to spend her remaining time helping others, raising money, raising awareness and rallying an entire community behind Sarcoma UK.”

‌



View 9 Images Adel Murphy-Copeman and Georgie Copeman

Adel says cancer took an enormous amount from the couple, but there were things it could never touch.

“Cancer had taken so much from us, but it hadn’t taken our ability to love, to laugh, or to appreciate the smallest moments,” she said. “We embraced this journey together. Georgie never complained, she never got angry. She had the most incredible attitude and mindset towards it.

Article continues below

“Her strength to just keep going, to keep fighting over the last six months inspired me every single day. This journey taught us that life isn’t measured by how many days we had. It’s measured by what we did in the days we were given.”

Georgie’s message towards the end of her life, Adel says, was equally clear: “Having a mission and helping people to understand that you can keep fighting, you can keep doing good things no matter what.”

Now Adel intends to make sure that mission continues. “They say some people leave footprints on this earth, but Georgie has done something more,” she said. “She has left a handprint on our hearts, and this will remain long after her footprints have gone.”

News.title: New prescription warning for blood pressure, statins, iron medications
News.content:
New prescription warning for blood pressure, statins, iron medications

Massive research study found ‘prescribing cascades’ caused by medications not new medical conditions

View Image Medications can set off ‘prescribing cascades’ where more drugs are used to combat side effects (Image: Getty)

A new study has found that prescribing medications such as blood pressure drugs, statins, an Alzheimer’s drug, and iron supplements leads to ‘prescribing cascades’ to combat adverse reactions. The research, published in BMJ involved a massive 2,297,942 people to investigate the impacts of prescriptions.

‌



A prescribing cascade occurs when a drug is prescribed to a patient, an unrecognised adverse reaction develops, and a second drug is prescribed to manage that reaction under the mistaken impression that a new medical condition has appeared.

‌



The research, published in BMJ and led by Dr Paula Rochon, director of research at the Weston and O’Born Centre for Mature Women’s Health at Sinai Health in Toronto, has revealed that certain drug combinations are a common but little-known contributor to drug harm at the population level and add unnecessary costs to the healthcare system.

‌



Doctors cure cancer by hacking cells, genetic mutation linked to lung disease, dementia warning in muscles, and stomach fungus protects you from radiation - all this and more in our science newsletter

A potentially inappropriate prescribing cascade (PIPC) happens when a medication’s side effect gets mistaken for a new health problem, leading to another prescription that may not have been needed in the first place. One common example flagged in the study involves non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

Commonly prescribed for pain, these drugs are associated with a rise in blood pressure, which can lead to a new prescription for high blood pressure, rather than a second look at the original pain medication. Older adults are especially vulnerable to this pattern because they’re more likely to be on multiple medications at once, due to having multiple conditions, making it harder for both patients and clinicians to trace a new symptom back to an existing drug.

‌



Dr Rochon said: “These sequences of events are common but often missed in clinical practice. Knowing what medications, you are taking, when they were started and for what indication is important in order to identify possible prescribing cascades that may be problematic “

NHS TV doctor sodium and potassium warning over supplements READ MORE :

New study warning over deficiencies after taking Wegovy, Liraglutide READ MORE :

The researchers examined each PIPC against three factors: how common the initial drug was in the population, how often it was followed by the second drug, and how strong the link was between the two. That analysis allowed them to pinpoint the 24 potentially inappropriate prescribing cascades most commonly seen in the population and with a potential to cause harm.

Dr Rochon explained “Our concern is that so often these conversations between the health care prescriber and the patient are being missed, so people don’t recognize the sequences of events and that they are connected to one another.”

‌



The work also carries a particular weight for mature women, as they tend to live with more chronic conditions than men over their lifetime. Mature women are prescribed more drug therapies, and experience more adverse drug events. By being on multiple medications at once, they are more exposed to the risk that a drug’s side effect gets mistaken for a new diagnosis rather than traced back to its source.

Potential next steps for health professionals:

The first involves technology. Automated clinical decision support tools could flag a prescribing cascade in real time and prompt a second look before a new prescription is added. This information could be leveraged in one of several automated ways to help clinicians be aware of these potentially inappropriate prescribing cascades at the point of care.

Next is optimising the role of pharmacists as part of the care team and more directly integrating them into the prescribing process alongside physicians. Their expertise can help identify these potentially inappropriate prescribing cascades for further evaluation.
