It took Taylor’s side until 25 January to accumulate seven points last season but they look significantly improved and have built on the progress they made during the second half of 2025-26.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors had spurned a couple of decent chances on the counterattack before the break, including Hannah Cain scuffing over from a promising position. Overall, however, Everton, whose only two league goals this season have been own goals, will be concerned about their comparative lack of creativity.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Spurs go second, Man Utd earn first win Show Victoria Pelova scored twice as Tottenham moved up to second in the WSL table with a 4-0 win over Aston Villa, while Manchester United earned their first win of the season, edging West Ham 2-1. Dutch midfielder Pelova [pictured] broke the deadlock in the 54th minute at Brisbane Road, and then fired in a second off the underside of the crossbar, taking her tally to four goals in two WSL games. Spurs sealed victory as Caitlin Dijkstra headed in, and Cathinka Tandberg added a fourth with two minutes left. Manchester United secured their first WSL victory under new manager Eva Olid, defeating West Ham in Leigh. Elisabeth Terland’s header set United on their way after nine minutes, with summer signing Andrea Medina doubling the lead late in the second half. Viviane Asseyi scored a late penalty for the visitors. Océane Hurtré fired Birmingham City ahead after 40 seconds against Crystal Palace, scoring the quickest goal of the season so far. Shanade Hopcroft’s long-range free-kick had Palace level on the half-hour, before Hurtré restored Birmingham’s lead with an angled strike. Palace fought back to lead at St Andrew's, their goals coming from Bethany England and Lexi Lloyd-Smith, but Suzu Amano struck with three minutes left to secure Birmingham a point in a thrilling 3-3 draw. Press Assocation Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Asked about that wait for one of his own players to score a league goal, the Everton head coach, Scott Phelan, spoke calmly, saying: “We know we need to be more decisive in those actions, 100%. We have won two games as well and three on the bounce, so we don’t forget that. [But] yes, we want to start contributing more in the final third and that’ll be a challenge for all of us.

“We’ve played four games, so it’s definitely not panic stations. We’ve got good players in those areas of the pitch, we’re convinced they will contribute more – we’ve just got to wait for that moment to appear and hopefully it’s sooner rather than later.”

Phelan’s team still sit comfortably in the middle of the table with two wins from four games. Perhaps the most disappointing aspect for Everton fans will be that they can no longer rely on their annual collection of three points from Anfield.

Sports.title: Denmark dominate Wales in Nations League to leave Bellamy ‘really hurting’
Sports.content:
Wales wilted in Copenhagen as a 2-0 defeat to Denmark left them bottom of their Nations League group with no points or goals from their first two games.

After a first half in which Wales were very much second-best and fortunate to reach the break level, Denmark’s domination was rewarded by a Ben Davies own goal and a Gustav Isaksen strike in the second period.

Wales lost Thursday’s opener to Portugal 1-0 and Sunday’s result leaves them already facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation from Group A4. Denmark were under similar pressure after being beaten 3-2 by Norway on Thursday, but rose to the occasion and should have won more comfortably.

“I’m really hurting. When you see an athletic team run over you a little bit … but then, will we improve? I think we will,” said the Wales manager, Craig Bellamy. “This team will get better, these players will keep improving. For me now it’s just focus, two more games to go.”

Bellamy had happy memories of the Parken Stadium when as a 19-year-old he had scored the Wales winner in a Euro 2000 qualifier. Bellamy had promised to make changes given the short turnaround of fixtures and, in the event, made six with Charlie Savage’s surprise promotion the most notable switch.

The son of former Wales international Robbie Savage, Charlie joined the squad after several withdrawals, with his previous two caps having both come against Gibraltar. Daniel James, Kieffer Moore and Sorba Thomas formed a reshaped frontline, while Chris Mepham and Connor Roberts were drafted into defence.

View image in fullscreen Craig Bellamy made a number of changes to the team that lost 1-0 in Portugal, but could not deliver a different result. Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Denmark were soon playing their way through a porous Wales midfield though, and chances came their way. Neco Williams was caught out by Joachim Andersen’s pass from the back and Isaksen flashed his shot wide. Isaksen then sent over a cross that Patrick Dorgu headed off target.

The hosts thought they had taken the lead after 24 minutes. Wales were exposed by a counterattack led by Mikkel Damsgaard and Isaksen met Rasmus Højlund’s cross with a thumping volley, only for VAR to rule offside in the buildup.

Damsgaard struck a post seconds later and it looked a matter of time before Denmark would score. But Dorgu headed off straight down the tunnel in a potential injury blow for Manchester United, and Wales began to create chances of their own.

Thomas was just off target from 20 yards after an Andersen error and Wales went even closer two minutes before the interval. Brennan Johnson got to the byline after working a one-two with Thomas and pulled the ball back to Roberts, whose shot under pressure was tipped away by Filip Jörgensen from close range.

Williams fired straight at Jörgensen at the start of the second half, but Wales were behind after 53 minutes from a free-kick. Damsgaard delivered a delicious ball and, while Højlund wheeled away celebrating the final touch, it ultimately went in off the unfortunate Davies for an own goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Isaksen put the contest beyond Wales after 66 minutes. Moore headed off the Wales goalline, but the Lazio winger was quickest on to the loose ball and his deflected strike went in off the underside of the bar.

Mohamed Daramy spurned a great chance to add further Danish gloss and both sides had late efforts ruled out, with Williams’s header disallowed for a push by Ethan Ampadu.

It does not get any easier for Wales with a visit from Erling Haaland’s Norway on Thursday, before a return date against Denmark in Cardiff.

“I said to the players before the game, ‘this is going to be tougher than Portugal’,” Bellamy added. “It was a different challenge, but a very difficult one. The best team won overall.

“As disappointed as I am with that, the result I probably think was fair. We move on. It will be a tough watch back. How the players put their bodies on the line was brilliant. They are really special for that. I really admire that, but I want more.”

Sports.title: Portugal manager issues response to Cristiano Ronaldo snubbing fans as historic streak ends
Sports.content:
Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insists it is up to Cristiano Ronaldo to explain his post-match dash down the tunnel.

Ronaldo was an unused substitute for the first time in 18 years as Portugal ran out 2-1 winners over Norway in Oslo.



2 The last time Ronaldo was an unused sub came at Euro 2008 Credit: AFP

However, it was his actions immediately after the contest that generated headlines.

Rather than celebrating with his teammates and the 500 Portuguese supporters who had made the journey, Ronaldo made a quick exit off the field.

Why did Cristiano Ronaldo snub Portugal's fans?

Speaking after the contest, Jesus admitted he was unaware of the Portugal skipper's act and explained why he chose not to bring him on.



"Only he can answer that," Jesus said regarding Ronaldo's fan snub.

"The fact is that just because he didn't play today doesn't mean I'm not counting on him.

"I told him I'd put him in, but I didn't think it justified making the change to a striker with Cris' characteristics."



Although Ronaldo did not see any action against Norway, Jesus hinted the five-time Ballon d'Or winner could return to the starting line-up for Portugal's clash against Denmark on October 1.

How Portugal's win over Norway unfolded?

Goncalo Ramos was handed a start up top and made the most of his opportunity, scoring the winner in the 54th minute.



The AC Milan striker cut out a pass from Norway goalkeeper Orjan Nyland and chipped the ball into an empty net.

Ramos thought he had his second goal of the night in the dying stages of the contest but it was ruled out by VAR for offside.

2 Ramos now has 12 goals for Portugal Credit: Getty

Joao Felix got things underway in Oslo when he struck in the 17th minute with a strike from the edge of the box.



Norway superstar Erling Haaland bagged the equaliser shortly after halftime, taking his international goal tally to 65 in just 57 fixtures.

But Ramos ensured Portugal departed with all three points in the Nations League contest.

Portugal's attention now switches to the fixture against Denmark.

The contest represents another chance for Ronaldo to inch closer towards his ambition of scoring 1,000 career goals.

Ronaldo, 41, is only 21 goals shy of his dream.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp oversees unwanted 62-year first as Germany hit historic new low
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp oversees unwanted 62-year first as Germany hit historic new low

Jurgen Klopp's nightmare start as Germany boss continued on Sunday night with a shock defeat to Greece.

The four-time World Cup winners were beaten 1-0 in the Nations League thanks to Dimitrios Kourbelis' second half strike.

5 Klopp is still waiting for his first win as Germany manager after losing to Greece Credit: Getty

It follows a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands on Thursday, leaving Klopp still awaiting his first win since taking charge.

Meanwhile, Germany's winless run now extends to four matches and dates back to a World Cup group stage victory over Ivory Coast on June 20.

What unwanted history has Jurgen Klopp overseen?

Their latest setback sees Klopp's side lose to Greece for the first time in their history.

In ten previous meetings, Germany had claimed seven wins along with three draws between the two sides.

The result also puts a dent in their hopes of reaching the Nations League Finals.

Germany now trail group B leaders Greece by five points with four matches remaining.

They sit third in the standings behind the Netherlands, who beat Serbia earlier on Sunday.

Klopp, who succeeded Julian Nagelsmann as national team boss in August, will be hoping to bounce back against Serbia in Munich in his side's next outing on Thursday.

Germany will then conclude the international break with a trip to Greece.

The two sides meet again in Thessaloniki in a week's time on October 4.

5 Greece claimed their first ever win over Germany on Sunday after 10 previous meetings Credit: Getty

Germany results against Greece November 1960: Greece 0-3 Germany October 1961: Germany 2-1 Greece November 1970: Greece 1-3 Germany November 1974: Greece 2-2 Germany October 1975: Germany 1-1 Greece June 1980: Germany 0-0 Greece September 2000: Germany 2-0 Greece March 2001: Greece 2-4 Germany June 2012: Germany 4-2 Greece June 2024: Germany 2-1 Greece September 2026: Germany 0-1 Greece

As well as suffering Germany's first-ever defeat to Greece, Klopp has also failed to win either of his opening two matches in charge.

The former Liverpool boss is the first national team head coach to not win any of their first two fixtures for since 1964.

Helmut Schon was the last Germany manager to achieve the unwanted feat 62 years ago.

His side were held by Sweden and Italy in his first two matches before thrashing Cyprus 5-0 in their next outing.

Schon would go on to win the 1970 World Cup and 1972 Euros during a legendary 14-year tenure.

He also reached the finals of both the 1966 World Cup and 1976 Euros in that period.

5

5 Klopp is the first Germany manager for 62 years not to win either of his first two matches in charge Credit: Getty

Since Schon's departure, nine different permanent managers had picked up a win in their first two matches prior to Klopp's appointment.

What did Jurgen Klopp say about Germany's defeat?

Speaking on the shock result, Klopp allayed any fears from Germany fans over their side.

He said: "The result isn't great, but it's part of the process - absolutely, the line-up, the way the team was put together, and all the changes were 100 per cent my responsibility.

"That was my idea, it was clear that we weren’t going to completely tear apart a deep-sitting opponent, I could have easily lived with not winning the game by a big margin, but you can’t lose it.

"The goal was unlucky, but it fits in a way with the situations they had, they were basically just playing long balls.

"We defended those first balls reasonably well in most situations, but we weren’t as dominant as we could have been given the physical quality of our players.

5 Germany sit third in their Nations League group after picking up just one point from two matches Credit: AFP

"We've only been together for a week, we're a newly formed team, so we need routines, football needs training, everything was great this week, except for large parts of this game."

But while Klopp is remaining upbeat, 2014 World Cup winner Bastian Schweinsteiger has claimed they are now only an 'average' side.

Speaking on ARD's coverage of the match, he explained: "We're no longer a top team. We're now just an average team.

"We no longer have players who make the difference. Even Greece have (Konstantinos) Karetsas, (Christos) Tzolis, (Vangelis) Pavlidis, for me those are players who make the difference.

"Hopefully Jurgen Klopp manages to develop a team that can play Klopp football."

Sports.title: Liam Gallagher leaks Man City’s punishment if club lose appeal over financial charges
Sports.content:
Liam Gallagher leaks Man City’s punishment if club lose appeal over financial charges

Manchester City will avoid being relegated and having their titles taken away if their appeal doesn't go their way.

That's according to Oasis legend Liam Gallagher, who has commented on his beloved club as they await their sanctions for breaching Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules.

3 Gallagher claims he has been told what sanctions City face for their FFP breaches Credit: Getty

City have been found guilty of almost all of the charges against them following an investigation by an independent commission.

It comes after the club were initially charged in February 2023 with 115 alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018.

talkSPORT understands both current and former Premier League clubs are weighing up taking collective legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, City are yet to be sanctioned for their offences amid a potential appeal against the commission's decision.

However, Gallagher has now claimed he has received word of what punishment awaits the club.

What has Liam Gallagher said about Man City?

The singer shared the news with his followers on X, writing: "Just been told by someone in a very, very high position if we lose our appeal, which we won’t, we’ll be getting a fine and transfer ban and that’s it.

"So all you desperate neurotic s****bubbles hush it up to ras. MCFC. LG."

His bold claim prompted one user to comment asking if Gallagher was allowed to say what he had posted.

In response, the 54-year-old added: "Just said it keep up."

What sanctions could Man City face?

Gallagher's expectation of a fine and transfer ban follows calls for a range of punishments from fans and pundits.

3 City will face a fine and transfer ban but avoid relegation, according to Gallagher Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Some supporters have argued City should face point deductions and relegations for their offences.

Meanwhile, talkSPORT's Henry Winter has called for the club to be stripped of the Premier League titles won during the period when the breaches occurred.

This would see City's 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18 titles taken off of them.

Elsewhere, there have been calls for the club's owners and senior officials to step down in the wake of the verdict.

talkSPORT understands the EFL are willing to work in tandem with the Premier League on potential punishments against City.

This could see the club face football oblivion by being expelled from both the Premier League and Football League.

3 City fans are awaiting their sanctions after being found guilty of almost all charges in their FFP case Credit: Getty

In practice, this would prevent City from continuing their existence any higher than the fifth-tier of English football.

Speaking on talkSPORT, Ben Jacobs explained: "My understanding is the Premier League have been pushing for a significant, a record, a ground-breaking, a severe points deduction, and even having Manchester City relegated.

"I can also exclusively tell you that if Manchester City are kicked out of the Premier League, the EFL plan to read the verdict, and they are willing, in solidarity, to back the Premier League position and try to keep Manchester City out of the EFL as well.

"So there's a danger in a doomsday scenario that Manchester City could be kicked out of football altogether."

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah dropped for Egypt clash as bizarre reason is given for axing
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah dropped for Egypt clash as bizarre reason is given for axing

Mohamed Salah will not feature for Egypt against South Sudan regarding fears over the playing surface.

The Trabzonspor forward has not travelled with the squad for their match at Juba Stadium on Tuesday.

3 Salah has scored 68 goals in 120 caps for Egypt since making his international debut in 2011 Credit: Getty

Salah is not part of the matchday squad for the Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in order to avoid picking up an injury on the astroturf pitch.

The upcoming match in Juba will be played on an artificial surface.

Due to the surface, a decision was made by the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) prior to their previous match for Liverpool legend Salah not to play.

The 34-year-old started Friday's goalless draw against Angola as his side began their qualifying campaign.

However, he will not be part of the side against South Sudan ahead of a potential return for Egypt's friendly clash with South Africa on October 4.

What have the Egypt FA said about Salah?

In a statement, the EFA confirmed their decision as well as explaining the reasoning behind it.

They said: "The Egypt national team's technical staff, led by Hossam Hassan, has decided to rest Mohamed Salah for the match against South Sudan scheduled for 29 September because of the playing surface.

"It was agreed between the national team's technical staff and Mohamed Salah before the Angola match that he would not play against South Sudan, and the technical staff preferred this approach in order to protect the player."

Salah has been captain of the national team since 2019 and has scored 66 goals in 120 caps for his country.

He was also part of their squad at this summer's World Cup, marking his second appearance at the finals.

3 Egypt have decided not to play Salah over fears he will pick up an injury on the astroturf pitch Credit: Getty

Egypt will be hoping he can guide them to a record-extending eighth AFCON title in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda next summer.

However, they have not added to their haul since 2010, with Salah's best finish at the tournament a pair of final defeats in 2017 and 2021.

As well as Angola and South Sudan, the Pharoahs will also face Malawi in their qualifying group.

Salah's absence on Tuesday comes amid a prolific start to his career in Turkey.

The ex-Reds winger joined Trabzonspor in August following his Anfield exit.

He signed a two-year deal with the club after a nine-year spell in the Premier League.

3 Salah started Egypt's goalless draw with Angola on Friday Credit: Getty

Salah has already scored seven goals and added two assists in six league appearances for Trabzonspor.

Those strikes include a hat-trick against Galatasaray in their last outing.

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane provokes anger from Real Madrid as Kylian Mbappe forced to leave France camp
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe's injury has reportedly created tension between France boss Zinedine Zidane and Real Madrid.

Mbappe linked up with the France squad for the opening round of Nations League fixtures, but was forced off less than an hour into Les Bleus' 1-0 win over Turkey on Friday - five minutes after scoring the decisive goal in Izmit.



2 Mbappe had to be substituted shortly after scoring his 67th international goal Credit: AFP

What injury has Kylian Mbappe picked up?

According to L'Equipe, Real Madrid wanted Mbappe to be rested amid concerns over a knee issue – but Zidane opted to play his captain from the start.

And while scans confirmed Mbappe had not torn his ACL, the 27-year-old has now left the France camp.

It has since been confirmed by Madrid that Mbappe suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee.



Zidane is said to have moved the striker into the care of Madrid medical staff quickly in an apparent step to ease tensions.

Madrid boss Jose Mourinho will hope to have his No.10 back as soon as possible, with Los Blancos playing five games between the resumption of the league season after the three-week international break and the end of October.



That run concludes with a trip to Barcelona for the first El Clasico of the campaign.

A blistering start to the season

Mbappe has been in inspired for for Madrid - racking up eight goals in as many games across all competitions at the start of this term.



However, Madrid have endured a rocky start to the new LaLiga season and sit fourth in the table after losing two of their opening seven matches.

They were beaten 2-1 by local rivals Atletico Madrid last time out, going down to ten men early in the second half as Dean Huijsen saw red.

And it proved to be a controversial encounter at the Metropolitano.

2 Mbappe has been involved in all eight of Real Madrid's games so far this season Credit: Getty

Madrid, who were left furious by the referee's decisions, felt Atletico should have had two men sent off themselves.



France's new era up and running

France, meanwhile, minus Mbappe, continue their Nations League League A Group 1 campaign away to Belgium on Monday.

That will be Zidane's second game in charge after he succeeded World Cup-winning manager Didier Deschamps.

Zidane had previously had two spells at the helm of Real Madrid, the club where he spent some of the best years of his playing career.

Between 2016 and 2018, he led them to an incredible three straight Champions League triumphs.



Madrid return to action – with Mbappe available, they'll hope – at home to Villarreal on Saturday, October 10.

Sports.title: Liverpool and Manchester United handed further injury blows as star duo are forced off
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Manchester United handed further injury blows as star duo are forced off

Liverpool and Manchester United's injury woes could be set to intensify after Sunday's Nations League action.

Both Cody Gakpo and Patrick Dorgu were forced off during the first half of their nations' respective matches.

3 Gakpo is the latest Liverpool player to suffer an injury on international duty Credit: Getty

Gakpo was taken off just 17 minutes into the Netherlands' clash with Serbia.

It comes after Alexander Isak left the Sweden camp to return to Merseyside early due to an injury.

The Reds have confirmed the striker will be assessed by the club's medical staff after scoring against Romania on Friday.

How did Cody Gakpo suffer his injury?

Fans will be hoping Gakpo will not be joining Isak on the treatment table in the coming days.

However, they face a nervy wait to discover the severity of the injury which ended his night early against Serbia.

Gakpo was on the end of a strong challenge from Sasa Lukic in the centre of the park just 12 minutes into the match in Belgrade.

Despite initially staying down after the foul, he appeared as if he would be able to continue, only to signal to the bench that he would have to come off moments later.

The 27-year-old was subsequently replaced by Ruben van Bommel in the 17th minute.

It did not appear to affect Xavi's side, though, as they took the lead through a Mexx Meerdink penalty before half-time.

Gakpo has two goals and four assists in six appearances across all competitions so far this season for Liverpool.

3 Gakpo was forced off following a heavy challenge from Lukic during the Netherlands' clash with Serbia Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Andoni Iraola's side return to action at home to Manchester City on Sunday, October 11.

The Reds boss is already without long-term absentees Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley.

How did Patrick Dorgu pick up his injury?

As for United, they face similar concerns over Dorgu after he lasted just over half an hour for Denmark against Wales.

The versatile full-back headed straight down the tunnel after limping off in the 31st minute to be replaced by Mohamed Daramy.

Dorgu's injury follows the news that Bruno Fernandes will miss Portugal's match on Sunday.

The Red Devils captain has been ruled out of his country's trip to Norway due to injury.

3 United also now face an anxious wait over the fitness of Dorgu Credit: Getty

Fernandes also missed training on Saturday having been taken off late on against Wales on Thursday.

However, he remains with the squad and has not been ruled out of their final two matches of the international break.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool striker gets stand named after him at World Cup stadium
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool striker gets stand named after him at World Cup stadium

Celta Vigo have renamed a stand after club legend Iago Aspas ahead of hosting matches at the 2030 World Cup.

The former Liverpool striker will also be honoured with a statue outside the entrance to the stadium.



3 Celta have renamed the Tribuna stand after all-time top scorer Aspas Credit: Getty

Aspas is Celta's all-time leading scorer and appearance maker having returned to his boyhood club for a second spell in 2015.

How many goals has Iago Aspas scored for Celta Vigo?

Either side of a disappointing two years at Anfield, the 39-year-old has scored 223 goals in 578 appearances for the club.

In contrast, the ex-Spain international scored just once in 15 matches for Liverpool between 2013 and 2015.



The veteran forward signed a new one-year deal with Celta in May through to the end of this season.

His legacy has now been immortalised in the stands as well as outside Bailados.



The club are have renamed the Tribuna stand after Aspas as part of their redevelopment project.

Their home since 1928 is currently being expanded ahead of the 2030 World Cup.



Once completed, the capacity will increase from 24,870 to more than 40,000 fans.

Ongoing work on the Gol stand had caused fans to speculate it would be the section named after Aspas.

A total of 7,000 new seats will be installed once it fully reopens in January, with the partially open stand currently holding just 800 supporters.

3 Aspas will also be honoured with a statue outside the entrance to Balaidos Credit: Getty



However, Aspas' name will instead adorn the Tribuna, which has been renamed the Iago Aspas Tribuna.

Mayor of Vigo Abel Caballero confirmed the decision in a video announcement as he responded to the online speculation.

Caballero explained: "Why the Tribuna stand? First, because it is already operational and, therefore, the name is immediate.

"Second, because it will be the stand with the largest capacity in Balaídos.



"And third, very importantly, because next to the Tribuna stand will be the sculpture that the City Council is going to install for Iago Aspas, right there in front."

He added: "Therefore, everything fits. So the Tribuna stand will immediately be called the Iago Aspas Tribuna stand, because it is already operational."

3 Celta's Balaidos will have its capacity increased to more than 40,000 ahead of the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

Celta's stadium renovation

Whilst the renovations began last year, work on the Tribuna is not set to begin until later in the season.



The stand will be reconstructed, with its capacity increasing from 5,500 seats to 16,000.

It will also be moved backwards to accommodate the additional seating.

Balaidos has been selected as one of 20 stadiums to be used in Spain, Morocco and Portugal for the 2030 World Cup.

The three nations will co-host the tournament alongside opening matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to mark the World Cup's centenary.



Celta's ground previously hosted matches during the 1982 edition of the tournament, which marks the last time Spain served as hosts.

Sports.title: Calls to strip Man City of Premier League titles as ex-club chairman wants ‘terminal’ punishment
Sports.content:
Manchester City face a 'hammering' after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Henry Winter, who has also called for Man City to be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won during the period in which they were found to be in breach of the rules.



2 It's been suggested City should be stripped of three Premier League titles, including their first under Pep Guardiola in 2017/18 Credit: Getty

City were found guilty on Friday of the majority of the 115 charges they faced and, if an appeal fails, they could be hit with unprecedented sanctions, including relegation multiple levels down the pyramid.

Asked on talkSPORT by Pete Graves what he thought City's punishment would be, Winter said: "I think they're going to get hammered.

"I think it will be 50 points [deducted] to trigger a relegation [to the Championship] this season, and then we'll see whether [things are taken further].



"There would obviously have to be some sort of agreement with the EFL if they were going to drop them into League One, but as the great [football finance expert] Kieran Maguire points out, that is possible."

Pressed on whether City could even be expelled from the top four divisions altogether and end up in the National League, Winter said: "That is a huge, huge punishment, but the severity of what they've done, as [former City and FA chairman] David Bernstein eloquently pointed out earlier – and he's a Manchester City fan – they absolutely deserve not just to have the whole book thrown at them but almost the whole library."



On the subject of City's Premier League titles from the 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18 seasons, Winter added: "I would wipe those."

The charges cover the period between 2009 and 2018, with Roberto Mancini, Manuel Pellegrini and Pep Guardiola each winning one of those titles.



Earlier, Bernstein had told talkSPORT City needed to be penalised in a way that 'affected their league status'.

"I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough," he began. "We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient.

"Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status.

2 Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 to 2003, overseeing the club's rise back to the top flight Credit: Getty



"And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing. Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down.

"But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know.

"I think it does depend partly on the timing."

City continue to protest their innocence over the charges.

Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak reiterated that point in a letter to fans on Saturday, writing: "Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began."

Meanwhile, talkSPORT understands that City players do not have relegation release clauses in their contracts.

Sports.title: Man City stars Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias spotted in deep post-match conversation as relegation threat looms following 115 charges verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City stars Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias spoke furtively following their international clash – just days after the club's guilty verdict in their battle against the Premier League.

Dias covered his mouth while Haaland shook his head in the aftermath of Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on Sunday night.

There is no way of ascertaining for sure what they were saying, but the club's future will no doubt be on players' minds after Friday's titanic news.

Dias obscures what he is saying, but also smiles at one stage, while Haaland uses two fingers to make a quotation gesture.

Man City have been found guilty of 114 out of 115 charges of breaking the Premier League's financial regulations, Daily Mail Sport understands. Potential punishments could include a fine, points deductions, being stripped of their titles, or even relegation.

Manchester City's squad will only get the chance to talk about it together in earnest next week when they return from the international break, with their next fixture coming at Liverpool on October 11.

Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias were locked in conversation after the Norway-Portugal clash

Dias covered his mouth while Haaland made a quotation gesture as they caught up

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges

Haaland had been scheduled to speak in a press conference ahead of the Portugal clash but was reportedly removed from that duty.

The striker has previously spoken on City's situation, though. After signing in 2022, he was asked if he had considered the investigation looming over City, to which he replied: 'No, I haven't thought of that or anything.

'I am confident that the club know what they are doing and I really don't think I should speak too much about this.'

We are yet to hear the thoughts of City's players on the topic but their former midfielder Rodri did say ahead of Spain's 3-2 victory over England at Wembley: 'They [Man City] always express the confidence that they never did something wrong and we believe in that.

'Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence.'

City have publicly maintained their innocence throughout the process, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak saying last week: 'Our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.'

It is inevitable that they will appeal the reported verdict.

Man City were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation

The charges stretch from the years 2009 to 2023, encompassing much of the Pep Guardiola era, though the most serious end at 2018

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

A three-man panel was tasked with considering the evidence, with the initial expectation a verdict would have been reached on the case within months. It has since taken three-and-a-half years.

The original 115 charges were extended to a total of 130 after an administration issue in what is the most expensive and wide-ranging case in English football history.

City remained steadfast in maintaining their innocence over more than 115 alleged breaches across eight years, some including the start of the Pep Guardiola era.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups.

In 2022, Guardiola said he would quit the club if he felt the club's hierarchy had ever lied to him. The next year, he said he would not walk out on his deal, even if he was relegated to League One.

The club have maintained that they are innocent throughout the process and are expected to appeal

Guardiola always insisted he was 'fully convinced' that the club is innocent and said in May: 'I trust them, I trust them. Because I spoke with them and I trust how they behave and how they did.'

City vehemently denied any breaches of financial rules but the investigation started in December 2018 after German website Der Spiegel published documents from a Football Leaks cache which had originated from Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto

It alleged that City had overstated sponsorship income with money paid from the club's owners instead of sponsors linked to Abu Dhabi.

Roberto Mancini's wages were said to have doubled via a secret contract with an Abu Dhabi club when he was at Man City, while they were also alleged to have broken rules over approaching young players.

The Mail on Sunday has led the way on reporting the story. In July 2021, they reported on emails that appeared to suggest that Man City had millions funnelled into the club by Abu Dhabi to help inflate their income.

Back in February 2020, the club were banned from the Champions League and fined £25million after they were found to have seriously misled European footballing governing body UEFA and broken financial fair play rules.

This was then lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport which also reduced the club's fine to £9m.

City spent £440million over the summer, equalling the British transfer record by signing Enzo Fernandez for £125million.

Staff at the City Football Academy learned of the news via Daily Mail Sport and other media reports. There was no official email, with some initially left fearing for their jobs and asking senior managers for an explanation.

'It felt like the club was completely blindsided,' one employee, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told this newspaper.

Sports.title: Dana White admits he 'doesn't know' if Tyson Fury's fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead after Gypsy King claimed rival wants to pull OUT of the £150m bout amid Eddie Hearn's feud with promoter
Sports.content:
Dana White admits he 'doesn't know' if Tyson Fury's fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead after Gypsy King claimed rival wants to pull OUT of the £150m bout amid Eddie Hearn's feud with promoter

Dana White has cast doubt over Tyson Fury's heavyweight blockbuster against Anthony Joshua, admitting that he has 'no idea' whether the £150million showdown will go ahead on December 11.

The battle between British boxing's biggest names was plunged into jeopardy over the weekend, with Fury claiming his arch rival 'wants to pull out' of the fight amid a dispute between White and Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn.

Fury's claim made for a dramatic escalation, with the pair announcing their Cardiff bout just over 24 hours earlier.

White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and had fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

That warning appears to have thrown the event into chaos, with Fury claiming Hearn's 'ego' is presenting a major stumbling block in the long-awaited bout taking place.

Dana White has admitted he has 'no idea' if Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will go ahead

Tyson Fury announced on Saturday that Joshua 'wants to pull out' of the December 11 contest

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference on Saturday night, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time. He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

White's comments follow Fury's expletive-laden Instagram video, in which he labelled Joshua and Hearn 'cowards'.

He said: 'Breaking News: Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight they are saying he is not going to fight now.

'They're little s*** house cowards, mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego, he's making up a million different things and threatening that "we're not going to fight" you little coward.

Fury and Joshua have been on a collision course for 15 years but a fight has never transpired

Fury and Joshua's fight was due to take place on Friday December 11. The pair are set to meet for a press conference on September 30

'AJ pull your finger out you white flag, yellow-bellied coward. You know now we're coming home, now I'm coming home the Gypsy King is coming back to the United Kingdom to thrash you in front of all my fans in Wales.'

Fury went on to call Joshua a 'body-building sausage'.

He also claimed that boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh is now looking to find a new person to fight Fury at 'the drop of a hat'.

Fury continued: 'So I hope [Hearn and Joshua] are happy you little cowardly b*******, I've never seen anything like [Hearn and Joshua] you pure s*** houses and this is mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. What a little p****.'

The 38-year-old then posted a mocked up poster of himself and light heavyweight champion David Benavidez, hinting that the 29-year-old American could replace AJ in the Cardiff contest.

It is understood that both men are set to pocket around £75million for arguably the biggest bout to be staged on British soil, if it goes ahead.

Sports.title: Wrestling superstar dead at 40... just hours after he performed on HBO in national championship match
Sports.content:
The wrestling world has been left stunned after it was revealed that AEW star PAC has died at the age of 40, just hours after performing in a huge pay-per-view show.

The English-born wrestler, real name Benjamin Satterley, competed live on HBO Max against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship in Chicago on Saturday night, eventually losing and shaking his opponent's hand.

He then appeared on the PPV event again shortly after, returning during the main event - a World Championship match-up between Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay.

Just hours later, AEW confirmed the tragic news of PAC's passing, but no cause of death or further details have yet been revealed.

In a statement, AEW said: 'All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac.

'A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability.

Wrestling star PAC has died just hours after performing on AEW's latest PPV event in Chicago

Then performing in WWE as Adrian Neville, the wrestling icon is seen at Wrestlemania in 2017

'Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley's family, friends and fans.'

Satterley had also previously competed in WWE under the alias 'Neville' from 2012 to 2018, once again known for his high-flying acrobatics.

On social media, fans were stunned to hear of the tragic news, with one writing: 'I'm completely lost for words, I just saw him on Wednesday. RIP PAC.'

Another added: 'In complete and total shock. There aren't words enough to describe how gutting this is. One of the greatest high flyers of his generation, still in his prime right now... nothing about this feels right or real...'

Retired wrestler and WWE exec Adam Pearce, meanwhile, posted on X: 'I'm speechless. My heart goes out to the family, friends, and everyone affected by the passing of Pac.

'Ben, you were an incredible performer. I truly enjoyed every interaction we had…even the ones that sucked. It was a pleasure to be around your passion, to watch you work, and to work alongside you. Godspeed, Bastard Pac. Rest well, my friend.'

Satterley hailed from Newcastle in the United Kingdom, and is seen posing there back in 2014

PAC was well-known around the world for his high-flying ability and he competed on Saturday

Tributes poured in from around the world for the wrestling legend after his death at just 40

WWE Diva Rhea Ripley said: 'What a tragic day. What an extremely talented person. Speechless… RIP PAC.'

Satterley was something of a globe-trotter in the wrestling world, first competing in the United Kingdom and also appearing in the likes of New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Mexico's Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre.

He earned himself the nickname 'The Man That Gravity Forgot' for his high-flying tricks, which garnered him a huge following around the world.

While at AEW, he won the All-Atlantic Championship in 2022 and became most famous as part of the 'Death Riders' group, alongside fellow members Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta.

Sports.title: REVEALED: Why Christian Horner could land dream Ferrari role, how Bernie Ecclestone is pushing his cause, Geri's view on an Italy move and the Prancing Horse chief who's under pressure: VOICE OF THE PADDOCK
Sports.content:
REVEALED: Why Christian Horner could land dream Ferrari role, how Bernie Ecclestone is pushing his cause, Geri's view on an Italy move and the Prancing Horse chief who's under pressure: VOICE OF THE PADDOCK

If Ferrari want to live up to their reputation and recreate a new chapter in their storied history, they should sign Christian Horner immediately.

They have not won a world championship since 2008, nearly 20 years ago, in which intervening years Horner accrued 14 titles at Red Bull, taking in the drivers’ and constructors’ garlands.

I can reveal that Bernie Ecclestone, best man at Horner’s wedding to Geri Halliwell 11 years ago, has lobbied for this outcome. And persistently so.

I understand that Piero Ferrari, second and only living son of the Scuderia’s founding father Enzo, is in support of the proposition Ecclestone is promulgating, and Piero remains a big player at the team, as vice-chairman and eminence grise.

He can see the benefits of the union, but it requires a leap of faith from chairman John Elkann – one over which he havers – to go outside mainland Europe to employee his team principal.

Horner gets on well with Elkann, very well. Indeed, Elkann supported Horner when he lost his job at Red Bull last year.

Frenchman Jean Todt was given the Ferrari team principal role to great success with Michael Schumacher in the late Nineties and the early years of this century, delivering five drivers’ titles, but, among the Maranello hierarchy, ‘an Englishman?’

Bernie Ecclestone was Christian Horner's best man in 2015 and is lobbying for him to get a new role at Ferrari

Upon that thought alone hinges whether Horner will ever take up the position at Ferrari.

Make no mistake, Horner is open to the idea of running the team, as he revealed in an interview in The Times last week.

‘At this stage in my life, there’s only one team for which I would accept non-participation in ownership,’ he said. ‘Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula One. It’s the dream. And arguably it’s the sleeping giant of Formula One.’

I understand that Geri would be open to the move to the Maranello area, living in Italy and splitting her time between their estate in Oxfordshire and house in Highgate, London, to support her husband.

For Ferrari, it would make eminent sense. They are struggling under the current clownish leadership of Fred Vasseur, whose health issues also cloud the issue.

He missed a day in Monaco this year with heart problems exacerbated by the stress of the job.

Vasseur’s CV also indicates he is ill-prepared for the task.

This Frenchman can count himself fortunate indeed ever to have been handed the chance to lead the Scuderia. For, based on his track record in Formula One, he hardly warranted such promotion. He entered the top tier of motor racing in 2016 as team principal of Renault. They finished ninth out of 10 in the constructors’ championship.

He moved to Sauber, later to be rebranded Alfa Romeo, the following year. He joined midway through the season and they finished 10th. Next year, eighth. Then eighth, ninth and six. He did not take them to one victory in that span, nor into the top half of the table.

This year Ferrari are doing OK, but with no chance of winning either title, despite lying second in the constructors’ standings behind Mercedes. There are grumblings at Maranello behind the cryptic scenes about his future.

Horner and wife Geri are open to the move to Ferrari's Maranello base

Vasseur, so successful as a boss in junior formulas, is widely seen as a man at sea where he is. And everyone at Maranello knows it. He has not bothered to learn more than a few words of Italian, either, which is not conducive to working there. There is an arrogance or a laziness in his failure to do so.

For Horner to work at Ferrari, he needs a free hand, to be able to hire and fire.

As Ecclestone explained: ‘He should say to them give me five years and I do it my way, totally, entire freedom, and if it works, I stay; if it doesn’t, you get rid of me.’

Bernie's got his gun back!

On the subject of Bernie Ecclestone, he was recently stopped by police after flying from Switzerland to Portugal – the two countries where he predominantly lives with his Brazilian wife Fabiana – for carrying a shotgun into the country.

I can reveal that the situation has been resolved amicably through talks with the authorities in Portugal.

Fabiana, 49, explained to police in Lisbon that the gun was being transported for clay-pigeon shooting and that, despite the lack of documentation Bernie carried (no ‘blue book’), all was above board.

The Ecclestones are happily reunited with the gun, and all is well.

‘It’s all been sorted and there is no problem; there never was any problem at all, really,’ Ecclestone, 95, told me.

Ecclestone and his wife Fabiana have their shotgun back after he was stopped upon entering Portugal

Time to give it up, Fernando...

Another abominable weekend just gone for Aston Martin in Azerbaijan. Both cars retired. How much longer should Fernando Alonso race on, one wonders? He is a great driver in my estimation. Yes, a two-time world champion, and a great one at that, but he has not won a race for 13 years.

The Spaniard is 45 and in a team going nowhere fast. Is it not time to stop to preserve his own dignity?

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini breaks silence on Manchester City guilty verdict: Club's former manager - accused of receiving 'double' contract from owners - insists it's 'not my problem'
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini breaks silence on Manchester City guilty verdict: Club's former manager - accused of receiving 'double' contract from owners - insists it's 'not my problem'

Roberto Mancini has claimed Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules is 'not my problem', despite the club's failure to disclose his full pay being among the alleged breaches.

The Premier League accused the club of widespread financial doping over an era of sustained success and Daily Mail Sport understands they have succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims.

City have won 26 trophies since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, including eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups and the Champions League as part of their 2023 Treble-winning season.

Among the alleged breaches by the club was an alleged failure to provide full details of Mancini's pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

In 2018, German publication Der Spiegel dropped a series of bombshell articles based on a tranche of emails obtained by subsequently convicted Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto.

It was claimed Manchester City had been effectively cheating by using a variety of underhand techniques to swerve both Premier League and UEFA rules on financial fair play.

Roberto Mancini has claimed Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules is 'not my problem'

Der Spiegel alleged in 2018 that Mancini received a separate payment for four days' work as a consultant on top of his Man City salary after being appointed the club's manager in 2009

Mancini, it was alleged, had signed a £1.45million a year deal with the club when he took over as City manager in 2009 but had also picked up £1.75million a year for four days' work as a consultant for Abu Dhabi side Al Jazira, which is also owned by Man City owner Sheikh Mansour.

The 61-year-old, who began his second spell as Italy boss earlier this week, defended Man City after being asked about the verdict while insisting the case was 'not my problem'.

'I don't think Manchester City were found guilty, on the contrary,' Mancini said, as per Gazzetta Dello Sport.

'It's not a problem that concerns me, but it's not a new thing.

'Manchester City are not guilty and the double contract is not my problem, but theirs if anything.'

During his time at Man City, Mancini led the club to victory in the 2011 FA Cup, representing their first major trophy since 1976.

Tony Pulis, who managed beaten finalists Stoke City, has claimed he feels 'cheated' following the verdict in the Man City case.

Mancini famously then led Man City to the Premier League title in the 2011-12 season, which was clinched by Sergio Aguero's injury time winner.

Mancini famously led Man City to the Premier League title in 2012, which was clinched by Sergio Aguero's injury time winning goal against QPR

Rio Ferdinand and David de Gea, who were part of the Man United side that dramatically finished second, have both called for Man City to be stripped of that title in recent days.

Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

As well as allegedly failing to provide full details of Mancini's pay, Man City were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups.

On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: The new Miracle at Medinah: Team USA completes wild comeback to win the Presidents Cup in front of Trump
Sports.content:
The new Miracle at Medinah: Team USA completes wild comeback to win the Presidents Cup in front of Trump

Team USA completed one of the greatest comebacks in Presidents Cup history to overcome their international rivals in front of a raucous crowd at Medinah.

The Americans headed into Sunday singles three points down and at risk of a humbling loss, but Scottie Scheffler and Co won eight of the 12 singles matches to seal an 11th straight win.

The day began with a rousing speech from Donald Trump, before the players went out and stormed back, with Jacob Bridgeman clinching the trophy for his country.

There were key rallies on the back nine by two-time major champion Collin Morikawa and 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun.

Outplayed over three days in team matches, the Americans leaned on their strength in singles to make up a three-point deficit.

President Trump was on the first tee for the start of all 12 singles matches, and he kept his speech short. 'It's going to be a very interesting game of golf,' he said.

Team USA celebrates after Jackson Koivun secured a huge win for his country at Medinah

Jacob Bridgeman holed the winning putt as America surged back from three points down

The day began with a speech from Donald Trump, who watched the start of all 12 matches

The president had hot-footed it to Illinois fresh from watching Texas beat Tennessee in Knoxville on Saturday, and he drew roaring applause from the packed grandstands at Medinah.

Dressed in a dark suit and red tie, Trump smiled, pumped his fists, and blew kisses to the excited crowd as spectators broke out into deafening chants of 'USA! USA!'

Taking to the microphone ahead of the Sunday singles matches, Trump poked fun at reports that he had requested a 15-minute speech window from the PGA Tour.

'You know, the fake news media will say I got a very bad reception. We got a good reception!' Trump told the cheering gallery.

'He [PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp] said, could you make a short speech? I said, no, I don't have the courage to make a speech - these people want to see golf, they don't want to hear speeches!

''I'll only say this: Our country is doing great, better than ever before.'

His Sunday arrival brought enhanced security measures across Medinah, with gates opening at 8 a.m. as the Secret Service implemented tight restrictions.

Koivun celebrates after birdieing the 12th hole on his way to a big win in the Sunday singles

Trump continued his whirlwind weekend of sport on Sunday after attending the Texas game

The lighthearted quip came after Golfweek reported on Saturday that Trump had asked organizers for 15 minutes to address the crowd before the start of play.

Trump stepped aside quickly to let the action begin, as Brandt Snedeker's U.S. squad looked to battle back from a 10.5 - 7.5 deficit against Geoff Ogilvy's International team.

On Sunday, it was Cameron Young and Justin Thomas who set the tone early. Scottie Scheffler took down Nico Echavarria with a show of pure sportsmanship when a spectator disrupted the Colombian's swing.

Patrick Cantlay had another moment, as he always seem to do in this competition, holing a birdie putt from just inside 60 feet on the par-3 16th against hard-luck Adam Scott.

Scottie Scheffler was another of the Americans who secured a big win at Medinah on Sunday

Trump is accompanied by Secret Service as he walks to make his speech at the Presidents Cup

Outside the gates at Medinah, some anti-Trump protestors spoke out against the president

Five matches remained on the course - the Americans were 1 up in three of them, the other two were all square. All the Internationals had to do was find three points from them. The Americans simply refused to budge.

Koivun was 2 down through 10 holes to the Internationals' top performer this week, Si Woo Kim, when he won three straight holes to flip the color to American red on the board. The kid drilled his tee shot on the 18th, and twirled his iron when he knew the approach was pure. He wound up with a 2-up victory, and then it was a matter of time.

The clinching point came from Jacob Bridgeman, who rolled in a 3-foot par putt on the 18th green for a 1-up victory over Min Woo Lee, assuring the Americans the 15 1/2 points they needed.

Sports.title: Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'
Sports.content:
Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'

Manchester City's former chairman David Bernstein believes punishment handed to the club after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules must affect their top flight status.

Daily Mail Sport reported that the Premier League has succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims against Man City, with the club found guilty of the 'vast majority' of the 115 charges of financial rule breaking.

An appeal from Man City is considered an inevitability, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak declaring on Saturday that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as Football Association chair 2011-13, has warned that financial penalties will not be enough of a punishment.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Bernstein stressed the fines would not be sufficient as he cited their vast spending in the previous transfer window.

Man City spent £440million in the summer and equalled the British transfer record signing £125million Enzo Fernandez.

Man City's former chairman David Bernstein believes the club's Premier League status is at risk after they were found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 rule break charges

Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as FA chair 2011-13

Bernstein believes that while the club's wealth would render a fine insufficient, Man City could face automatic relegation or a points deduction that effectively ensures they will drop out of the top flight.

'I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough,' Bernstein said.

'We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient.

'Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status.

'And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing.

'Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down.

'But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know.

'I think it does depend partly on the timing.'

Bernstien suggested Man City's wealth would make a financial penalty for the club 'insufficient'

Man City enjoyed staggering success during the years covered by the Premier League charges

Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that the verdict will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800million.

In late 2024, Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight – be found guilty.

Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City’s cheating.

On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak insisted the club remains confident of clearing their name and ‘proving innocence’

In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp's home debut falls flat as Germany suffer surprise defeat by Greece - as former captain tears into 'average' team
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp's home debut falls flat as Germany suffer surprise defeat by Greece - as former captain tears into 'average' team

Jurgen Klopp suffered defeat in his first home match as Germany boss as Greece earned a shock 1-0 victory in their Nations League match.

Dimitrios Kourbelis struck 16 minutes from time in Augsburg to give Greece, who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups, a famous win.

Kourbelis's deflected effort ensured Greece beat Germany in an international match for the first time.

Klopp is yet to win either of his first two games in charge of Germany after his team were held to a 1-1 draw by the Netherlands on his return to the dugout on Thursday.

The former Liverpool boss took the job after leaving his role as global director of football at the Red Bull group.

'The result isn't great, but it's part of the process, absolutely,' Klopp told ARD.

Jurgen Klopp suffered defeat in his first home match as Germany boss as Greece earned a shock 1-0 victory

Dimitrios Kourbelis scored the winner for Greece, who beat Germany for the first time

'The line-up, the way the team was put together, and all the changes were 100 per cent my responsibility. That was my idea.

'It was clear that we weren’t going to completely tear apart a deep-sitting opponent. I could have easily lived with not winning the game by a big margin, but you can’t lose it.

'The goal was unlucky, but it fits in a way with the situations they had. They were basically just playing long balls. We defended those first balls reasonably well in most situations, but we weren’t as dominant as we could have been given the physical quality of our players.

'We've only been together for a week, we're a newly formed team, so we need routines. Football needs training. Everything was great this week, except for large parts of this game.'

Klopp added: 'There's no reason for me to fall into depression and say: "we're so bad". We're not. But we're also not that good.

'I don't want the players to be judged conclusively: this one can't do this or that. If you want to criticise someone, do it with me.

'Let the new ones develop. The established ones, they're top players in their clubs, they have my support. And feel free to criticise me, but not the boys.

'I was surprised that some people booed. The future is as rosy as we imagine it. We're going at it with everything we've got. We'll continue down the path.'

Klopp defended his players post-match and volunteered to take the criticism for the defeat

Former Germany captain Bastian Schweinsteiger tore into the team after the defeat, the country's first against the Euro 2004 winners.

'We're no longer a top team,' said Schweinsteiger. 'We're now just an average team.

'We no longer have players who make the difference. Even Greece have Karetsas, Tzolis, Pavlidis - for me those are players who make the difference.

'Hopefully Jürgen Klopp manages to develop a team that can play Klopp football.'

Klopp had warned his side pre-match that they were facing Greece's 'golden generation'.

The Germany boss will have a new squad for their next two Nations League fixtures of the international break.

It followed him calling up 44 players earlier this month, with the former Liverpool boss splitting the group into two to handle the fixtures and give him an opportunity to assess more players.

Germany lie third in their Nations League group on one point, with Greece leading the way on six and the Netherlands lying in second on four.

Klopp will seek a first victory when Germany host Serbia on October 1, before taking on Greece again three days later.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits ‘toughest days’ of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."
