Bamakpeh, who has been a leading voice against the operationalization of this Executive Order, points out that this Presidential directive is crippling the businesses of local rubber farmers.

Bamakpeh, as usual, informed the media on the weekend that warehouses across the country are overflowing with unsold rubber, long-standing export contracts have been terminated, and thousands of smallholder farmers are now forced to sell at rock-bottom prices just to survive.

“Meawon Liberia Inc. and many other Liberian-owned companies have been completely cut off. We can no longer honor our international trade agreements. Our workers are now jobless, and farming families cannot sustain their homes or send their children to school,” he stated.

For him, Executive Order 151, which allowed the export of unprocessed rubber upon payment of US$150 per metric ton – a system he intoned, kept local businesses alive while generating revenue for government was the best option that supports the growth of local economy.

According to the Meawon boss, the new Order does not serve ordinary Liberians, but rather protects foreign concession companies and paves the way for a foreign monopoly over Liberia’s rubber sector.

During his appearance before the House Committee on Agriculture, when he was called to provide clarity on the controversies surrounding the Order, Minister Nuetah told lawmakers of the Lower Chamber of Liberia’s bicameral Legislature that the directive was the best way forward for the industry.

But to the local farmers, this is a betrayal of trust by siding with foreign interests and, as such, the President should have him dismissed and appoint a new minister who prioritizes the business interests of local farmers.

Most disappointingly, Bamakpeh noted that the ban was imposed without any grace period, despite the Ministry of Agriculture knowing that local exporters were holding huge stocks.

“The Minister has been confrontational with farmers in the field instead of addressing their welfare and this is really killing us. He is seeking foreign investors at the United Nations General Assembly while suppressing Liberian businesses at home,” Bamakpeh asserted.

“It is my perspective that Minister Alexander Nuetah is operating with executive shielding to the detriment of Liberia’s rubber industry. We urgently request that the administration repeal Executive Order 166 and dismiss the Minister of Agriculture without delay,” Bamakpeh added.

World.title: HH Says Zambia Is Peaceful, Opposition Says Look Closer
World.content:
HH Says Zambia Is Peaceful, Opposition Says Look Closer – A Discussion on Zambia’s Current State

President Hakainde Hichilema told world leaders at the United Nations that Zambia is a peaceful country where people can come and invest. Opposition leaders say the situation on the ground tells another story about zambia.

Foreign Affairs Minister Mulambo Haimbe read the President’s statement in New York. It said Zambia is not at war, and that people disagreed during the elections but handled their differences peacefully, reflecting the spirit of zambia.

“Zambia is at peace, Zambia is open for partnership, and Zambia is ready to grow,” the statement said.

The President invited investors to create jobs, build skills and grow businesses in farming, mining, energy, tourism and other sectors under the Grow Zambia Agenda. He said the Government will take lawful measures to stop any political dispute from turning into violence, and that Zambia is asking for a seat on the UN Human Rights Council from 2027 to 2029.

EFF leader Kasonde Mwenda said the President should not tell the world there is no crisis. Zambians are going through the hardest time since independence, he said, with a disputed election, a divided nation and opposition leaders in detention.

Mr Mwenda said Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others have been locked up on treason charges, which carry no bail, and asked the State to release them while it continues looking for evidence.

Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba said the President’s advisers either gave him wrong information or he chose to ignore it. He said the European Union, the African Union and others had raised concerns about the election.

The President goes to the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday and Wednesday to look for more investment for Zambia.

World.title: Zambia Is Not At War, Haimbe Tells UN General Assembly
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema told the United Nations General Assembly that Zambia is peaceful, stable and open for investment after last month’s elections. At home, opposition leaders rejected the message, saying the country is sliding into a deepening post-election crisis.

The statement was delivered on Saturday night at the 81st session of the Assembly in New York, and was read on the President’s behalf by Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Minister Mulambo Haimbe, who opened with a direct assurance.

“It is important to emphasise that Zambia is not at war. Zambia is a peaceful, stable and sovereign nation,” Mr Haimbe said.

The Head of State said the conduct of the August 13 general election, before, during and after voting, reflected citizens’ enduring commitment to democracy, national unity and constitutional governance. He acknowledged the differences that naturally come with a democratic contest, but said Zambia had shown they can be resolved through established constitutional and legal institutions.

“Our democratic process should never be mistaken for conflict or instability,” President Hichilema said. “Our message is clear: Zambia is at peace, Zambia is open for partnership, and Zambia is ready to grow.”

He said necessary measures, within the confines of the law, would be taken to prevent political disputes from degenerating into violence, armed mobilisation, insurgency or the emergence of militia groups.

The address doubled as an investment pitch. Mr Hichilema presented the Grow Zambia Agenda as the framework for moving the economy from basic fiscal stabilisation to wealth creation and job growth, with opportunities in mining, critical minerals, agriculture, manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, tourism and digital services.

“Our message to investors is: come to Zambia. Invest with us. Produce with us. Trade with us. Grow with us. Zambia is open for investment,” he said.

On climate, the President said Zambia was ready to contribute to global solutions, but those who contributed least to climate change must not bear a disproportionate share of its costs. He called for a fairer and more responsive global financial architecture, and reiterated support for United Nations reform, including permanent African representation on the Security Council in line with the Ezulwini Consensus and the Sirte Declaration.

He also thanked international election observation missions for their contribution. Mr Haimbe used the platform to reaffirm Zambia’s candidacy for the UN Human Rights Council for the 2027 to 2029 term, describing it as a reflection of the country’s commitment to constitutionalism, the rule of law, fundamental freedoms and human rights.

The message met firm resistance at home. Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) president Kasonde Mwenda said Zambians should be worried about a President who claims there is no crisis while the situation worsens.

“It is worrisome for Zambians to hear a President they expect to set the tone for resolving national problems declare that there is no crisis in the country when the crisis is deeper and degenerating,” Mr Mwenda said.

He said Zambians were living through their most difficult period since independence, and that the President’s assertions pushed citizens who look up to him into hopelessness.

“We have a disputed election and a polarised nation and political situation,” he said.

Mr Mwenda listed what he said citizens wanted answered: the blocked presidential election petition, alleged abductions and arbitrary arrests, and rising post-election tension. He singled out the long detention of opposition leaders Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others, who face treason charges.

“The accused are technically serving a sentence since treason is unbailable even before they appear in court,” he said. “The best the State could do for now is to free them as it continues its search for evidence.”

He added that the President’s tone at Friday’s swearing-in of the Deputy Auditor General suggested there was no room for reconciliation and healing, and urged the Head of State to search his heart.

Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba went further, likening the President’s claim of peace and tranquillity to shooting himself in the foot and questioning the role of those advising him.

“The Security and Law Enforcement Community briefs the President daily through intelligence reports, even on the tiny things,” Mr Sinkamba said. “If intelligence reports are indicating that there is no crisis, then the problem is with the advisors. But if intelligence indicates that there is a post-election crisis in the country and the Head of State is ignoring that, then the President is shooting himself in the foot.”

He said international bodies, including the European Union and the African Union, many of which helped finance the polls, had raised red flags about the election, and that international monitoring missions had witnessed the process and its aftermath first-hand.

“The whole world is watching,” Mr Sinkamba said.

Mr Hichilema now takes the same investment message to the United Arab Emirates, where he will be on a working visit on Tuesday and Wednesday at the invitation of Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan

World.title: DEC Summons Archbishop Banda Over Toyota Hilux As Opposition Cries Persecution
World.content:
The Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) summoned Lusaka Catholic Archbishop Alick Banda for questioning today over a Toyota Hilux allegedly obtained unlawfully from the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA). Police warned the public against any gathering or procession linked to his appearance.

The summons follows a warn-and-caution statement recorded from the cleric on January 5, 2026. Investigators allege that between April 22, 2021 and December 27, 2023, Dr Banda had in his possession a blue Toyota Hilux, registration number ALF 7734, suspected to have been unlawfully obtained from ZRA, contrary to Section 319 of the Penal Code, Chapter 87 of the Laws of Zambia.

The details were set out in a joint statement by DEC public relations officer Allan Tamba and Zambia Police Service spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi, who confirmed the date of the interview.

“He has been invited to appear before the Drug Enforcement Commission today in line with ongoing investigations,” Mr Tamba said.

The Hilux forms part of a wider investigation into about 22 ZRA motor vehicles alleged to have been improperly disposed of, an inquiry that has already resulted in court convictions against other individuals. The statement stressed that the charge against the Archbishop relates specifically to the alleged possession of unlawfully obtained property, and cautioned the public against inflammatory statements on the matter.

Mr Chilabi said only Dr Banda’s legal representatives and designated individuals connected to the case would be allowed to accompany him. He was equally clear about what was expected of everyone else.

“In view of the foregoing, members of the public are urged to refrain from engaging in any unlawful assembly, public procession, or conduct that may breach the peace or contravene relevant laws,” he said.

Police said they would take appropriate measures, in accordance with the law, to prevent any conduct that breaches the peace.

The opposition responded sharply. New Heritage Party (NHP) president Chishala Kateka said the Catholic Church was facing intense political persecution for standing up for the truth, and that the Archbishop had been singled out for his outspokenness.

“It is such a strange and unfortunate thing in as much as we are not privy to why he is being summoned again,” Ms Kateka said. “In my view, Bishop Banda is a target of persecution because of his courageous voice.”

She described the summons as part of a desperate political plot to hound the cleric out of office at all costs. It was in the public domain, she said, that the State had been trailing him for some time, and the action would be seen as an attack on the entire Church.

“It is in the public arena that some individual desperately wants Bishop Banda completely removed from his position,” she said. “It is just that the Catholic Church does not necessarily act on external political pressure.”

Ms Kateka tied the case to the arrests of other public figures. She said former minister Katele Kalumba was re-arrested at Ibex Police Station on Saturday, and warned that any citizen could be next.

“We cannot continue as Zambians to live in constant fear like that,” she said.

The only difference in the Archbishop’s case, she said, was that he had been respectfully summoned. She called for dialogue and reconciliation, urged the State to reconsider what she described as a militant approach towards perceived rivals, and said the DEC engagement should respect both the law and the office of the Archbishop.

Former Justice Minister Given Lubinda accepted the authority of investigators but pressed for openness.

“Let me be clear from the outset: no citizen, however prominent, is above the law,” Mr Lubinda said in a statement. “But equally, no citizen, however insignificant, is beneath the protection of the law.”

He said the DEC must act professionally, fairly, impartially and without intimidation, and asked the Commission to tell the nation whether the renewed summons concerned the vehicle over which the Archbishop was warned and cautioned in January. If it did, he said, the authorities should explain its basis within the limits of an ongoing investigation.

The joint DEC and police statement ties the summons directly to that vehicle, the January caution and the wider inquiry into the ZRA fleet.

State House, for its part, maintained that no one in Zambia is being persecuted. It said there are no political prisoners in the country, that the law should not bend for anyone because of status or position, and that people summoned by law enforcement agencies should comply rather than claim persecution, citing other leaders who had answered summonses and cooperated.

The Wake Up Campaign for a Better Zambia also backed due process. Its board chairperson, Bishop Joseph Malamba, called for national unity, healing and reconciliation, and referred to the detention of Mr Kalumba over a statement he described as inappropriate and divisive.

“These are some of the elements causing trouble and divisions in the nation,” Bishop Malamba said. “Individuals who breach the law through their conduct or statements should be dealt with through established legal processes.”

Dr Banda is due at the Commission today, accompanied only by his lawyers and designated individuals, with police pledging to act against any conduct that breaches the peace.

World.title: Kangwa suspension cost Zambia – Musonda
World.content:
Zambia legend Charles Musonda says Chipolopolo paid heavily for Kings Kangwa’s absence in the 3-1 defeat to Algeria in the opening 2027 AFCON qualifier.

Kangwa, now with Greek giants Panathinaikos, missed Friday’s clash at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium after being slapped with a CAF suspension for accumulating two yellow cards in Zambia’s final group game at the last AFCON in Morocco.

Zambia launched Group I with a loss, conceding twice after Fashion Sakala’s 57th minute equaliser had cancelled Jaouen Hadjam’s second-minute opener.

For ex-midfield dynamo Musonda, the aggressive line-up fielded by coach George Lwandamina – four players capable of scoring – lacked balance without Kangwa’s influence.

“For the first time in a long time, I saw a team with four players capable of scoring. We definitely missed the boy from Greece in midfield,” Musonda said.

Musonda also offered a blunt translation of Lwandamina’s post-match comment that Algeria “can make 10 teams” because of their population.

“When Chicken George says ‘population’ he means talent. Today, I am seeing Zambian players performing. That is how a national team should be selected on merit. Club level performance matters,” he said.

The former Anderlecht and Mighty Mufulira Wanderers icon weighed in on the goalkeeping debate after Willard Mwanza shipped three in Tizi Ouzou.

“Decide who your No. 1 goalkeeper is and trust him. Even the best make mistakes. Confidence matters. Mweene knows better. You can’t question him,” he said, backing trainer Kennedy Mweene.

Musonda praised captain Sakala for earning his place with a brilliant goal and constant threat, but demanded more defensive discipline.

“Nobody is bigger than the team. If you want your place, earn it through performances. Sakala did exactly that, brilliant goal and always looked dangerous but should help to make the defensive block even ‘K’ right side must do it,” he said.

He insisted Zambia has enough firepower to recover, listing Patson Daka “Cagliari boy”, Edward Chilufya “Sobolo”, Lameck Banda and the Tanzania-based contingent, but warned against individualism.

“We have options.. Daka, Sobolo, Lameck Banda and the Tanzanian boy. The talent is there. But they should not be selfish in front of goal. It’s the team that scores not an individual.”

Musonda, 1988 African Footballer of the Year runner-up, said he watched Togo’s 1-0 win over Burundi in Lomé, which left Zambia bottom of Group I, but believes Algeria-Zambia was the more competitive tie.

“I watched Togo-Burundi. Algeria-Zambia was more competitive but don’t take any team lightly. Football isn’t played on paper.. it’s played on the pitch. 90 plus minutes.”

With Chipolopolo now needing to beat Togo on September 29 at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola to keep their qualification hopes alive, Musonda called for unity.

“Now let’s stop talking and support the team in Ndola. We are a footballing nation from way back when our population was even less but had talent,” he said.

World.title: Government committed to promote peace, development
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has assured the international community that Zambia remains committed to peace, democracy and inclusive development, following the country’s recently concluded general elections.

President Hichilema has noted that Zambians exercised their constitutional right to choose their leaders during the polls, in line with Article 21 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights which affirms that the will of the people shall be the basis of the authority of government.

He has stressed that Zambia is not at war, but remains peaceful, stable and sovereign, noting that the democratic process should never be mistaken for conflict or instability.

The Head of State said this in a General Debate Statement delivered for him by Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mulambo Haimbe, during the United Nations General Assembly, in New York.

President Hichilema said despite political differences that naturally accompany elections, Zambia has demonstrated that such differences can and must be managed peacefully through constitutional and legal institutions.

President Hichilema reaffirmed the government’s unwavering commitment to preserving Zambia’s long-standing tradition of peace, stressing that authorities would continue to ensure political differences are addressed through due process of the law.

He added that the calm atmosphere before, during and after the elections reflects the Zambians’ enduring commitment to peace, democracy, national unity and constitutional governance.

The Head of State however added that measures would be taken, within the confines of the Constitution, to prevent disputes from degenerating into violence, armed mobilisation, and insurgency or militia groups.

He further encouraged partners to view Zambia through the lens of peace and stability, and to deepen support for programmes that promote inclusive economic growth, job creation, infrastructure development, human capital development, agriculture, energy, health and other priority areas.

“Our message is clear: Zambia is at peace, Zambia is open for partnership, and Zambia is ready to grow,’’ the Head of State emphasised.

He further expressed appreciation to international election observation missions for what he described as their invaluable support and contribution to Zambia’s democratic process.

The General Debates Session was held under the theme, “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All,’’ he stated.

World.title: Veep calls on Chiefs to promote peace, unity
World.content:
Vice President Mutale Nalumango has appealed to traditional leaders to continue promoting peace and unity in the country as a pre-requisites for national development.

Mrs Nalumango underscored the need for stability if developmental initiatives such as the Grow Zambia Agenda are to be successful.

Mrs Nalumango said this in a speech read for her by Minister of Green Economy and Environment, Gilbert Siame during the Walamo traditional ceremony of the Lungu people of Mpulungu district.

The Vice President highlighted the significant role traditional leadership plays in ensuring national building, and in the preservation of culture, and tradition.

“Let us build a country where culture and development walk hand in hand, a country where a child will be in school in the morning, and dance at the Walamo ceremony in the evening with pride and dignity,” Mrs Nalumango said.

And Mrs Nalumango says the government recognises the rich mineral endowments in Mpulungu and that the government will endeavor to ensure the full exploitation of minerals for the benefit of local people.

The Vice President added that Mpulungu district is well-positioned to contribute to renewable energy.

“I have been informed that there is potential for high grade lithium in this area and we all know that it is important for clean energy,” she said.

She further emphasised the need for responsible mining activities and ensuring that water sources remain safe.

Mrs Nalumango also called on young people to take advantage of the small-scale and artisanal fund under the Ministry of Mines and Mineral Development once operational and benefit from it.

And Senior Chief Tafuna, Mwine bu Lungu, Chimwando II, reiterated his chiefdom’s commitment to fostering national healing in the post-election period.

Speaking through his representative, Jane Sakala, Senior Chief Tafuna said people of bu Lungu will continue to preach peace and tolerance.

“Elections come and go, but our country remains, let us not allow politics to divide us,” he said.

The 2026 Walamo Traditional Ceremony was celebrated under the theme “Preserving our cultural, traditional, and customary heritage.

World.title: FAZ appoints Copper Queens Assistant Coaches
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) has appointed ZESCO Ndola Girls Head Coach, Florence Mwila and Technical Advisor Wisdom Zulu as first and second assistant coaches on an interim basis to reinforce the Copper Queens technical bench ahead of the back-to-back 2028 Olympic qualifiers against Uganda.

The appointments are with immediate effect.

FAZ General Secretary, Charles Chakatazya disclosed this in a press statement released to ZANIS in Lusaka today.

Chakatazya said the two coaches have been called by the FAZ Technical Committee to assist Head Coach, Charles Haalubono prepare the Copper Queens for the two-legged Olympic qualifier against Uganda.

ZESCO Ndola Girls Head Coach, Florence Mwila, who is also Head Coach of the Zambia Under-20 Women’s National Team, guided the Copper Queens to victory at the 2024 COSAFA Women’s Championship as interim coach.

She became the first female coach to lead Zambia to the regional title and previously served as Assistant Coach to the late Copper Queens Coach, Bruce Mwape.

The Copper Queens will face Uganda in an away match in Kampala on October 8, 2026 in their first leg of the 2028 Olympic qualifier, while the return game will be played home at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on October 13, 2026.

Chakatazya said FAZ will continue supporting the technical bench as the Copper Queens seek to qualify for their third consecutive Olympic Games.

The FAZ General Secretary has also called on soccer fans and all football stakeholders to rally behind the ‘girls’ including an all-local technical bench.

World.title: Government making strides to build local vaccine manufacturing
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema says Zambia is making deliberate efforts to build capacity for local vaccine manufacturing as part of measures to strengthen the country’s health security and resilience against future epidemics.

President Hichilema has noted that Zambia has increased investment in the health sector, aimed at building a stronger, more resilient system capable of safeguarding lives and livelihoods, while positioning the country to contribute meaningfully to global health security.

He has, however, noted that despite these gains, Zambia remains vulnerable to epidemics therefore calling for the expedited conclusion of negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing Annex under the WHO Pandemic Agreement.

The Head of State said this in a General Debate Statement delivered for him by Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mulambo Haimbe, during the United Nations General Assembly, in New York.

The President reported that the government increased domestic budgetary allocations to the health sector from approximately 7 percent to over 10 percent, enabling the recruitment of health workers, expansion and modernisation of health infrastructure, and improved availability of essential medical supplies.

He however stressed the importance of strengthened access to technology and enhanced preparedness capacities to detect and respond to future health threats.

President Hichilema further urged the international community to build a fairer global system that provides developing countries with affordable financing, policy space for economic transformation, and stronger climate action backed by adequate resources.

He said Zambia continues to face the devastating effects of droughts, floods and changing weather patterns, which have severely impacted agriculture, food security, water availability, energy generation and livelihoods.

The Head of State stressed that while climate impacts transcend borders, vulnerable nations such as Zambia should not be left to bear the greatest costs despite contributing least to global emissions.

He called for predictable, accessible and affordable climate finance, technology transfer, and greater investment in adaptation and resilience, consistent with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.

“For Africa, adaptation is not optional. Our farmers require climate-resilient agriculture; our communities and cities need resilient infrastructure; our energy systems must become more diversified; and our water resources, forests and ecosystems must be protected,” the President stressed.

President Hichilema also reaffirmed Zambia’s commitment to strengthening water security, climate resilience and sustainable management of natural resources, while ensuring that climate and water action delivers tangible benefits for future generations.

He noted Zambia’s active participation in preparations for the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, where the country is co-chairing the Interactive Dialogue on Water for Cooperation with Finland, emphasising the importance of water security to climate resilience and sustainable development.

World.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Fails to Return Home, 'Hale and Hearty', Says Presidency
World.content:
The presidency said the president would also attend events marking Nigeria's 66th Independence Anniversary and the premiere of a film commemorating the late MKO Abiola.

The presidency has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu's prolonged absence from Nigeria, saying he is "hale and hearty" and will return to the country this week.

The Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, said Mr Tinubu had been on a working vacation and continued to perform his official duties from abroad.



"President Tinubu is hale and hearty. He has been on a working vacation, which he is perfectly entitled to," Mr Onanuga said in a statement on Sunday.

The statement came after growing criticism of the president's absence from Nigeria, including his decision not to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Mr Tinubu left Nigeria on 30 August for London to begin a three-week annual leave, which the presidency later described as a working vacation. He later travelled to Paris, France, where he met French President Emmanuel Macron and French businessman Vincent Bolloré.

On 21 September, the presidency announced that Mr Tinubu had extended his stay abroad by a few days and would return to Nigeria at the weekend.

While in France, Mr Tinubu attended the signing of agreements between the Ogun State Government and DP World for the development of the Gateway Deep Sea Port and the Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone.

The projects are expected to attract more than $7 billion in initial investment and create over 50,000 direct jobs, according to the Ogun State Government.

The proposed deep seaport at Ogun Waterside is expected to have a four-kilometre berth and an 18-metre draft. The project is intended to ease pressure on the Lagos port corridor and improve Nigeria's capacity for maritime trade and exports.

Mr Onanuga argued that Mr Tinubu's physical absence from Abuja had not prevented him from discharging his responsibilities.

"In this digital age, he does not need to be physically present in Abuja to do the work for which he was elected in 2023," he said.

The president's absence from the UNGA, however, has continued to attract criticism from opposition politicians.

Peter Obi, the 2023 Labour Party presidential candidate, on Sunday questioned Mr Tinubu's whereabouts and criticised his absence from the global gathering.

"Where is Nigeria's President?" Mr Obi asked in a post on X.

Mr Obi said Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama's address to the 81st UN General Assembly demonstrated the importance of presidential representation at the gathering.

He questioned why the president of Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, had been absent from the UNGA for three consecutive years.

"Although our Vice President, Kashim Shettima, was present, the question remains: Where is the President?" Mr Obi wrote.

The presidency has previously defended Mr Tinubu's decision to skip the UNGA, saying Nigeria was adequately represented by Mr Shettima, who delivered the country's national statement. The government also said the president remained in contact with officials at home and continued to direct government affairs while abroad.

The criticism has extended beyond Mr Obi. A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party led by former minister Kabiru Turaki criticised the extension of Mr Tinubu's vacation, arguing that he should have travelled to the United States for the UNGA after his engagements in Europe.

Close 

The African Democratic Congress also questioned the constitutional implications of the prolonged absence of both Mr Tinubu and Mr Shettima, while some lawmakers called for the National Assembly to examine whether the constitutional procedure for presidential absence had been followed.

Mr Onanuga, however, said Mr Tinubu would return home this week.

The presidency said the president would also attend events marking Nigeria's 66th Independence Anniversary and the premiere of a film commemorating the late MKO Abiola, the businessman and democracy campaigner who died in detention after the annulment of the 12 June 1993 presidential election.

World.title: Sudan: Army Rejects Ethiopia's Allegations of Supporting Opposition
World.content:
Khartoum — The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) categorically reject allegations made by the Ethiopian Army's Chief of Staff that Sudan is supporting the opposition, describing them as baseless, at a time when information and facts indicate the continued support and assistance provided to the Rapid Support (RSF) Militia (Janjaweed) from Ethiopian territory, including training, supplies, and the use of Ethiopian territory for military activities, including strategic and suicide drones.

In a statement issued by its Spokesperson, the SAF said, "We have followed the statements made by the Chief of Staff of the Ethiopian National Defense Forces, including the allegations that Sudan is supporting the Ethiopian opposition."

The statement continued, "The Armed Forces reaffirm that Sudan is committed to international law and the principles of good-neighborly relations and does not interfere in the internal affairs of other states. At the same time, Sudan will not allow any infringement upon its sovereignty or national security."

The Armed Forces called on the Ethiopian side to exercise accuracy and responsibility and to resort to dialogue and official channels in a manner that preserves the security and stability of both countries and the region.

The SAF Spokesperson concluded, "The Sudanese Armed Forces will remain vigilant in protecting the nation's borders and sovereignty and capable of confronting any threat to its security and stability."

World.title: Liberia: Poor Road Conditions Spark Outcry
World.content:
Large and small vehicles get stuck on poor roads in rural Bong County, as in other areas of Liberia (file photo).

Monrovia — Rural dwellers are decrying increasing bad road conditions they are facing at the time of the presence of yellow machines brought into the country by the government to help with roads improvement across the country.

From Montserrado, to Nimba, Grand Gedeh, Lofa, Gbarpolu, as well as other counties, the cries about bad road conditions remain the same, as citizens endure tough times traveling from one region to another.

Here in Montserrado County, residents of Todee District have raised concerns over the poor condition of roads in the area, saying the situation is affecting transportation, economic activities, and access to essential services.

The concerns were highlighted during a live coverage by DN-News Online TV, where residents described the road conditions as difficult and called for urgent government intervention.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

According to the residents, the deplorable condition of the road is making it difficult for people to move between communities and for farmers and traders to transport their goods to markets.

They said motorists and passengers are also spending extended periods navigating the difficult road conditions, resulting in delays and increased transportation costs.

Motorcyclists and vehicle drivers are reportedly among those facing major challenges, with difficult sections of the road making transportation more stressful and contributing to vehicle damage and additional maintenance expenses.

Residents said the road challenges are also affecting their daily economic activities, particularly farmers who depend on reliable transportation to move agricultural products from their communities to market centers.

They further expressed concern that the poor road conditions could affect access to essential services, including health care, education, and other services that require regular movement between communities.

During the live coverage, residents appealed to the government and relevant authorities to pay urgent attention to the road situation and consider rehabilitation efforts.

They said improving the road would help reduce transportation difficulties, support farmers and traders, and make it easier for residents to access markets and essential services.

Residents of Todee believe improved road infrastructure would also contribute to economic activity and the overall development of communities in the district.

They are therefore calling on the government, particularly the relevant road authorities, to assess the situation and take steps to address the challenges faced by residents and road users.

World.title: Mozambique: Two Die as 40,000 Flock to Macaneta Beach on Holidays
World.content:
Maputo — At least two people have lost their lives amidst large crowds at a popular tourist Macaneta Beach, in Marracuene District, southern Mozambican province of Maputo.

The tragedy occurred on Friday during celebrations of a national holiday, which marked the 60th anniversary of the National Liberation Struggle and the 51st anniversary of the Armed Forces for the Defense of Mozambique (FADM) Day.

According to Shafee Sidat, mayor of Marracuene, the deaths occurred outside the sea, after 30,000 to 40,000 people flocked to the beach.

"There were no deaths by drowning at the beach, contradicting reports circulating that about 20 people had died during the gathering. We deployed municipal police, local authorities and lifeguard teams to ensure the safety of beachgoers", he said.



The large concentration of people was also accompanied by incidents of petty crime, "particularly mobile phone theft, as well as the accumulation of large amounts of rubbish on the beach and along access roads."

The authorities acknowledged that there are safety challenges, but "stricter measures will be implemented to strengthen safety and improve the organization of the area during periods of high visitor numbers."

The mayor further said that Macaneta Beach should become an example of organization and discipline, calling on visitors to help preserve public spaces.

Elias Nobel, a lifeguard, explained that rescue teams carried out about 30 interventions involving people at risk of drowning, with all the operations successfully completed.

On Saturday morning, cleaning teams began removing accumulated waste from the road leading to Macaneta at around 6:30 a.m., where large quantities of bottles and broken glass were found.

The clean-up operation is expected to continue due to the volume of waste, according to those responsible for the operation.

Authorities are urging beachgoers to use the available waste collection points and avoid leaving rubbish on the ground, particularly bottles and other sharp materials that could pose a risk to people and vehicles.

World.title: Kenya: Hospitals Risk Social Health Authority Lockout As Contracts Expire
World.content:
Nairobi — Healthcare providers across the country risk being locked out of the Social Health Authority (SHA) system from Thursday if they fail to complete the contracting process for the new 2026-2029 cycle.

In a notice issued on Monday, SHA Chief Executive Officer Dr Mercy Mwangangi said existing contracts with healthcare providers will expire on September 30, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.

The authority warned that facilities that have not secured an executed contract for the new cycle will no longer be allowed to provide services to SHA beneficiaries from October 1.

Their access to the SHA provider portal will also be switched off, raising concerns over possible disruptions for patients who depend on the facilities for treatment.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Providers without an executed contract for the 2026-2029 cycle will not be permitted to offer services to SHA beneficiaries after that date, and their access to the SHA provider portal will be switched off," Mwangangi said in the notice.

The warning comes just days before the expiry of the current contracts, placing hospitals and other healthcare facilities under pressure to complete outstanding requirements.

SHA has urged providers that wish to continue serving its beneficiaries to apply for a new contract and complete the contracting process before October 1.

The authority said facilities that fail to secure new contracts should make arrangements to transfer patients already receiving treatment to contracted providers to ensure continuity of care.

The directive could particularly affect patients undergoing ongoing treatment, including those requiring regular reviews, procedures or other services covered by SHA, if their preferred facilities are not among those contracted under the new cycle.

SHA said the contracting exercise is part of the transition to the 2026-2029 provider contracting cycle, which was launched earlier this month through the authority's new electronic contracting platform.

The Ministry of Health said the new framework, known as HAKIKA, is intended to strengthen contracting, verification, payment and accountability arrangements between SHA and healthcare providers.

The new contracts cover services under the Primary Health Care Fund, Social Health Insurance Fund, Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund and the Public Officers Medical Scheme Fund. The contracting period runs from October 1, 2026, to June 30, 2029.

The electronic contracting portal allows facilities to submit applications, provide supporting documents, complete verification and execute contracts digitally.

The latest notice, however, puts the responsibility on individual providers to ensure they have completed the process before the deadline.

SHA asked providers with outstanding contracting requirements to act promptly to avoid interruptions to services for beneficiaries.

World.title: South Africa: Elections 2026 - How This North West Town Went From Boom to Bust
World.content:
Stormwater pipes have been lying on the roadside for two years, according to residents in Matlosana Local Municipality in the North West of South Africa.

Matlosana municipality is under a financial recovery plan after years of mismanagement

The City of Matlosana Local Municipality in the North West is under a financial recovery plan after years of mismanagement, with billions of rands owed.

Residents report flooded roads, unreliable water and electricity, sewage spills and deteriorating infrastructure.

Matlosana's unauthorised, irregular, fruitless and wasteful expenditure reached R10.8-billion by 2024/25, while the municipality takes about 600 days to pay creditors.

The Auditor-General found that Matlosana spent 85% of its allocated budget but achieved only 58% of its basic service and infrastructure targets, while water losses reached 57% and electricity losses 44%.

"Forgotten" by the municipality is how Gideon Matseke describes his community in the township of Khuma, east of Stilfontein in the North West City of Matlosana.

Its untarred roads were flooded when we visited. Stormwater pipes have been left for two years on the roadside and never installed.



But according to Matlosana's 2024/25 annual report, the stormwater project is complete. Meanwhile roads and sometimes homes are flooded when there are heavy rains.

The City of Matlosana Local Municipality is home to about 430,000 people and includes Klerksdorp, Jouberton, Orkney, Kanana, Stilfontein, Khuma, Hartebeesfontein and Tigane.

Decades of mine closures have compounded years of municipal mismanagement. The once booming gold-mining area is now a distressed municipality placed under administration. Residents told us the water and electricity supply is unreliable and sewage spills are common.

In the township of Kanana, south of Klerksdorp, resident Richard Ndlovu said sanitation is one of their biggest concerns. The local pump station has not been working for years, he said.

Raw sewage spilling from the station has eroded a channel and now flows into the Skoonspruit River, a tributary of the Vaal.

Ndlovu said taps run dry and he sometimes has to collect water from other areas for his mother, wife and three children.

Residents of Klerksdorp, the administrative and economic centre of the municipality, also say they are battling with inconsistent water and electricity and deteriorating infrastructure.

Gerard Horn, who has lived in central Klerksdorp for decades, said municipal services are "collapsing". He is currently in a dispute over his utility bills. The Auditor-General (AG) has flagged estimated billing for utilities in Matlosana.

Beside his house is a collapsing stormwater drain which he reported months ago. "Every day [the hole] gets closer to the fence," he said.

He said the potholed streets frequently burst car tyres. "Things are just not maintained," he said.

Ward 39 councillor Inge Wilken (DA) said complaints are often ignored and when repairs are done the work is "shoddy". In her ward, she said, live electrical wires run across streets, "sometimes patched up with cheap insulation tape", placing children at risk.

The AG, national and provincial government, Parliament and civic organisations have raised concerns about factional battles, alleged corruption, and deteriorating service delivery in the municipality.

Matlosana has been in and out of administration since 2013. Governance failures have eroded oversight mechanisms, noted cooperative governance minister Velenkosini Hlabisa in a recent parliamentary response.

Matlosana is now operating under a mandatory Section 139 Financial Recovery Plan, overseen by Moatlhodi Dilotsotlhe, who was appointed by the province.

The National Treasury temporarily withheld R299-million of Matlosana's July 2026 equitable share allocation in part due to its failure to investigate and take action on unauthorised, irregular, fruitless and wasteful expenditure, which stood at R10.8-billion at the end of 2024/25.

It takes the City roughly 600 days to pay creditors, 20 times longer than stipulated by the Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA). This has caused contractors to halt work on key projects.

Mayor Fikile Mahlophe told Parliament in August 2026 that funds from the Treasury have since been released after the municipality "demonstrated progress" on disciplinary boards and creditor payments.

The municipality largely blames budget constraints for its woes, citing how its monthly collection rate averages around 60% due to mine closures and economic decline.

But the AG points to a much larger crisis in its recent qualified audit opinion. It found 85% of allocated budget was spent, but the City achieved only 58% of its basic service and infrastructure targets.

R156-million of a R295-million budget was spent on repairs and maintenance. This equates to less than 3% of the value of its infrastructure, whereas Treasury's minimum recommendation is 8%.

The lack of maintenance and underinvestment is evident in the City's water losses that stand at 57% (2024/25).

Wilken noted that one water leak in her ward has been ongoing for over two years.

Matlosana currently owes R2.8-billion to the Midvaal Water Company.

Electricity losses stand at 44%. Although the municipality received a R380-million write-off through the Eskom debt relief programme, finance minister Enoch Godongwana said that R1.92-billion was still owed to Eskom at the beginning of August.

This debt has "limited the municipality's ability to fund day-to-day operations", the AG said.

Tens of millions of rands were spent on external financial consultants, the AG noted.

Of the municipality's eight planned water pump station refurbishments, the City says several stations, including Kanana and Jouberton, have been completed. But residents say they still experience water shortages.

In Kanana, only five of 1,150 planned outside water-borne toilets were constructed. Mahlophe said that extortion by construction mafias had halted work. He subsequently told the Standing Committee on Public Accounts (SCOPA) that roughly 2,700 toilets have since been completed.

The AG served the City with four material irregularity (MI) notifications involving financial losses, public harm and systemic non-compliance.

The AG told SCOPA that cases involving potential fraud, corruption, and supply chain management failures had been referred to the Public Protector and the Hawks on 28 April 2026.

Sewage spills from dysfunctional wastewater treatment works pose an environmental threat and health risks. The AG referred an MI relating to continuous pollution at Orkney treatment works to the Department of Water and Sanitation on 14 April 2025.

The City conceded in its 2024/25 annual report that service delivery has been "inadequate, posing health risks" and "continues to impede economic growth".

Political instability

Matlosana has been politically unstable for some time. Chief financial officer (CFO) Mercy Phetla was formally dismissed after a prolonged disciplinary hearing and battles in the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) and in court.

She has denied all allegations, but a December 2025 disciplinary inquiry chaired by advocate Smanga Sethene found Phetla guilty of "calculated acts designed to defraud the municipality".

Phetla was accused of financial misconduct, exceeding delegated authority and receiving kickbacks from a service provider. Her VW Amarok, valued at R1.4-million, was seized by the NPA in November 2025.

Allegations include approving duplicate and irregular payments that lost the municipality millions, and making awards without required tax clearances and declarations, while documents linked to duplicate payments were allegedly removed from municipal premises.

The disciplinary report recommended her dismissal, which was done by municipal manager Lesego Seametso in January 2026. A criminal case was also opened.

Close 

MEC Gaoage Molapisi told GroundUp that although there were severe factional battles, now that the CFO has been dismissed he said things are now "functioning well". The PER's term of reference has been extended, assuming large responsibility of the council and accounting officer

Yet in early February, factions supporting Phetla in the ANC-led council along with councillors from smaller parties voted to reverse the enforcement of the independent findings and withdraw Phetla's termination letter. The High Court in Mahikeng then halted this.

Phetla challenged the disciplinary action in court, but a High Court application and subsequent appeal in the Supreme Court of Appeal were dismissed. The CCMA later found the dismissal procedurally fair and substantively justified.

Matlosana's council then suspended Seametso over alleged financial and operational irregularities on 31 March, before an April High Court ruling ordered her reinstatement. The court said municipal attorneys had failed to produce a valid council resolution of the suspension. Some in the opposition, including DA caucus leader Gerhard Strydom, called Seametso's suspension "procedurally flawed and unlawful" led by "a faction" on the side of Phetla.

The municipality is pursuing recovery of funds and blacklisting contractors linked to the irregular payments.

The prolonged factional battles in council led to the intervention of North West cooperative governance MEC Oageng Molapisi. Announcing another provincial government intervention in February, Molapisi cited "councillors being divided" between Phetla and Seametso.

Molapisi told GroundUp that although there were severe factional battles, now that the CFO has been dismissed things are "functioning well".

The provincial executive representative's term of reference has been extended.

GroundUp has been waiting for comment from the City of Matlosana since 11 September.

World.title: Kenya: Nairobi Motorists Face More Delays As Eldoret Road Closure Extended
World.content:
Traffic in the streets of Nairobi (file photo)

Nairobi — Motorists using Eldoret Road in Nairobi will have to contend with an extended road closure after the Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) pushed the reopening date to December 30.

The affected section, which was initially scheduled to reopen on September 18, will now remain closed until 6pm on Wednesday, December 30, 2026, as works on a vehicular bridge across the Nairobi River continue.

KURA said the extension had been necessitated by unforeseen logistical and site-related challenges encountered during construction of the bridge.

The authority cited delays in the delivery of critical construction materials and equipment, saying the setbacks were beyond the contractor's control.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The extension has become necessary due to unforeseen logistical and site-related challenges encountered during the construction of the Vehicular Bridge across the Nairobi River, including delays in the delivery of critical construction materials and equipment," KURA said in a public notice.

The closure had initially taken effect at 6am on Monday, May 18, with motorists advised to use alternative routes while construction was underway.

The latest extension means motorists will have to continue using the alternative traffic arrangements already in place for several more months.

KURA urged motorists to follow directions from traffic police officers and traffic marshals to ease movement around the affected section.

The authority said it remained committed to completing the bridge within the revised timeline while meeting the required safety and quality standards.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused as we endeavour to Transform Urban Mobility," KURA said.

The affected section lies along Eldoret Road near the Nairobi River, with alternative traffic movements provided through connecting roads, including Wangu Road, Heshima Avenue, Mohammed Yusuf Road, Sinoni Road and 19th Street.

The traffic plan also provides for pedestrian movement through a temporary pedestrian bridge.

The extended closure is expected to continue affecting motorists travelling towards Eastleigh, Uhuru Estate and Jogoo Road as construction works proceed.

KURA has advised road users to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional travel time when using routes around the construction area.

The authority said the existing traffic arrangements would remain in force throughout the extended closure period.

World.title: Kenya: Court of Appeal Upholds Affordable Housing Levy Law
World.content:
Nairobi — The Court of Appeal has dismissed two appeals challenging the legality of the Affordable Housing Act, 2024 and the Affordable Housing Levy.

A five-judge bench upheld the High Court decision of October 22, 2024, which dismissed petitions challenging the constitutionality of the law.

The appellants had argued that the Act violated constitutional provisions on property rights, devolution, public participation, taxation and the right to adequate housing.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

They also challenged the appointment of the Kenya Revenue Authority Commissioner-General as the collector of the Affordable Housing Levy.

In a judgment delivered on Friday, September 25, the Court of Appeal found no merit in the appeals and upheld the legal framework establishing the Affordable Housing Levy and the Affordable Housing Fund.

"Having considered the submissions made, we find no merit in this appeal, which we hereby dismiss," the judges said, adding that there would be no order on costs because of the public interest nature of the case.

The court also upheld the role of the KRA Commissioner-General as the collector of the levy, saying the law expressly designates the office for that purpose.

The judges further found that there was sufficient public participation during the enactment of the Act.

The court, however, found that the Commission on Revenue Allocation (CRA) should have been given an opportunity to consider the Bill and make recommendations before it was debated and passed by Parliament.

It said Article 205 of the Constitution requires the CRA's input to be sought before a Bill is discussed in Parliament, rather than during implementation.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said on Sunday that living public officials should not have buildings named after them and proposed a rule to prohibit such renaming efforts.

This comes as President Donald Trump continues to push to rename the Kennedy Center after himself. The president has also sought to rename other prominent federal buildings in Washington, D.C., after himself since returning to the White House last year.

Kennedy said public officials, including Trump, should not "spend public money on private ads for themselves."

"The White House sees it differently, but … you can’t spend public money to … promote yourself," Kennedy told host Margaret Brennan during an appearance on CBS News' "Face the Nation."

KENNEDY CENTER CEILING PARTIALLY COLLAPSES AS TRUMP-LED BOARD PUSHES FOR 2-YEAR CLOSURE

Kennedy's comments came as a new ad promoting Trump appeared on multiple networks, that was funded by the federal government.

The senator then suggested public officials should be barred from having a building named after them while they are still alive.

"I may end up with a sombrero on my head, but I also think we ought to have a rule that no politician can have a building named after him when he’s alive," he said, referring to Trump mocking Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., last year by sharing AI videos of the lawmakers wearing sombreros.

FEDERAL JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP'S NAME REMOVED FROM KENNEDY CENTER, SAYS ONLY CONGRESS CAN RENAME IT

Trump has attempted to rename multiple buildings after himself since returning to the Oval Office, including the Kennedy Center, although federal judges blocked multiple attempts by the center's board — handpicked by Trump — to add the president’s name to the building.

Trump's name was briefly added to the building's facade but was ordered removed after courts ruled that only Congress holds the authority to change the center's name.

The State Department also added Trump’s name last year to the U.S. Institute of Peace, but former institute officials removed by the Trump administration filed a court motion earlier this month to block construction crews from putting the president’s name onto the outside of the building.

Trump also suggested he wanted New York's Penn Station and the D.C. area's Dulles Airport named after him as a condition for a funding deal earlier this year.

The president has additionally floated a project to construct a promenade connecting the back of the Lincoln Memorial to the Potomac River, saying that allies wanted to call it the "Trump Promenade."

World.title: Houston Astros secure the most embarrassing kind of Major League Baseball history with AL West win
World.content:
When Major League Baseball changed the schedule to ensure that the final day of the regular season featured all 15 games starting within a few minutes of each other, Sunday is what they envisioned. Mostly.

While most postseason spots and seeds were decided either within the last week or the last few days, there were two races that came down to the final day of the year. The American League West race featured the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers entering the day tied at 80-81, remarkably, and the third wild card spot in the National League between the Philadelphia Phillies and Arizona Diamondbacks.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The Phillies, who as recently as last week had a 99.1% chance of reaching the postseason, per FanGraphs, avoided a historic collapse and clinched a wild card series appearance with a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays.

WITH ONE MONTH LEFT, AMERICAN LEAGUE TEAMS ARE HEADING TOWARDS AN EMBARRASSING, HISTORIC LOW

But the Astros, even with a win, did in fact make an embarrassing type of history: they are officially the worst division-winning team in baseball history.

The previous low-water mark was the 2005 San Diego Padres, who won the NL West with an 82-80 record. And while the Astros won 9-0 over the long-eliminated Athletics to avoid the 80-82 record, 81–81 marks a new low winning percentage for a division winner over a full season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Even crazier? The Astros were extremely fortunate to finish the season at .500.

While wins and losses are what decide the standings and outcomes, run differential has proven over time to be a significantly better predictor of future win and loss records than the previous standings. Essentially, the better you are at outscoring the opposition, the more likely it is that you'll win more games moving forward. One-run outcomes are not sustainable, but blowouts are illustrative of team quality.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Run differentials are also used to build "expected" records. Meaning that in the history of baseball, a specific run differential is expected to result in a given number of wins and losses. The Miami Marlins, for example, outscored the opposition by just three runs over the course of the season, which is an "expected" record of 81-81. Makes sense, they were even with the other teams in the league, they should finish at an even .500.



By contrast, the Milwaukee Brewers finished with a league-best +214 run differential, good for an "expected" record of 103-59. They finished 103-59.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

But teams frequently over perform or underperform against their expected win-loss record, for any number of reasons. A bad bullpen could mean a team wins blowouts, but loses more than their fair share of close games. Bad luck. Poorly timed injuries. Poor defense. Inconsistent hitting with runners in scoring position. The randomness of baseball. Or a dominant closer who shuts the door consistently in close games.

This year's 81-81 division winning Astros team was so bad they were outscored 32 runs over the course of the season, good for just an 78-84 expected win-loss record. While the Rangers and their fans are sure to be disappointed with the outcome, missing out on the final day, they were even worse. Texas had a -46 run differential, and a 76-86 expected record.

These are not good baseball teams.

So it's a near-certainty that Houston will make a quick postseason exit, right?

Yeah, no, not at all. Houston plays the Chicago White Sox in the best-of-three wild card series, which the Astros now host as division winners. Chicago's a better team, but the randomness inherent in the small sample size of a playoff series makes the result effectively a toss up. In fact, FanGraphs gives the Astros a 55% chance of advancing to the ALDS.

Should Houston win that series, they'd play the extremely mediocre Cleveland Guardians, who finished with a +11 run differential and 85-77 record. Cleveland may be slight favorites in that series, maybe 57-43, but hardly a foregone conclusion. Which means we could be staring down the barrel of an 81-81 team reaching the ALCS.

MLB always hoped for last-minute drama by starting every game around the same time on the final day of the regular season. They got it.

They also got the worst-ever division winning team because the league's financial incentives and playoff structure encourage owners to do the bare minimum and spend as little as possible to win 85 games and hope for the best. Or in Houston's case, 81. The Astros benefited, and fans were forced to watch the AL West "battle" lost.

World.title: Foiled terror plot at bomber base signals wider threat to US military installations: expert

Five men arrested near a key U.S. bomber base in the U.K. on Sunday may have planned a "complex," coordinated attack with potentially far-reaching security implications for American military installations globally, a former U.S. intelligence official warned.

As counterterrorism police investigated after officers detained the suspects near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, a former Pentagon official also said President Donald Trump will ultimately be the one to decide the consequences if indeed the "trail leads to Tehran."

The men were initially held on suspicion of offenses under Britain’s Explosives Act before being arrested on terrorism charges in connection with the airfield, a key U.S. Air Force hub and the primary European base for American strategic bombers.

On Sunday, Trump said U.S. authorities had been monitoring the suspects prior to their capture.

FORMER UK PRIME MINISTER TONY BLAIR WARNS EUROPE ‘WE DON’T WIN’ IN WAR WITHOUT US SUPPORT

"We had them under investigation," Trump told reporters in Chicago. "They were looking to do big damage to our fort."

"It may have been Scotland Yard. I don't know. We worked with a lot of them. We had them under view for a long time, and we got them," Trump added.

According to Sky News, counterterrorism police were investigating whether Iran is linked to the suspected bomb plot.

Former Trump White House official Morgan Murphy told Fox News Digital that British authorities are leading the investigation alongside U.S. law enforcement and intelligence.

"Every phone, bank record and rental receipt will be run through British and American intelligence, and if the trail leads to Tehran, it will be found," Murphy clarified.

"But as American airmen and bombers seem to have been the target, Air Force investigators on the base, the FBI in London, and American intelligence will likely all work the case."

"If conclusive evidence proves Iran is behind an attempted attack on U.S. forces, the American President will ultimately decide how Tehran pays," Murphy added.

BRITAIN INTRODUCES SWEEPING NEW POWERS TO TARGET FOREIGN STATE-LINKED GROUPS INCLUDING IRAN'S IRGC

Former Defense Intelligence Agency official Andrew Badger told Fox News Digital the number of suspects and vehicles involved raised the possibility of a sophisticated operation.

"We are going to see elevated security protocols across Europe, across the U.K., and across the entire world for any U.S. installation," he said.

"This is a very significant threat, and again, seeing that we had five individuals involved and three different reported vans at the scene, this could have been a very complex, highly orchestrated operation," Badger added.

"This isn't just some type of amateur lone wolf operation," he said, noting Fairford’s strategic importance to the U.S. military. "Fairford is also where the U.S. houses its strategic bombers for Europe as well as the rest of the world."

He said a potential attack posed broader risks beyond the airfield itself which he said "could have had significant security implications. It could have damaged the nearby area."

HOW IRAN ATTACKS ARE FORCING THE PENTAGON TO RETHINK ITS DECADES-OLD MIDDLE EAST BASE STRATEGY

"They could have tried to use a VBIED or a vehicle-borne explosive device where the first van could have gone off at the front gate, and then the other vans would have gone in and tried to go for the strategic bombers," Badger said.

British authorities have not publicly identified who they believe was behind the suspected plot or announced a motive, but RAF Fairford had taken on greater strategic importance during the war with Iran.

The U.K. government previously authorized U.S. forces to use the Royal Air Force bases Fairford and Diego Garcia for limited defensive operations, including destroying Iranian missiles and launchers at their source.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) later warned that any base used to attack Iranian territory would be considered a legitimate target.

"Any base used to launch attacks on Iranian territory is a legitimate target for our forces," the IRGC said, according to reports.

"Tehran warned London in July to keep American bombers off Fairford, and if this plot traces back to Iran, the answer must be more bombers, not fewer," Morgan said.

IRAN EXPERT BRANDS ISLAMIC CENTER OF ENGLAND IRAN'S 'UK OFFICE,' URGES IMMEDIATE CLOSURE

A local councilor told Reuters there had been a recent security alert at Fairford and surveillance had been stepped up.

"So there was a specific threat about six weeks ago from the Iranians on this base. At the time, there was increased surveillance around the area," he told the outlet.

Badger, however, cautioned against assuming Iran was responsible while pointing to other potential threats.

"This could be Iran trying to gain strategic leverage in negotiations, but there are other actors as well," Badger added.

"But there's Russia, who's been launching a campaign of gray zone or hybrid warfare attacks across Europe, as well as Islamic extremists, which are still a significant threat here in the U.K."

"Was this some type of retaliation by Iran to perhaps try to gain leverage or to try to inflict a cost for the U.S. withdrawing from these negotiations? Again, we don't know for sure, but it is a possibility," Badger said.

Badger also pointed to RAF Welford, a major U.S. ammunition storage facility that primarily supports operations at RAF Fairford.

US EMBASSIES IN MIDDLE EAST WARN AMERICANS OF 'UNFORESEEN ESCALATION' AS LATEST STRIKES HIT IRAN

"RAF Welford is actually the second-largest weapons and ammunition depot in all of Europe," Badger said, noting that the facility where the U.S. stores ammunition "could have been a target as well."

"Other bases across Europe, including European and U.S. partners, have already been on a heightened state of alert," Badger continued.

"But of course, after this attack, I think they're going to be in an even more heightened state. You're going to have more frequent security patrols."

"There are reports that RAF Fairford was put onto what's called the Delta alert, which is the highest state of security alert within the military base system," Badger said.

"So this is basically that 'an imminent terrorist attack is inbound,'" he concluded.

World.title: ‘Storm fatigue’: Hawaiians reeling from back-to-back hurricanes as Nolo’s threats diminish
World.content:
HILO, Hawaii — Hawaiians have storm fatigue, Hilo’s mayor said Sunday, as the third hurricane to approach the islands in recent weeks continues to spin offshore.

The relatively calm state has been battered by the effects of multiple hurricanes, including Lala, Lowell and now Nolo, as the eastern and central Pacific have churned out at least 19 named storms. None of the three hurricanes has made landfall in Hawaii.

“So there’s storm fatigue and there’s some PTSD,” Mayor Kimo Alameda told NBC News on Sunday.

“I mean, you know, there’s a lot of anxiety around the weather now. You know, a lot of our folks out in the south side, they experienced, you know, catastrophic flooding,” he said, referring to the impacts of Hurricane Lala last month.

That storm killed two people, Alameda said, and damaged more than 200 homes without making landfall. Gov. Josh Green subsequently issued three disaster proclamations related to damage from separate storms in September alone.

Officials have reported some rescues but no deaths or major damage from Nolo.

“We did take some hits in some parts of the island,” Alameda said. “For the most part, we dodged a huge bullet. It could have been much worse.”

More than 120 National Guard members were activated on the island for Nolo, among roughly 400 statewide, after Green issued an emergency proclamation. President Donald Trump recently approved an emergency declaration, authorizing the Federal Emergency Management Agency to coordinate assistance and provide funding support.

In Nāʻālehu, at the island’s southern point, Peggy McKibbin surveyed silt-covered roads from her four-wheeler Sunday and pointed out the lingering damage from Lala — a bakery, a fire station and a hardware store wiped out.

“Everyone has been very much affected by this,” McKibbin said.

Nolo was a Category 4 major hurricane Sunday afternoon and forecast to strengthen, but the center was expected to remain south and southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.

A hurricane watch was in effect for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, which the storm was expected to approach Tuesday, according to the National Hurricane Center.

The Pacific has been unusually active this season, according to National Weather Service lead forecaster Bob Oravec, with storm activity running above average during what is already the peak of hurricane season. He said the pattern is consistent with El Niño years, when the Pacific often gets more tropical storms and hurricanes.

Alameda, Hilo’s mayor, said people are ready if another hurricane comes their way.

“Unfortunately, we’ve been having a lot of practice,” he said, noting a recent tsunami threat and earthquake, as well as a precautionary eye on the volcano Kīlauea.

Mexican navy personnel fill sandbags in Lazaro Cardenas last week. Enrique Castro / AFP via Getty Images

Mexico’s Baja Peninsula, meanwhile, was bracing for the arrival of major Hurricane Polo on Monday after it lashed parts of the country’s southwest coast with rain and strong winds. Polo remained a dangerous Category 3 storm with top sustained winds of 125 mph, the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami said Sunday afternoon.

Polo was moving to the north-northwest at 12 mph about 285 miles west-southwest of Cabo San Lucas at the peninsula’s southern tip, according to the hurricane center.

The Mexican navy said in a statement that it had gathered personnel and humanitarian aid in the ports of Guaymas and Mazatlán, on the Pacific Coast, and deployed three vessels that could ship aid to coastal communities isolated by the hurricane.

Also Sunday, Tropical Storm Rachel formed off Mexico’s southwest coast. Rachel had maximum sustained winds of 40 mph and was about 275 miles south of Acapulco. A tropical storm watch was in effect.

Ryan Chandler, Shanshan Dong and The Associated Press reported from Hilo and Dennis Romero from San Diego.
