World.title: Acampada en Sol por la vivienda, en directo | El Gobierno reconoce que va a ser “un lunes muy largo” de negociaciones para sacar adelante el decreto
World.content:
Irene Montero: “Las casas son para vivir y hay una fuerza social suficiente para conseguirlo”

La eurodiputada de Podemos Irene Montero afirma que “lo que hay que hacer” es prohibir la venta de viviendas para especular, los desahucios sin alternativa habitacional, expropiar las viviendas a los fondos buitre y bajar el precio de los alquileres, según ha indicado en una entrevista en TVE donde ha celebrado la “fuerza social que está empujando para que se acabe esta gravísima crisis de vivienda que está impidiendo a la gente vivir con dignidad”. “Las casas con para vivir y hay una fuerza social suficiente para conseguirlo”, ha apuntado Montero, que se ha referido a la acampada de la Puerta del Sol como “la imagen de la mejor España”: “Esos momentos en los que la gente recuerda el aprendizaje más importante de cualquier ser humano, que es que, si las cosas son injustas, hay que organizarse y luchar juntas para cambiarlas”.

“Diga lo que diga la negociación de partidos, este es un momento en el que la negociación está desbordada”, ha dicho la eurodiputada de Podemos, que ha señalado que la fuerza social que estos días se ha manifestado en diferentes ciudades de España “no cabe en un real decreto ni en una negociación partidista”. En este sentido, y preguntada por un acuerdo de mínimos que ponga de acuerdo a las diferentes fuerzas políticas, Montero ha afirmado que “las cosas no están para mínimos, sino para arreglar el problema, no para poner un parche”. “El Gobierno está negociando primero con Junts y con el PNV para generar el relato de que no dan los números y hacerle un trágala a la gente que está en la calle y decir, 'bueno, es que no se podía hacer otra cosa'. Pues a lo mejor esta vez el trágala hay que hacérselo a los especuladores y a lo mejor esta vez el trágala lo tienen que tener aquellos partidos que están representando los intereses de los rentistas y especuladores, porque esta situación ya no da más de sí”, ha expresado antes de afirmar que la “posición de Podemos es la de la gente, la de la mayoría social que quiere que se acabe el negocio de la vivienda”.

World.title: Ciberseguridad: el socio que toda pyme debe tener
World.content:
Las pequeñas y medianas empresas están expuestas a ataques cada vez más sofisticados con los que los ciberdelincuentes acceden a los sistemas para robar datos y dinero. Pero se puede reducir el impacto de muchos de estos incidentes o directamente evitarse si la empresa está preparada y los empleados saben cómo actuar

La era digital permite a las pequeñas y medianas empresas desempeñarse con una agilidad nunca vista y ser más eficientes y productivas. Un mundo de ventajas en el que también se cuelan los ciberdelincuentes. Ya no hay que forzar una cerradura de madrugada para entrar en un negocio; basta con enviar un SMS o hacer una llamada y que el empresario o el empleado confiado haga clic donde no debía para que los ladrones accedan al corazón informático de la empresa.

Las pymes también son objetivo de los ciberdelincuentes, asegura Alfredo Díez, coordinador del grupo de trabajo de ciberseguridad de la Confederación Española de Organizaciones Empresariales (CEOE). Y resultan, en muchos casos, más vulnerables que las grandes compañías: suelen carecer de personal especializado y trabajan con menos recursos. “Incluso en el caso de las microempresas y los autónomos, en ocasiones, el propio empresario tiene un único dispositivo para uso personal y profesional, lo que aumenta el riesgo”, advierte el experto.

Díez considera que es especialmente importante que este colectivo, el mayor del tejido empresarial español (el 99,8%), preste atención a la ciberseguridad para la supervivencia de su negocio y que, sobre todo, invierta en ello y dedique una partida de sus presupuestos a blindarlo digitalmente. Especialmente, continúa Díez, en este momento en el que la inteligencia artificial (IA) multiplica la efectividad de los ataques. “Hasta ahora, la mayoría de los ataques podían ser masivos e indiscriminados, pero ahora se crean estafas a medida para cada empresa o para cada empleado con mucha más facilidad. La IA permite personalizar y escalar ataques dirigidos que antes requerían mucho más tiempo y trabajo”, advierte el coordinador de CEOE.

La inteligencia artificial (IA) permite a los atacantes crear esos mensajes más personalizados y creíbles, que imitan el tono profesional de cada sector y eliminan señales que antes los delataban, como las faltas de ortografía o una personalización defectuosa. Incluso pueden traducir sus comunicaciones a varios idiomas, o suplantar mediante voz e imagen a algún miembro de la empresa para llevar a cabo su estafa. La IA también les da la posibilidad de recabar información de sus objetivos con mayor rapidez, como conocer la situación por la que pasa y adaptar su ataque.

Una empresa ciberresiliente

Las pymes que priorizan la ciberseguridad cuentan con una ventaja respecto a las demás. El daño económico es una de las principales consecuencias de un ataque, pero no es la única. A él se puede sumar la pérdida de reputación y de confianza por parte de los clientes, cuyos datos, en ocasiones, también se ven expuestos. Recuperar el prestigio suele requerir tiempo y esfuerzo. Hoy, las grandes empresas tienen en cuenta la seguridad a la hora de elegir proveedores en su cadena de suministro, por eso, la defensa digital no es solo protección, también es un factor de competitividad. Una pyme fiable es más sólida y presenta más garantías a la hora de contar con sus servicios.

En este contenido repasamos los principales ataques a los que hoy están expuestas este tipo de compañías y qué pueden hacer empresarios y trabajadores para no caer en ellos, porque hoy, señala Jesús Cristóbal, profesor de IA y análisis de datos de OBS Business School, la cuestión no es asumir que nunca ocurrirá, sino estar preparados si ocurre.

Cuando el ataque empieza con un mensaje, el ‘phishing’

La suplantación de identidad es una de las amenazas más habituales para las pymes. Puede llegar por correo electrónico, SMS, llamada o incluso videollamada, haciéndose pasar por un banco, un proveedor, un cliente o un miembro de la propia empresa. El phishing, especialmente a través del correo electrónico, sigue siendo una de las vías más utilizadas. Los ciberdelincuentes imitan comunicaciones legítimas y recurren a pretextos como una incidencia con la cuenta bancaria, el acceso al correo o los servicios en la nube para provocar una reacción rápida. El objetivo suele ser que la víctima haga clic en un enlace, facilite sus credenciales o abra la puerta a un acceso no autorizado.

El fraude guiado que utiliza varios métodos de comunicación para convencer a la víctima es cada vez más común precisamente por su efectividad. Los estafadores envían un mensaje en el que avisan de un problema que se debe solucionar llamando a un número de teléfono que indican. A partir de ahí guían a la víctima para conseguir sus propósitos.

Ejemplo de correo fraudulento Fuente: Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (Incibe)

En algunos casos, el phishing también se utiliza para instalar programas maliciosos (malware) en los equipos o sistemas de la víctima. Su propósito es infiltrarse con fines fraudulentos: robar información, espiar la actividad del usuario y la empresa o dañar los equipos para aprovechar sus vulnerabilidades. En un ataque de ransomware, los delincuentes pueden cifrar los sistemas para impedir su uso y exigir un rescate para recuperarlos. En otros casos, además, roban información y amenazan con publicarla.

El ransomware puede tener graves consecuencias para una pyme, señala Jesús Cristóbal, profesor de análisis de datos e IA en OBS Business School. Paraliza la actividad de la empresa, puede exponer sus datos privados y generar posibles sanciones por la filtración de información de clientes. Genera pérdidas económicas y un daño reputacional del que cuesta mucho recuperarse.

Cuando la estafa se disfraza, el proveedor o el directivo falsos

Los ciberdelincuentes pueden adoptar la identidad de alguien conocido por la empresa para llegar a cabo su engaño. Se aprovechan de las redes de confianza tejidas en el entorno laboral para sustituir a proveedores y empleados. Con el propósito de preparar el ataque, llevan a cabo una labor de investigación en torno a la compañía. En muchas ocasiones, ya se han adentrado en su sistema en un ataque previo de phishing. El principal objetivo de esta estafa es obtener dinero o información sensible y puede presentarse de diversas formas:

Suplantación de un proveedor. Los ciberdelincuentes envían un correo electrónico en el que se hacen pasar por un proveedor habitual.Se imitan los elementos que lo identifican, como los colores, el logotipo, y manejan un lenguaje cercano, incluso familiar, para avisar deque desde ese momento en adelante los pagos deben hacerse a una nueva cuenta. Este tipo de fraude suele encuadrarse en el llamado business email compromise (BEC), en el que los atacantes manipulan o suplantan comunicaciones empresariales para desviar pagos o conseguir información sensible.

Fraude del directivo o del CEO. En esta modalidad, los atacantes envían correos electrónicos o realizan llamadas o videollamadas haciéndose pasar por un cargo con responsabilidad y capacidad de decisión, como un directivo o gerente, para pedir información confidencial, credenciales para entrar en el sistema o solicitar una transferencia urgente. Aunque puede parecer una orden legítima, el objetivo es desviar dinero o facilitar un acceso que permita cometer un fraude mayor. Esta modalidad ha incorporado recientemente la clonación de voz y la imagen generada mediante IA para hacer el engaño más creíble, gracias a la técnica del deepfake. Los ciberdelincuentes crean una imagen en movimiento del directivo que se utiliza durante una videoconferencia.

Fraude de desvío de nómina. Existe un tipo de estafa que afecta a los empleados. Los ciberdelincuentes suplantan la identidad de un trabajador para conseguir que la empresa modifique la cuenta bancaria en la que se ingresa su salario. ¿Cómo lo hacen? Envían un correo electrónico en el que solicitan el cambio de cuenta, en ocasiones, incorporando documentación falsificada. Si la empresa no verifica esa petición por otra vía, la nómina siguiente se transfiere a una cuenta controlada por los atacantes.

Las herramientas que protegen la pyme, mucha formación y ‘phishing’ ético

Cualquier empresa, por pequeña que sea, puede convertirse en objetivo de los estafadores. La diferencia está en su capacidad para detectar el engaño, impedir que una decisión equivocada se convierta en un incidente mayor y reaccionar con rapidez si finalmente ocurre. Para ello, la preparación debe combinar personas formadas, procesos de verificación y medidas de protección.

Anticipación: personas y procesos que frenan el engaño Verificar las operaciones sensibles. Los cambios de cuentas bancarias, los pagos excepcionales, los accesos a información delicada o cualquier solicitud fuera de lo habitual, deben comprobarse por una vía adicional, aunque la petición parezca legítima. La verificación no debe depender solo de la intuición de una persona. Formar a los empleados. La concienciación es una de las primeras líneas de defensa. Los trabajadores deben conocer las señales de una posible comunicación fraudulenta y saber cómo actuar ante ellas. Conviene partir de hábitos sencillos, como revisar el remitente, comprobar los enlaces y evitar abrir archivos adjuntos inesperados o sospechosos. Reconocer las señales de manipulación. Hay determinados indicios que deberían activar una alerta: Una urgencia que no es habitual

Una petición de confidencialidad

Un tono distinto al esperado

Presión para saltarse verificaciones

Instrucciones para completar una operación fuera de los canales habituales Entrenar a los equipos con phishing ético. Estas simulaciones reproducen intentos de phishing en un entorno controlado para comprobar cómo reaccionan los empleados e identificar áreas de mejora. Los resultados permiten orientar la formación hacia los comportamientos que presentan mayor riesgo y reforzar progresivamente la capacidad de respuesta de la organización. Reducir el impacto si algo falla Limitar los accesos. Cada empleado debe disponer únicamente de los permisos necesarios para hacer su trabajo. Así, si una cuenta resulta comprometida, el atacante tampoco obtiene acceso automático a toda la empresa. Activar la autenticación multifactor. Añadir una segunda prueba de identidad al entrar en el correo, la banca online o las aplicaciones de gestión dificulta el acceso incluso cuando las credenciales han sido robadas. Realizar copias de seguridad periódicas. Las copias de seguridad permiten recuperar información tras un ransomware u otro incidente, siempre que estén actualizadas y se mantengan separadas del sistema principal. Si el incidente ocurre: responder y seguir funcionando Actuar rápido y comunicarlo internamente. Si un empleado ha pulsado un enlace fraudulento, ha facilitado credenciales o detecta una actividad sospechosa, debe comunicarlo cuanto antes al responsable correspondiente. Comunicar un error cuanto antes ayuda a contener el incidente y reducir su impacto. Activar un plan de continuidad. La empresa debe tener previsto cómo mantener las funciones críticas mientras se contiene el ataque y se recuperan los sistemas. Esto implica saber qué operaciones son imprescindibles, cómo pueden seguir funcionando y cómo mantener informados a empleados, clientes y proveedores cuando sea necesario. Denunciar y pedir ayuda. Ante un incidente, la empresa puede solicitar asesoramiento especializado y, cuando corresponda, denunciarlo ante las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad del Estado. Incibe ofrece apoyo a empresas en la gestión de incidentes de ciberseguridad. No pagar el rescate. Incibe desaconseja pagar en caso de ransomware: no existe garantía de recuperar la información, se financia a los ciberdelincuentes y se puede aumentar el riesgo de nuevos ataques. Contar con apoyo externo especializado. Las pymes pueden apoyarse en proveedores y servicios de ciberseguridad adaptados a su tamaño y presupuesto, con capacidades de monitorización, protección, gestión de accesos, respuesta ante incidentes y formación.

Prepararse frente a estas amenazas no consiste en esperar que nadie se equivoque nunca. Consiste en construir una empresa capaz de poner barreras cuando alguien se equivoca, limitar el impacto de un incidente y seguir operando si ocurre. Y esa preparación ya no afecta solo a la propia compañía. Una empresa forma parte de las cadenas de suministro, comparte datos, sistemas y procesos con clientes y proveedores. Su nivel de seguridad también puede convertirse en riesgo, o en confianza, para quienes trabajan con ella.

World.title: Porto Ercole, el pueblo de Italia donde la ‘dolce vita’ sigue mirando al mar
World.content:
Entre barcos de madera, terrazas frente al puerto y hoteles que forman parte de la historia del Mediterráneo y de la visión del fotógrafo Slim Aarons, en este enclave al sur de la Toscana la vida cotidiana sigue marcando el ritmo

Cuando llega la última hora de la tarde, la italiana Porto Ercole recupera su mejor versión. Los barcos regresan al puerto, las terrazas se llenan lentamente y la luz suaviza las fachadas de color ocre que trepan por la colina. Una Vespa atraviesa el paseo. Alguien recoge la ropa del balcón. Los camareros se mueven entre las mesas cuando llega la hora del aperitivo. En realidad nada parece extraordinario, y ahí está parte del encanto de este enclave en la costa del Argentario. La escena podría repetirse hoy o dentro de una década.

Este es uno de los lugares a los que la gente regresa. Las familias romanas que llevan generaciones pasando los veranos aquí. Los navegantes que conocen cada cala y quienes buscan un Mediterráneo que conserva su ritmo. Argentario no se parece demasiado a la Toscana que se suele imaginar. En vez de los campos infinitos de cipreses, aquí aparecen pinares que descienden hacia el mar y acantilados esculpidos por el viento.

Una callejuela en el casco antiguo de Porto Ercole. Atlantide Phototravel / GETTY IMAGES

Apenas a una hora y media en coche desde el aeropuerto de Roma (o en tren hasta Orbetello-Monte Argentario, a 10 kilómetros del pueblo), y a poco más de dos horas desde Pisa, los casi 3.000 vecinos de Porto Ercole han conseguido preservar algo cada vez más difícil de encontrar en el Mediterráneo: la sensación de estar en un lugar donde la vida cotidiana parece seguir marcando el ritmo.

Antes de que llegara Instagram, el fotógrafo estadounidense Slim Aarons (1916-2006) convirtió esta costa en uno de sus escenarios favoritos. Sus fotografías ayudaron a construir el imaginario de la dolce vita, retratando comidas interminables, barcos de madera, piscinas frente al mar y una elegancia que parecía surgir sin esfuerzo. Por delante de su cámara pasaron Gianni Agnelli, Lee Radziwill, los Getty o la familia Missoni… y muchas de aquellas escenas inmortalizadas siguen pareciendo posibles.

El encantador pueblo de Porto Ercole se encuentra en la costa del Argentario. Roberto Nencini ( GETTY IMAGES )

Las mañanas transcurren despacio en Porto Ercole; hay quienes comienzan el día con un expresso mirando al mar y los que prefieren perderse por las calles que rodean el puerto, donde se suceden pequeñas boutiques. Fue en una de esas tiendas donde empecé a entender mejor el pueblo. Había llegado la noche anterior y, después de descubrir que durante las noches aquí a veces corre un poco de fresco (aunque durante el verano son muy calientes, con temperaturas que suelen rondar los 30 grados de día y 25 grados de noche o más), entré en Ester Gi en busca de una capa ligera. Mientras me la probaba, Ornella, la encargada, empezó a hablar de Porto Ercole como solo hablan los italianos de los lugares que quieren. La Sirena para cenar pescado. O la Hosteria Alicina. O Il Gambero Rosso. Una recomendación llevaba a la siguiente y, antes de darme cuenta, ya no hablábamos de restaurantes, sino del pueblo. Ornella lo conoce bien, porque durante 14 años trabajó en la boutique del Hotel Il Pellicano y ha visto pasar generaciones de familias que repiten cada temporada. “Es como una pequeña joya”, dice al hablar del pueblo. “La gente vuelve porque aquí se sienten como en casa”.

Escuchándola, es fácil entender por qué, tarde o temprano, cualquier conversación sobre Porto Ercole acaba desembocando en el hotel Il Pellicano. “En realidad, toda su historia es una historia de amor”, explica. Y es difícil encontrar una mejor prueba de ello. Patricia Daszel, una socialité estadounidense, quedó fascinada por el piloto británico de guerra Michael Graham después de verlo fotografiado en un periódico como superviviente de un accidente aéreo. Años después se conocieron en Pelican Point, en California, se enamoraron y encontraron en unos terrenos de la familia Borghese, suspendidos sobre una cala de aguas cristalinas de Argentario, el lugar perfecto para construir una casa e invitar a sus amigos. Aquella residencia acabaría convirtiéndose en el hotel, que inauguraron en 1965.

Vista aérea del hotel Il Pellicano, en Porto Ercole. Pellicano Hotels

Ahora, 60 años después, Il Pellicano parece haber conservado una manera de entender el verano. Una buena parte de las fotografías más conocidas de Slim Aarons se tomaron aquí. El embarcadero, las plataformas junto al mar y las icónicas toallas de rayas amarillas y blancas siguen formando parte del paisaje. También la forma de vivirlo: un baño antes de comer, una sobremesa que se alarga y, al caer la tarde, el Bar Roberto, donde Federico Morosi lleva 18 años detrás de la barra.

La familia Sciò ha sido clave para conservar el carácter del alojamiento. Roberto Sciò llegó primero como huésped, se enamoró del lugar y lo hizo suyo en 1979. Desde entonces, el hotel ha mantenido esa combinación de elegancia relajada y discreción, hoy bajo la dirección de su hija Marie-Louise, y que también se percibe en La Posta Vecchia, la histórica propiedad familiar cerca de Roma.

Terraza junto al Mediterráneo de Il Pellicano. Pellicano Hotels

El espíritu de Il Pelicano también se percibe fuera del hotel. Ornella me insistió varias veces en que pasara por Medusa a la hora del aperitivo, un pequeño local abierto por Stefano y Alin, dos antiguos miembros del equipo que decidieron emprender su propio proyecto. Pedí una bruschetta de tomate y mozzarella mientras observaba la escena. Solo se escuchaba hablar italiano y sentí nostalgia de ese Mediterráneo de antes, con más veraneantes que turistas.

Cuando le pregunté a Ornella qué explicaba mejor Porto Ercole, no mencionó los hoteles ni los famosos. Habló de quienes crecieron veraneando aquí y siguen regresando cada año. Aunque esa fidelidad de la que hablaba no ha impedido que el pueblo empiece a escribir un nuevo capítulo. LA ROQQA es probablemente el mejor ejemplo. Inaugurado en 2023, hacía años que la apertura de un hotel no generaba tanta conversación en el pueblo. Mientras que Il Pellicano está más escondido sobre el acantilado, aquí el hotel forma parte de la vida cotidiana. Al cruzar la puerta, una puede mezclarse con las calles del centro o improvisar un aperitivo antes de regresar. Desde la entrada, donde suele descansar un pequeño Fiat descapotable que parece sacado de una fotografía de los años sesenta, LA ROQQA deja clara su personalidad. El interiorismo combina referencias retro, diseño contemporáneo y una paleta inspirada en los colores del puerto.

La mejor hora para subir a su rooftop Scirocco quizá no sea la cena, sino ese momento previo en el que el sol empieza a caer sobre Porto Ercole y el puerto cambia de color. La barra rinde homenaje a Caravaggio, con creaciones inspiradas en algunas de sus obras más célebres y reinterpretaciones del clásico Negroni. En la cocina también manda el producto local. Pescados del Tirreno, pasta fresca preparada a mano, verduras de temporada y vinos de la Toscana dan forma a la carta. Uno de los platos preferidos de la casa es su spaghetto otto pomodori, preparado con distintas variedades de tomate cultivadas en los alrededores de Porto Ercole.

La terraza Scirocco del hotel LA ROQQA, en Porto Ercole.

Explorando los alrededores

Quienes tienen algunos días más encuentran motivos de sobra para seguir explorando Argentario. A pocos minutos a pie desde Porto Ercole está la cala Le Viste. Hacia el norte, La Feniglia es una playa de arena bordeada por un pinar protegido perfecta para pasar la mañana, mientras que Spiaggia Lunga es más tranquila y salvaje.

Vista de la playa de La Feniglia. Andrea Pistolesi ( GETTY IMAGES )

La historia aparece donde menos se la espera. En Forte Filippo, fortaleza que los españoles levantaron en el siglo XVI para proteger la ruta marítima entre sus territorios italianos, y que sigue dominando la bahía a lo alto de las colinas. O en el último viaje de Caravaggio, que pasó aquí sus últimos días y murió en 1610 mientras intentaba regresar a Roma. A pocos kilómetros, Porto Santo Stefano es el punto de partida de los ferris hacia las islas de Giglio y Giannutri. Están integradas en el parque nacional del Archipiélago Toscano, el mayor parque marino protegido de Europa.

Porto Ercole conserva algo que resulta cada vez más difícil de encontrar, porque aquí las tardes siguen midiendo el tiempo en baños, aperitivos y conversaciones que se alargan sin mirar el reloj. Quizá por eso la dolce vita, más que una promesa, sigue pareciendo una forma de vivir.

World.title: Odemira, una ruta por el concejo del Alentejo más salvaje
World.content:
Cerca de 50 kilómetros de costa, pueblos blancos y arenales vírgenes desfilan por el concejo más extenso de Portugal, una tierra marcada por la fuerza creativa y donde el interior rural choca con el océano

Es muy común encontrar al escalabardo por el Alentejo, irrumpiendo de pronto en los caminos o cruzando temerario la carretera. El escalabardo, conocido también como meloncillo, es un mamífero pequeño y alargado, de pelaje pardo y cabeza afilada, similar a un hurón o una comadreja. Un icónico animalito que, por su conexión con esta tierra portuguesa, también da nombre a una interesante iniciativa ambiental, social y comunitaria desarrollada en la localidad de São Luís. “Damos un nuevo uso a la ropa que se deshecha para que, en lugar de acabar en la basura, pueda reutilizarse de manera creativa”, explica Ana Baleia desde su sede en esta freguesia de la región de Odemira, trazada con casas blancas y calles empedradas.

La creatividad es, de hecho, la enseña que enarbola este concejo, el más extenso de Portugal, erigido en un importante foco de inspiración al que acuden numerosos artistas y creadores para desarrollar su talento. Odemira, parte del parque natural del Suroeste Alentejano y Costa Vicentina, está considerado uno de los rincones más salvajes del litoral portugués. Aquí, donde el interior rural se da de bruces con el océano, se concentra la naturaleza más pura. “Puede que sea la diversidad (el mar, el río, la llanura, la sierra) pero lo cierto es que todo en esta zona estimula la creación artística”, apunta Baleia, a propósito de tradiciones tan arraigadas como la cerámica, el mimbre o el trabajo en telares, que conviven con otras disciplinas más contemporáneas.

Más información Recorriendo Esposende, un museo moderno al aire libre único en Portugal

Los secretos del océano

A juicio de los artesanos, es la belleza del entorno la que mantiene vivas las costumbres en un rincón marcado por la presencia del agua. Considerado uno de los ríos más limpios de Europa, el Mira atraviesa la región del Alentejo con la peculiaridad de fluir de sur a norte y el privilegio de dejar a su paso todo un despliegue de paisajes vírgenes. Recorrer Odemira es descubrir llanuras doradas por el sol, colinas ondulantes y campos alfombrados de viñedos hasta donde alcanza la vista. Estampas que chocan de pronto con una costa escarpada que da lugar a acantilados, dunas y calas solitarias.

Cigüeñas blancas anidan en los salientes de los acantilados marinos, en cabo Sardão. Cristina Candel

Nada como aventurarse por este litoral embravecido para dar con playas tan espectaculares como Almograve, encajada entre oscuras formaciones rocosas, o Carvalhal, donde el oleaje favorece la práctica de surf, o la pequeña y recogida Nossa Senhora, a la que se accede por pasarelas de madera. Pero es cerca de la playa de Cavaleiro, concretamente en el cabo Sardão, donde acontece un fenómeno sin igual: este lugar es el único punto conocido en el planeta en el que las cigüeñas blancas anidan en los salientes de los acantilados marinos, en vez de hacerlo en los árboles o los tejados. Un comportamiento especial que se puede observar muy de cerca, sobre los farallones y con el Atlántico de fondo, especialmente durante la primavera.

Villas de ambiente marinero

Más allá de la naturaleza, esta región atesora toda la magia de los pueblos alentejanos, con su peculiar arquitectura de fachadas encaladas que contrastan con los zócalos pintados en azul. Pueblos que, fuera de la temporada alta, hacen gala de un ritmo pausado y de un ambiente acogedor en el que se respira una estrecha conexión con el mar. Empezando por el propio Odemira, que da nombre al concejo, allí donde el río comienza a ser navegable hasta toparse con el océano. Esta es una población encaramada sobre una colina, cuya actividad cultural se concentra en el Café-Librería Mirabolante, que a menudo organiza tertulias, recitales y exposiciones de arte.

Vila Nova de Milfontes, en la desembocadura del Mira, con la fortaleza de São Clemente integrada entre las playas fluviales y las casas blancas del casco antiguo. Cristina Candel

Situada en la desembocadura del Mira, a Vila Nova de Milfontes se la distingue por la majestuosa silueta de la fortaleza de São Clemente, integrada entre las playas fluviales y las casas blancas del casco antiguo. Un castillo que fue levantado para contener el ataque de los piratas que asolaron este tramo de costa, ya por entonces ribeteado de playas dunares y recoletas calas salvajes. Hoy, para descubrirlas a pie, a caballo o en bicicleta, existe toda una red de senderos que atraviesan esta localidad que, al no ser ni villa, ni nueva, ni disponer de mil fuentes, comparte con la cántabra Santillana del Mar el sambenito de “las tres mentiras”.

Vecinos de la pequeña villa marinera de Zambujeira do Mar. Cristina Candel

Estos mismos caminos discurren por Zambujeira do Mar, una pequeña villa marinera que se posa sobre un acantilado para asomarse a uno de los arenales más impactantes del sur de Portugal. En su entramado, apenas compuesto por unas cuantas callejuelas que siempre acaban en el océano, no falta alguna fachada señorial, pequeñas muestras de arte urbano y la Capela de Nossa Senhora do Mar, la cual, por su posición sobre un promontorio con vistas a la playa y el pueblo, resulta una localización excelente para contemplar la puesta de sol.

Unas notas de ‘saudade’

Fue la calma de esta región la que logró cautivar a la reina portuguesa del fado. Cuentan que Amália Rodrigues, quien eligió como refugio vacacional al discreto pueblo de Brejão (entre Odemira y Zambujeira) para huir del bullicio de Lisboa, alumbró muchas de sus canciones mirando a ese Atlántico que irrumpía de pronto tras sortear un camino de juncos. En su honor, este mismo paraje fue rebautizado como la Praia da Amália, en el punto donde la artista acudía para guarecerse del mundo.

Mural con la imagen de Amália Rodrigues firmado por el artista urbano Ivo Santos, en Brejão. Cristina Candel

Pero también su memoria ha quedado impresa en las paredes de Brejão a través de los murales pintados por el artista urbano Ivo Santos en el verano de 2018. Cuatro retratos gigantescos de quien conjugó su voz única con hermosos versos de poetas antiguos para hacer de este género musical un desgarrado canto a la nostalgia. Con su recuerdo permanece viva la saudade de esta tierra impregnada de océano: “Ven a saber si el mar tendrá razón / Ven acá a ver bailar mi corazón”.

World.title: Hospitals block access to patients’ records after cyber threat
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Some Dutch hospitals denied patients access to their medical records over the weekend because of security issues with the online gateway Citrix.

The national cybersecurity centre NCSC advised hospitals to disconnect their Citrix applications from the internet after discovering a “critical vulnerability” that could allow hackers to operate the system remotely.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an alert on Sunday, saying it had “received reports and partner threat intelligence confirming that threat actors are actively exploiting these vulnerabilities globally”.

The Amphia Ziekenhuis in Breda, the Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis in Tilburg and the Frisius medical centre in Leeuwarden were among the Dutch hospitals that reported problems at the weekend.

Doctors were still able to look at patients’ records, but the patients themselves could not during online consultations.

The Frisius MC said on Sunday it had blocked access as a precautionary measure in response to the alerts by the NCSC and Z-Cert, the agency specialising in digital security in healthcare, but its systems were now back online.

The interior ministry said some of its civil servants had been unable to work remotely at the weekend after its Citrix applications were switched off.

It is not the first time Dutch institutions have experienced security issues with Citrix and its access program, NetScaler. Last year the public prosecution service (OM) restricted access for two months after hackers exploited a gap in its security systems.

World.title: Amsterdam top destination for young people leaving home
World.content:
Most young people leaving home in the Netherlands head to Amsterdam, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS.

More than 174,000 people aged 18 to 30 moved out of their parents’ home in 2024, and a third of them settled in Amsterdam, one of ten councils tracked by the research. The city drew 12,760, well ahead of Rotterdam and Groningen.

The city was also the most popular destination for students, attracting 5,475, followed by Utrecht and Groningen. Nijmegen had the highest share of students

among young newcomers at 53.1%, followed by Utrecht and Leiden at 49.5% each.

The Hague was the exception: 65.4% of the young people who moved there were not students.

Just under a third of those leaving home were students, and half of them (49.9%) moved into privately rented housing. The rest went into social housing or owner-occupied homes. Non-students were most likely to move into an owner-occupied home (42.6%).

The figures only cover young people registered as living with their parents in the Netherlands at the start of 2024. They exclude anyone who moved to the country from abroad that year, such as newly arrived international students.

World.title: Israel strips Dutch diplomats’ status over settlement goods ban
World.content:
Israel is revoking the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats in the West Bank city of Ramallah in the latest pushback against the Netherlands’ ban on goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in occupied territories.

In a statement on social media, Israeli foreign minister Gideon Saar said the diplomats must return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documents within seven days, after which their diplomatic privileges and immunities will expire. He said the move was intended as a response to the ban that came into force last week.

“If the Netherlands wishes to continue representing its interests with the Palestinians, it may do so from Palestinian Authority territory, rather than from the territory of the State of Israel,” he said.

Dutch foreign minister Berendsen said in response that the move was “unnecessary” and that he “deeply regrets” it, adding that the ban on settlement goods “is not directed at Israel” but rather an obligation to comply with international law.

Last month, Israel expelled two Dutch officials from the US-backed centre in Kiryat Gat that coordinates the Gaza ceasefire.

Settlement ban

The Netherlands is the main EU import hub for goods produced in settlements in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights – all of which are considered occupied under international law.

The cabinet agreed to the ban in May. It covers imports of and trade in settlement goods, and also applies to Dutch companies operating abroad.

Saar said that “Israel will not ignore measures intended to harm it. Any country that acts in a hostile and unilateral manner against Israel will lose influence and relevance in the region.”

He also spoke of “growing antisemitism and incitement openly seen on the streets of the Netherlands. Not only are this antisemitism and incitement not being seriously addressed, but the anti-Israel policies of the Dutch Government are fueling them.”

Saar did not specify what he was referring to. This spring there were four attacks on Jewish and pro-Israel targets in the Netherlands, which Dutch investigators believe were coordinated by an Iraqi man arrested in the US. Experts have said the attacks were very likely directed by Iran.

Economic ties

Despite the dispute over settlement goods, the Netherlands is the biggest destination for Israeli capital in the world, holding €44.9 billion in investment in 2024 – nearly four times as much as the US, according to research by Amsterdam-based corporate watchdog SOMO.

It is also the world’s second biggest investor into Israel, with €27.3 billion invested there in 2024 alone.

Earlier this month, more than 230 former Dutch ministers, ambassadors, diplomats and civil servants called on the cabinet to take tougher measures against Israel, including a full arms embargo and the suspension of the European Union’s trade agreement with the country.

World.title: Dutch river cruise stranded as Rhine falls to new record levels
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The river Rhine dropped to a new record low level at the weekend at the Dutch-German border, with no sign of fresh rainfall in the days ahead.

The river measured 6.1m at Lobith, the point where it flows into the Netherlands, on Sunday, below the previous record of 6.12m set in August.

Further upstream in Cologne, a Dutch cruise ship became stuck in mid-river as water levels dropped to just 40 centimetres on the gauge, leaving around 1.5 metres of navigable depth.

The Dutch Melody, which carries 140 passengers, was able to continue downriver after being assisted by another ship, German river police said. The four-deck vessel is due to arrive in Nijmegen later on Monday.

River levels are expected to drop further this week due to low rainfall in the Alps. At Lobith the flow of water has fallen below 600 cubic metres per second for the first time on record.

Dutch water authorities have had to impose restrictions on river traffic as channels became narrower and shallower during the summer drought.

Vessels using the IJssel to travel from Arnhem to Zutphen are having to take a 300km detour after Rijkswaterstaat imposed a one-way system.

Some ferries across the rivers have been cancelled and river cruises have had to cancel trips or shorten their itineraries because sections of the Rhine have become impassable.

World.title: Jetten’s D66 conference speech interrupted by Gaza hecklers
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten’s speech to his D66 party’s weekend conference was interrupted by hecklers protesting against Israel’s military intervention in Gaza.

Jetten was briefly led from the stage by security guards after demonstrators twice shouted out at the start of the speech in the Amsterdam RAI arena on Sunday.

The prime minister initially said the protesters could stay in the conference hall if they sat down “so you don’t bother those sitting behind you”, but after the second interruption a handful of demonstrators were escorted out of the hall.

The demonstrators wore T-shirts with slogans such as Bloedcoalitie (“blood coalition”) and Liberaal/Neutraal/Genocidaal (“liberal, neutral, genocidal”).

Jetten said: “I see that you want to highlight the situation in Gaza and I understand that very much.”

Afterwards he told RTL Nieuws that the protest had been respectful. “The right to demonstrate and have your say is one of the strengths of our democracy, as long as it’s done respectfully, and that’s what we saw here in the hall.”

Budget delays

The conference marked the 60th anniversary of the foundation of D66 and the first time a prime minister had addressed the autumn gathering.

Jetten said his cabinet had made progress in several areas, such as drawing up plans to cut nitrogen pollution and preventing the online government services portal DigiD being sold to an American company.

But he admitted it had taken longer than hoped for his government to make a deal with opposition parties to pass next year’s budget. The minority coalition of D66, CDA and VVD needs the support of at least two other parties in both houses of parliament.

Jetten said he had seen signs during talks last week that parties “from left to right” were prepared to negotiate, proving that “broad co-operation is possible with this generation of politicians”.

The prime minister also insisted he would not give in to the “anti-Dutch forces that want to destroy our democracy from within”, referring to the violent demonstrations in The Hague a week ago that featured “appalling extreme right-wing slogans and even Nazi salutes”.

Jetten vowed that the “wave of optimism” would ultimately triumph over the loudest voices, echoing his predecessor Mark Rutte, who called on people to vote for “doers, not yellers”.

“They might shout louder, but we get more done,” Jetten said.

World.title: Meerdink double gives Xavi first win as Oranje coach in Belgrade
World.content:
Mexx Meerdink’s first two international goals were enough for the Netherlands to edge past Serbia and earn Xavi Hernandez his first win as coach in a gritty encounter in Belgrade.

Meerdink scored from the penalty spot in the first half after Crysencio Summerville was brought down in the area, and slotted the winner midway through the second half in a period when Oranje were dominating.

But there was a blow for Xavi ahead when Cody Gakpo had to be replaced by Ruben van Bommel in the 17th minute after going down under a heavy challenge from Saša Lukici in the penalty area.

The coach said he satisfied with his first week of competitive fixtures, including the 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam on Thursday, but saw plenty of room for improvement.

“I feel happy that we got three points, but we need to play better, especially in the first half,” Xavi said. “Second half we dominated more and attacked the spaces more.

“It’s important to get the three points, but the most important thing is we are generating lots of chances to score and the players feel comfortable with the structure that we have.”

Stodgy first half

Oranje had the better of a stodgy first 45 minutes of their second Nations League fixture, but only occasionally showed a cutting edge. Meerdink was unable to connect properly with Gakpo’s cross in the 15th minute, while a long spell of possession ended with Ryan Gravenberch dragging a shot wide.

The Dutch looked comfortable defending their lead and almost went further ahead when Serbia goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic needed all of his 2.02m height to tip Joey Veerman’s inswinging corner over the crossbar.

The home side equalised right at the start of the second half as they poured into the Dutch penalty area, drawing two good saves from Bart Verbruggen. The Oranje defenders were unable to clear their lines and the ball fell to half-time substitute Luka Jovic, who gave Verbruggen no chance from close range.

Dumfries dangerous

The Dutch took a grip on the game with Denzel Dumfries repeatedly finding space down the right, first picking out Van Bommel, whose shot hit the outside of the post, before an even better cross was turned over the crossbar by Tijjani Reijnders.

Meerdink’s winner in the 69th minute was provided by Guus Til, who had just come on as a substitute, as the AZ striker held off the close attentions of his marker to steer the ball into in the far corner.

Jovic remained Serbia’s greatest threat as the hosts pushed for an equaliser, twice flashing headers narrowly wide, while Van Bommel should have put the game beyond reach with a late breakaway, but his tame shot failed to test Milinkovic-Savic.

The Netherlands next play Greece, who beat Serbia 2-1 in their opening match, in Thessaloniki on Thursday.

World.title: Would you read a book if it was printed like a newspaper?
World.content:
Typically, book formats are pretty standard. Hardback, paperback, e-book. But in the 1970s, a Dutch publisher tried a new configuration for novels: the newspaper.

Theo Knippenberg attributes his publishing career to his mother, who had for years nagged him to find a respectable trade.

“Totally by accident, I became a publisher,” Knippenberg told DutchNews.

The now 80-year-old stumbled on his success at an arts festival in Utrecht in the late 1960s. He sold a series of tiny books, bound together with an elastic band, by Dutch writers.

Knippenberg expalined that he ran into author Harry Mulisch at a road crossing and convinced the writer of The Discovery of Heaven to let him publish an excerpt of an essay. Once Mulisch was on board, Knippenberg used it as leverage to convince other famous Dutch writers, such as Jan Wolkers, to contribute.

A voracious reader, Knippenberg found books unaffordable during his student years. He took the proceeds from the mini book sales and invested them into publishing equipment – not a traditional printing press but one built to print newspapers.

Thinner newsprint was cheaper to produce and therefore cheaper to sell. Together with his wife, Patty Voorsmit, Knippenberg launched Bulkboek.

The first edition, published in 1970, was Schroot by Belgian writer Jef Geeraerts. It follows a former colonel in the Belgian military who is struggling to adapt to life in the Congo.

Over the following 26 years, Bulkboek would publish 250 novels in the newspaper format.

Readers could 

The editions were aimed at secondary students and included interviews, critical essays and explanatory texts to help readers understand the work.

The works were selected based on published availability and “my own tastes,” Knippenberg said.

He knew nothing about how publishing worked and had to learn how to create the text sheets, include illustrations and run the books off. He describes his early set-up as “so primitive.”

The initial print runs were all books from Dutch or Flemish authors but by the late 1970s, Knippenberg began branching out. “I got ambitious,” he says. Leo Tolstoy, Pablo Neruda and Iris Murdoch were a few of the authors whose works found their way into the Bulkboek format.

The publisher also moved beyond the Netherlands into Belgium, Germany and France, and began to publish books in languages other than Dutch.

In the early 1990s, the economics of publishing had changed, as cheap paperbacks came onto the market.

Last year, Bulkboek was taken over by educational publisher BruutTAAL, but Knippenberg continues to be involved with some aspects of the company. The new endeavour is working on a series of publications of short stories.

“Students have much shorter attention spans these days,” he says, explaining why short fiction is a better way to draw in young readers.

The publication format continues. On second-hand book websites, Bulkboeks are still available for sale. Leo Tolstoy’s Boyhood, Cees Nooteboom’s Half the World and Willem Frederik Hermans’s The Signet Ring can all be found, many for two or three euros. Less than you would have paid when they were first published by Bulkboek.

World.title: Opposition parties Pro and Volt team up to force budget deal
World.content:
Opposition parties Pro and Volt have joined forces for the next round of budget negotiations as they try to step up the pressure on the cabinet to make further concessions on social security.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said ministers had spent the last week drawing up “a new and attractive offer” addressing opposition parties’ concerns on welfare, the cost of living and replacing the “Box 3” asset tax mechanism.

Pro leader Jesse Klaver said the combined votes of his left-wing party and the pro-European Volt would give the government a “stable majority” in both houses of parliament.

An agreement with both Pro and Volt would give the coalition parties a comfortable majority in the lower house and the 16 seats it needs in the Senate, where Pro is the largest group but still needs Volt’s two seats to get over the line.

But the right-wing liberal VVD, the party of finance minister Eelco Heinen, is anxious not to make too many concessions to Pro, which would risk driving its voters away to its rivals such as JA21 and Geert Wilders’ far-right PVV.

Pick a side

“We are fighting for progress for ordinary people and a fair contribution from the super-rich,” Klaver said. “We believe in progressive co-operation.”

Volt leader Laurens Dassen said: “The world is changing rapidly. People expect politicians to work together towards a sustainable and innovative future.”

Jetten has been under pressure from the opposition on left and right to choose a side after all parties poured cold water on his hopes of finding a route through the middle.

The prime minister argued he would be “short-changing the country” if he excluded one side from the talks, but JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said a broad approach “isn’t going to work” while Klaver warned his party would block the entire budget if the cabinet tried to do separate deals for each department.

Welfare cuts

Heinen has already agreed to postpone or cancel around half of the €6 billion cuts to welfare spending that were in the coalition agreement in February, but Pro wants the cabinet to go further.

Parties such as JA21, on the other hand, want to see even bigger welfare cuts, arguing that lower taxes are the best way to relieve the pressure on households and businesses.

Jetten and Heinen held talks on Saturday with Pro, Volt and the ChristenUnie, whose leader, Mirjam Bikker, said there had been “movement” from the coalition parties.

The ChristenUnie’s priorities are to ensure households are able to pay for essentials through the winter as energy and grocery bills rise. Bikker said it was “high time” that the coalition parties “feel the urgency” to make a deal.

BBB back on board

Later on Saturday the two ministers are due to talk to JA21 and the orthodox-protestant SGP, who have formed a right-wing alliance with 12 seats in the lower house.

Jetten and Heinen will also speak to Jan Struijs, leader of pensioners’ party 50Plus, and Henk Vermeer of the farmers’ party BBB, who are the second largest party in the Senate.

Jetten had initially said the BBB were no longer an option after the party backed a motion of no confidence during the budget debate, but he and Vermeer patched up their differences in a phone call last week.

World.title: Russia condemns Polish city’s “barbaric” removal of Monument of Gratitude to the Red Army
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the removal of a monument in the Polish city of Rzeszów expressing “gratitude” to the Soviet Red Army. It called the move “barbaric” and “sacrilegious”. The monument – part of which will be moved to a nearby Soviet cemetery and another to a museum – has been the subject of a long-running legal and political battle, amid wider debate in Poland about “decommunising” public spaces, especially in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 23 września 2026 r. w Rzeszowie (województwo podkarpackie), decyzją władz polskich i z naruszeniem dokumentów rosyjsko-polskich dotyczących ochrony obiektów dziedzictwa memorialnego, rozpoczęto proces demontażu pomnika wdzięczności żołnierzom… pic.twitter.com/HYuNeLG5dy — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) September 24, 2026 The Monument of Gratitude to the Red Army, standing 8.5 metres tall and weighing 6.6 tons, was erected in Rzeszów, southeast Poland, shortly after the end of World War Two, when the Soviets had pushed Nazi Germany out of Poland and then installed their own communist government. It is located on Ghetto Victims Square, a public space also created after the war on the grounds of the city’s former Jewish cemetery, which had been destroyed by the German occupiers in 1942. Poland’s Institute of National Remembrance, a state historical body, notes that the monument was erected just a few metres from where two Polish anti-communist resistance fighters who had been members of the wartime Home Army (AK) had been publicly hanged by the communists. The monument’s plinth featured bas-relief sculptures depicting Red Army Generals Ivan Konev and Karol Świerczewski, soldiers, and industrial and agricultural workers carrying a hammer and sickle. At the top of the 8.5-metre column was a statue of a woman and child. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. That triggered a legal battle in over the monument in Rzeszów. The government-appointed provincial governor and the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body, moved to have it dismantled, arguing that the monument glorified communism. But city hall – led by left-wing mayor Tadeusz Ferenc, who had been a member of the communist party before 1989 – challenged the decision. It argued that the monument did not promote communism and noted that its name, referring to gratitude to the Red Army, was not an official one. In 2019, the provincial administrative court sided with the city and overturned the decision to remove the monument. However, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 prompted many Polish municipalities that had not removed Soviet-era monuments to begin doing so. In April 2022, Rzeszów’s current mayor, Konrad Fijołek, announced that his city’s monument would be removed from its current location and placed in a Soviet soldiers’ cemetery elsewhere in the city. “In principle, I am not in favor of dismantling or demolishing monuments, as they are a testament to history,” said the mayor. “But in light of the current wartime reality, this monument should not remain in its current location. But we are not barbarians; we will not demolish the monument, but relocate it.” However, the IPN opposed the idea of relocating the monument and refused to cover the costs of doing so. It wanted it to be liquidated entirely. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 As a result, the city is paying 156,000 zloty (€35,700) for the monument to be removed, reports news website Wirtualna Polska. The bas-reliefs will go to the Soviet cemetery while the statue of mother and child will go to the city’s Museum of Technology and the Military. Work to remove the monument began this week and is expected to last until November. Once the above-ground section has been removed, a special conservation committee, including a representative of Poland’s Rabbinical Commission for Cemeteries, will determine how to proceed with the monument’s foundation. The beginning of the removal work prompted anger from Moscow, with the Russian embassy in Warsaw issuing a statement that called it a “sacrilegious step”. It demanded “the immediate cessation of work” and restoration of the monument to its previous state. “With regret, we must state once again: the barbaric policy of the Polish authorities, consisting of destroying everything that serves as evidence of the invaluable feat of the soldiers and officers of the Red Army in liberating Poland from Nazi occupation, is being continued at an ever faster pace,” they continued. Russia regards the Soviet Union’s driving of Nazi Germany out of Central and Eastern Europe at the end of World War Two as a “liberation”. However, many in the region reject that term, given that it involved bringing their countries under brutal Soviet domination instead. In its statement, the Russian embassy also claimed that the actions in Rzeszów are a “violation of Russian-Polish documents concerning the protection of memorial heritage sites”. Moscow regularly claims that Poland’s removal of Soviet memorials violates a 1994 agreement between the two countries on respect for graves and other places of memory. It did so in August this year, when protesting the demolition of a monument in the town of Pyrzyce. However, Poland points out that the agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. Russia has criticised the "sacrilegious" demolition of a Soviet monument in Poland, calling it a “flagrant violation” of a bilateral agreement. But Poland's @ipngovpl says it was a "propaganda object" that had to be removed under a "decommunisation" law https://t.co/73T99ZlPqU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Rzeszów is also home to one of the famous – or infamous, depending on one’s perspective – communist-era monuments in Poland, the 38-metre-tall Monument to the Revolutionary Struggle. It has become a landmark of the city. In 2017, the IPN recommended that it be removed under the “decommunisation” law. The owners of the land upon which it sits also wanted to demolish it. However, mayors Ferenc and Fijołek sought to protect the monument, and their efforts succeeded last year, when it was added to Poland’s list of protected monuments, preventing it from being destroyed. World.title: Polish president “doesn’t like” Trump inviting Putin to G20 but will still attend summit
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Polish President Karol Nawrocki “does not like” the fact that the Trump administration has invited Vladimir Putin to this year’s G20 summit in the United States, says his chief foreign policy aide. However, Nawrocki, who is a close ally of Donald Trump, still plans to attend the event – which Poland has been invited to as a guest rather than a full G20 member – in order to represent Polish interests and push for full membership of the group. 🔴 "Nie podoba nam się to". Nawrocki ma problem po decyzji Trumpa Prezydent Karol Nawrocki weźmie udział w grudniowym szczycie G20 w Miami, na który zaproszono również Władimira Putina. Szef Biura Polityki Międzynarodowej Kancelarii Prezydenta Marcin Przydacz przyznał na antenie… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) September 26, 2026 The G20, a major intergovernmental forum, holds an annual summit whose location rotates among members. This year’s event will take place in December at a golf resort in Miami owned by Trump. On Wednesday this week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that Trump has invited Putin to attend the summit, saying that “we think it’s an opportunity for him to engage…with other world leaders” and “we hope that’s an invitation he’ll accept”. “If you only meet with people that you agree with, then these are very nice meetings but nothing happens,” added Rubio. “In order to solve problems, you have to meet with people that you disagree with or the people that you might have some issues with.” Marco Rubio on Russia: We’ve invited President Putin to the G20. We think it’s an opportunity for him to engage not just with Trump, but with other world leaders. We hope that’s an invitation he will accept. pic.twitter.com/e0GSz7Y8gm — Clash Report (@clashreport) September 23, 2026 Last December, Rubio also announced Poland’s invitation to the summit as a guest, saying that it would be “assuming its rightful place in the G20”. In May this year, the US also “expressed its strong support for Poland’s accession to the G20 as a permanent member”. Poland will be represented by Nawrocki, who is a vocal critic of Putin and Russia, and is himself on a Russian wanted list for his work leading efforts to demolish Soviet-era monuments in Poland. In an interview on Sunday with news website Wirtualna Polska, the head of Nawrocki’s international policy office, Marcin Przydacz, was asked if the US was right to invite Putin. “We don’t like it,” he replied. “But we were invited to the G20 summit as guests, and it’s not our role to tell the participants who should be part of it,” he added, noting that Russia is a founding member of the G20. However, “if it were up to us, Russia should be isolated in all international forums.” Nevertheless, “President [Nawrocki] is going to Miami and doesn’t intend to change his plans at this stage”, confirmed Przydacz. “Poland will be at the G20 summit because it’s in our interest…This isn’t the only format in which we sit with countries we disagree with.” However, he also added that, “if the Russian leader actually intends to come, and is not just invited, we will discuss this with our European and Euro-Atlantic allies”. Putin has not attended a G20 summit in person since 2019, initially due to the COVID-19 pandemic and later amid the fallout from Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the International Criminal Court’s arrest warrant against him. The US is not a member of the ICC, so the arrest warrant does not apply on its territory. Przydacz told Wirtualna Polska that Putin “should be held accountable for his crimes”. Asked if Nawrocki would shake hands with the Russian president at the G20, Przydacz said that he “doesn’t think any interactions will occur”. The United States has expressed "strong support for Poland’s accession to the G20 as a permanent member" following talks in Warsaw, after which it also emphasised "strong and growing" Polish-American relations https://t.co/qTpCACnMfu — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 2, 2026 He also emphasised that Poland’s invitation to the summit was a “major success, demonstrating our growing role”. He said that Nawrocki would use the event to push its ambition to become a full member of the group. He added that it would also seek to “bring a Central European perspective” to the event, representing its entire region, which has so far been excluded from the G20. Earlier this week, Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski said that, in his opinion, the US should make Putin’s invitation to the G20 conditional upon Russia implementing a ceasefire in Ukraine, reported news website Interia. However, he noted that, when a G20 meeting of finance ministers took place in the US earlier this year, Poland had attended alongside Russia. President @NawrockiKn says that a planned new permanent US military base in Poland is “confirmed” because his American counterpart, Donald Trump, is “famous for keeping his word”. He also suggested that the new facility will be called “Fort Trump” https://t.co/uGGJSBe5nr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 23, 2026 Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Poland has been one of Kyiv’s closest allies, providing extensive military, humanitarian and diplomatic support to its eastern neighbour. Poland has also been one of the primary targets of Russia’s hybrid actions against European countries, including airspace violations, acts of sabotage, cyberattacks and disinformation. World.title: Poland extends tax rights to same-sex couples with foreign marriages
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Polish government has granted same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry the same tax rights as other married couples. The decision follows a ruling by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) requiring Poland – whose domestic law does not allow same-sex couples to form any type of legal union – to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU member states. Podpisałem dziś interpretację ogólną, która zapewnia, że osoby, które uzyskały transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa będą miały w polskich urzędach skarbowych takie same prawa i obowiązki podatkowe jak wszyscy małżonkowie. — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) September 24, 2026 “Today, I signed a general interpretation ensuring that persons who have obtained a transcription of their marriage certificate will have the same tax rights and obligations in Polish tax offices as all other married couples,” announced finance minister Andrzej Domański in a social media post. A general interpretation is an official position taken by the finance ministry aiming to clarify the application of tax law in a specific area. Among the benefits that couples with a transcribed foreign marriage certificate can now receive include preferential treatment under inheritance and gift tax rules and the ability to file joint personal income tax returns. Couples may also pay tax on behalf of a spouse and refuse to testify as a witness in proceedings involving their spouse. “This is about basic equality, justice and fairness,” Domański told broadcaster TVN. “We want these rights to be enforceable in an effective way.” The finance minister said that the decision would have a “negligible” impact on the state budget. He also noted that such couples would be subject to the obligations that apply to other married couples in Poland, which include liability for their spouse’s tax obligations. Osoby, które uzyskały tak zwaną transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa, będą miały przed polskimi urzędami skarbowymi dokładnie takie same prawa i obowiązki jak pozostali małżonkowie – powiedział minister finansów Andrzej Domański w rozmowie z Grzegorzem Kajdanowiczem w @faktypofaktach w… pic.twitter.com/uVwDaD3ZDk — tvn24 (@tvn24) September 24, 2026 The finance minister’s decision has drawn criticism from right-wing politicians, who argue that recognition of same-sex marriage violates the constitution, which states that “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland”. Paweł Szefernaker, chief of staff to President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, said Domański’s actions were “inconsistent with the constitution” and had been carried out “without legislation, without debate, without honestly telling Poles what is really happening”. “Everyone has the right to a private life,” he added. “However, the state has a duty to protect the legal order and provide tax support for marriage.” Patryk Jaki, a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party, said that the finance minister’s actions “clearly violate Polish law and will have legal implications in the future” for Domański, who is “writing additional points in the indictment against himself”. Sławomir Mentzen, one of the leaders of the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) group, said the tax interpretation “will be revoked on the very first day” if his party comes to power. To jest niezgodna z Konstytucją próba faktycznego zrównania małżeństwa ze związkami jednopłciowymi. Bez zmiany Konstytucji, bez ustawy, bez debaty, bez uczciwego powiedzenia Polakom, co naprawdę się dzieje. Każdy ma prawo do prywatnego życia według własnych wyborów. Ale państwo… https://t.co/0CQ9Lnfl02 — Paweł Szefernaker 🇵🇱 (@szefernaker) September 24, 2026 The changes follow a ruling issued by the CJEU in November 2025 ordering Poland to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU states. The court found that failing to do so infringes the freedom to move and reside within the EU as well as the right to respect for private and family life. In light of that ruling, in March this year, Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA) ordered Warsaw’s registry office to recognise a marriage conducted by two Polish men in Germany by transcribing it into the Polish civil registry. In May, the Polish government issued a regulation allowing such transcriptions of foreign same-sex marriages to take place nationwide. It went into force in August. However, even before then, some cities had begun transcribing marriage certificates, beginning with Warsaw and Wrocław in May. At the end of August, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski reported that 84 same-sex couples had already transcribed their foreign marriages under the government’s new regulation. Poland has begun paying benefits to same-sex couples who married abroad then entered their marriage into the Polish registry. The EU court ordered Poland to recognise such marriages, even though domestic law does not allow for any form of same-sex union https://t.co/svnRjyBO8Q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 22, 2026 While foreign same-sex marriages can now be entered into Poland’s civil registry, questions have remained as to what that will mean in practice for such couples, especially as domestic law does not recognise same-sex relationships. In another development, labour minister Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk announced last week that the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) has begun paying care allowances to qualifying same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry. World.title: Prosecutors drop case in which Wałęsa was accused of lying about being communist collaborator
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prosecutors have ended a decade-long case in which former president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa was accused of falsely claiming not to have authored documents relating to his alleged cooperation with the communist authorities. Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that helped bring down the communist regime in the 1980s, has always denied longstanding claims that, in the 1970s, he acted as an informant to the communist security services. The case has become highly politicised, with right-wing figures – especially from the Law and Justice (PiS) party that ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 – critical of Wałęsa. By contrast, the former president, who turns 83 next week, enjoys good relations with the current ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Waldemar Żurek, Tusk’s justice minister and prosecutor general, welcomed the decision to drop the case against Wałęsa, saying that, under PiS, “a politicised state apparatus hounded the legend of Solidarity, deliberately ignoring facts and basic logic”. Now, “truth has triumphed over an attempt to rewrite history”. Prokuratura ostatecznie umorzyła śledztwo przeciwko Lechowi Wałęsie. Przez lata upolityczniony aparat państwa ścigał legendę „Solidarności”, celowo ignorując fakty i elementarną logikę. Zignorowano bezsporny fakt historyczny – SB masowo fałszowała dokumenty i podpisy Wałęsy w… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) September 24, 2026 The case in question stems from statements made by Wałęsa in 2016 during an investigation by the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that also has prosecutorial powers. Those proceedings, in which the former Polish president testified as a witness, were launched after documents apparently carrying his signature were found in the home archives of former communist interior minister Czesław Kiszczak. The files indicated that Wałęsa, working under the code name TW Bolek, signed a commitment to collaborate with the communist Security Service (SB). They also included payslips and informant’s notes. The former president had told the media at the time when the documents were discovered that they had been forged. When speaking to IPN investigators, he also denied having drafted or signed all but one of the documents. However, prosecutors subsequently claimed that – after comparing the documents from Kiszczak’s file with others they said had been written and signed by Wałęsa, as well as consulting forensic handwriting experts – Wałęsa’s testimony was false in the case of over 50 of the documents. In 2021, the former president was charged with giving false testimony. Then, in 2023, he was indicted, meaning the case was sent to court. However, in 2024, after Tusk’s government had taken power from PiS, prosecutors asked that the case be returned to them by the court, which agreed to the request. Now, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw has announced that it is discontinuing the case entirely, after finding that there are no grounds for Wałęsa to be prosecuted. Lech Wałęsa will face trial accused of falsely testifying not to have signed documents of cooperation with the communist authorities. If convicted, he can be jailed for up to 3 years. He calls the claims against him "terrible insults and monstrous lies" https://t.co/X0eb4e5ahm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 30, 2023 In a statement explaining the decision, prosecutors claimed that there had been significant “methodological errors” made previously in attributing handwritten texts to Wałęsa and in handwriting comparisons between them. “There was no evidence to assume with 100% certainty that the comparative material actually came from Lech Wałęsa,” they wrote. In fact, “the evidence collected clearly indicated that Lech Wałęsa did not write long manuscripts during his life, and especially not in the 1970s”. “Some witnesses explicitly stated that, at that time, he was a secondary illiterate,” meaning someone who has lost their ability to read and write, said the prosecutors. “He was not able to write and could barely read.” This, along with other concerns over how the case was previously conducted, “led to the conclusion that there was no certain basis to assume that Lech Wałęsa was the author of the documents disclosed in the ‘Kiszczak files’, and therefore there was no evidence that he lied during the interrogation”. Hit! Ekipa Tuska ogłosiła Wałęsę analfabetą by wybronić go przed Bolkiem! To się nie dzieje! To niemożliwe! pic.twitter.com/PQnOn5XDb0 — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) September 24, 2026 Prosecutors also said that “the testimony of numerous witnesses proves that the files of TW Bolek, discovered in the possession of General Kiszczak’s widow, were most likely fabricated. Finally, they argued that, even if Wałęsa had given false testimony, he was protected by the constitutional right against self-incrimination while being interviewed as a witness. “The prosecution found that Lech Wałęsa could have feared that if he admitted to having prepared or signed the documents from the ‘Kiszczak files’…all his testimonies in which he denied being secret collaborator “Bolek” in previous proceedings…would be deemed false and would lead to his being held criminally liable.” Lech Wałęsa, Angela Merkel and Volodymyr Zelensky have been named the first distinguished members of the European Order of Merit. The award was created by the European Parliament to "honour those who did not simply believe in Europe, but helped build it" https://t.co/inosiiRQkW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 11, 2026 In response to the announcement, Wałęsa shared on his Facebook page the post by Żurek praising the prosecutors’ decision. Wałęsa then added a comment claiming that Jarosław and Lech Kaczyński, the founders of PiS, had ordered a right-wing historian, Sławomir Cenckiewicz, to fake the Kiszczak files. Cenckiewicz has written extensively about Wałęsa, including about his alleged collaboration with the communist security services. He also recently served as national security advisor to current Polish President Karol Nawrocki, who was elected last year with the support of PiS. In a series of social media posts on Thursday, Cenkiewicz said that he had “never read a bigger lie” than the prosecutors’ statement justifying dropping the case. He also ridiculed the idea that Wałęsa could have led the Solidarity movement in the 1980s and served as president in the 1990s if he was a “secondary illiterate”. Większego kłamstwa przebranego w wymiar sprawiedliwości RP nigdy nie czytałem! To większe kłamstwo niż skandaliczny wyrok Kapińskiego i spółki z 2000 r.! Reżim Tuska uznał, że Wałęsa nie był Bolkiem, a Instytut Sehna niczego kategorycznie nie ustalił! I powtórzyli brednie… — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) September 24, 2026 The accusations of communist collaboration have tarnished Wałęsa’s reputation among some Poles. In 2017, shortly after the Kiszczak files were uncovered, a poll by IBRiS for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 28% believed Wałęsa was not a national hero. However, 62% said that he was. Earlier this year, Wałęsa was named as one of the first three distinguished members of the European Order of Merit, a new initiative launched by the European Parliament, alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and former German Chancellor Angela Merkel.
