World.title: Iraq recovers 80 smuggled artifacts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice successfully repatriated 80 smuggled historical artifacts and rare artworks on Monday, September 28, 2026, marking another breakthrough in federal legal campaigns to recover looted antiquities from abroad.

According to an official statement issued by the ministry, the restitution was finalized through intensive international legal proceedings managed by the Directorate of External Litigation, executed in direct operational coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy of the Republic of Iraq in Washington, D.C.

The ministry stated that the legal recovery operations, directed and monitored by Minister of Justice Dr. Khaled Shwani, form an integral part of Baghdad’s overarching policy to safeguard Iraq’s cultural heritage and reclaim sovereign historical assets dispersed through illicit trading networks.

Through its dedicated Department for the Recovery of Antiquities and Assets, the Directorate of External Litigation manages active cross-border claims, targeting antiquities illegally excavated from unmonitored archaeological digs as well as stolen cataloged pieces traded internationally in violation of Iraqi heritage statutes and UNESCO conventions.

Federal judicial authorities emphasized that these coordinated actions reflect the justice ministry’s structured legal mandate to track, document, and pursue stolen national assets worldwide.

By leveraging bilateral judicial agreements and working through diplomatic missions across North America and Europe, the Iraqi government aims to ensure the comprehensive preservation of Mesopotamia’s civilizational legacy and institutionalize robust legal frameworks against the illicit trafficking of cultural antiquities.

World.title: Gulf Cup 27: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar clinch semifinals as Iraq eyes decisive clash
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Matchday Two of the group stage at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup in Jeddah concluded with three national teams securing early qualification for the semifinals, leaving the remaining knockout berth in Group A contested ahead of the final group round.

Host nation Saudi Arabia confirmed its place in the final four alongside Group B qualifiers the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, while regional football powerhouses Kuwait, Bahrain, and Yemen suffered early mathematical elimination from tournament contention.

In Group A, tournament hosts Saudi Arabia solidified their standing at the summit of the table with a maximum of 6 points and a positive four goal difference following back-to-back victories. Iraq occupies second place with 4 points and a plus-one goal differential, having recorded one win and one draw across their opening fixtures.

Oman sits third with 1 point and a negative three goal differential, while Kuwait trails at the bottom of the group with zero points and a negative two goal difference. The distribution leaves Iraq positioned for a decisive final-round Gulf derby against Saudi Arabia, coinciding with the simultaneous encounter between Oman and Kuwait to determine the group’s second qualifying spot.

Group B witnessed a decisive resolution as both the United Arab Emirates and Qatar secured semifinal qualification with a match to spare, each accumulating 6 points from two consecutive victories. The UAE maintains the top position by virtue of an advantageous goal difference of plus-seven compared to Qatar’s plus-three.

Yemen and Bahrain sit eliminated at the foot of the table without points, both carrying identical negative five goal differentials. The final group fixtures will settle group positioning between the two leading sides as the tournament bracket prepares for the knockout stage.

World.title: Iraq officially licenses Starlink satellite internet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC) confirmed on Sunday, September 27, 2026, that satellite internet provider Starlink has secured an official operational license, formally legalizing its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite broadband services across Iraqi territory.

Speaking to the official state news agency, CMC Chief Executive Officer Baligh Abu Kalal dismissed claims that Iraqi telecommunications traffic and user data are hosted or routed through Qatar, stating that federal security authorities maintain complete sovereign oversight over all network operations and registered hardware within the country.

The licensing milestone follows public contention between federal regulatory bodies and the Ministry of Communications. In mid-August 2026, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad argued that the ground gateway servicing Iraq was located in Qatar, raising sovereignty concerns regarding regional content filtering, pornography blocks, and executive internet throttling during national examinations and public demonstrations.

Sanad had framed terrestrial Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) expansion as Iraq’s premier digital priority against foreign satellite conglomerates. Responding to these concerns, Abu Kalal clarified that Starlink’s regulatory framework incorporates a rigorous security annex, granting Iraqi intelligence and regulatory apparatuses real-time visibility into all active terminals, user registries, and equipment distributed nationally.

Abu Kalal explained that while initial deployment encountered minor delays due to multi-agency security vetting, the first batch of customer subscription terminals has been released, with sequential hardware shipments proceeding smoothly to fulfill pending consumer orders via the company’s official portal.

Although Starlink originally scheduled the construction of domestic terrestrial ground stations within two years, surging local demand has prompted expedited bilateral negotiations to install local ground gateways across Iraq ahead of schedule.

The CMC executive stressed that satellite internet governance relies fundamentally on sovereign licensing frameworks, statutory compliance, and contractual obligations, ensuring that national security protocols remain fully enforced regardless of atmospheric broadcast mechanics.

World.title: Basra Oil and Gas Expo concludes with 300 companies from 18 nations
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) – The fourth edition of the Basra International Exhibition for Oil, Gas, Energy, and Petrochemicals concluded its proceedings at the Basrah International Fairground in Al-Maqal Port, Basra, gathering approximately 300 international and domestic corporate participants representing 18 countries.

Organized in close collaboration with operating entities of the Iraqi Ministry of Oil and regional energy bodies, the multi-day industry forum served as a strategic platform to showcase cutting-edge extractive technologies, negotiate joint-venture partnerships, and accelerate technological transfer across Iraq’s upstream, midstream, and downstream infrastructure.

Exhibits spanned specialized industrial solutions ranging from century-old quality assurance institutions and artificial intelligence-driven exploration software to hazardous chemical remediation models and municipal lighting engineering.

Third-party engineering assessment and asset integrity management were prominently featured by Germany’s TÜV Rheinland, an industrial testing and certification firm with over 150 years of operations.

Hazem Yahya Abdul-Qader, company representative to the exhibition, stated that TÜV Rheinland functions as an officially accredited third-party technical inspection entity under the Ministry of Oil, executing long-term compliance and materials conformity contracts with major state operators including the Basra Oil Company (BOC) and the Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC).

Abdul-Qader noted that the firm also maintains active service delivery agreements with KBR at the Majnoon oil field alongside the State Company for Heavy Engineering Equipment, providing full-lifecycle asset integrity diagnostics, risk evaluations, welder and inspector certifications, and mandatory specialized driver licensing to guarantee operating facilities meet stringent international safety and equipment preservation standards.

Advanced digital transformation in upstream exploration was showcased by China’s Beijing Jurassic Software, a 30-year veteran developer of petroleum modeling systems. Company representative Li Hui explained that the firm provides integrated software architectures tailored for oil and gas upstream workflows, incorporating exploration analytics, drilling and well-completion management, reservoir simulation, electrical submersible pump (ESP) system diagnostics, and scalable “Smart Field” management hubs designed to maximize reservoir exploitation efficiency.

Concurrently, regional manufacturing innovations were highlighted by Iranian lighting fabricator Ram Noor, with representative Asmaa Naeem detailing their deployment of seamless, single-piece decorative lighting poles manufactured in star, triangular, and square cross-sections to replace traditional round conical street lighting across industrial zones and urban districts.

Environmental remediation and oilfield waste management were represented by domestic Iraqi enterprise Al-Anfal, which specializes in hazardous and non-hazardous waste logistics across major southern producing assets. Company representative Hawraa Kadhim confirmed that Al-Anfal manages field services across Exploration Block 9, the Siba gas field, and the Artawi oil field, holding active environmental service contracts with Kuwait Energy and China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC).

Kadhim underscored that Al-Anfal operates as the sole licensed and environmentally certified entity in Basra authorized to transport, treat, and recycle industrial chemical waste in strict compliance with federal environmental conservation guidelines, highlighting domestic capabilities within Iraq’s extractive supply chain.

World.title: Iraq starts receiving gasoline from Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially started importing gasoline through Syria, creating a crucial overland energy corridor between the two nations.

This transit route serves as a critical alternative for Baghdad to secure vital fuel supplies amid difficulties facing maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The initial consignment consisted of roughly 32,800 metric tons of high-octane gasoline brought by sea from the United States. The shipment arrived at Syria’s Baniyas port aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Avanti.

The fuel was moved to storage tanks at the Baniyas refinery before being loaded into tanker trucks. At least 77 tanker trucks have already left the port, headed toward Iraq’s Baiji refinery, according to Reuters.

A transit contract between the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company (SPC) and Qatar’s UCC Holding, which provided the gasoline and is in charge of logistics, governs the operation.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has finalized the agreement to ensure the continuity of these supplies.

The route was only used in one direction, transporting Iraqi fuel oil by road to the Syrian port of Baniyas before being exported out by sea, reaching the US market for the first time in July.

According to officials, while the present transportation arrangement only covers gasoline, the corridor might potentially grow to include other petroleum products, crude oil, and other items.

World.title: Vitol becomes second-largest buyer of Iraq’s oil after UAE’s ADNOC
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Vitol has strengthened its presence in the Iraqi oil market by purchasing at least 25 million barrels of crude in September 2026, a move reflecting how major oil traders are capitalizing on supply disruptions in the Gulf region.

The Swiss-based Dutch multinational energy and commodity trading company is leveraging its shipping and logistics capabilities to provide export outlets for Iraqi crude amid the challenges facing tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz due to the conflict between the United States and Iran.

These purchases come as Baghdad seeks to maintain oil flows to global markets following a decline in exports during the early months of the war, when securing the transport of shipments from Iraq’s southern ports proved difficult.

The deal highlights the shifting dynamics of the Middle East oil trade, where the ability to secure tankers and arrange transportation has become a critical factor in accessing crude oil, alongside Iraq’s use of price discounts to attract buyers willing to take on shipping risks.

Vitol has purchased between 25 and 30 million barrels of Iraqi crude scheduled for loading this September.

An official in the Iraqi energy sector indicated that the company’s share amounted to approximately 25 million barrels, according to Reuters.

Vitol has become the second-largest buyer of Iraqi oil this month, trailing the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC), which purchased approximately 40 million barrels, compared to about 32 million barrels in August.

The moves came amid a drop in Iraq’s oil exports during the early months of the conflict, owing to the country’s ports’ position in the northern Arabian Gulf and the lack of its own shipping fleet, which hindered petroleum delivery to global markets.

According to data from Kpler, a leading data platform that tracks commodity flows and maritime shipping, Iraqi oil exports from southern ports averaged approximately 2.35 million barrels per day in August.

In August, Iran granted a number of Iraqi oil tankers permission to transit the Strait of Hormuz, following repeated requests from Baghdad for arrangements to ensure continued oil exports.

Iraqi oil shipments face challenges due to navigational risks in the Strait of Hormuz. Vessels transiting the waterway are exposed to the threat of Iranian attacks, prompting buyers to demand price discounts to offset higher transportation and insurance costs.

World.title: Iraq studies proposals to store oil in Oman, Egypt, Singapore
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is studying proposals to store crude oil in storage facilities in countries including Egypt, Oman, and Singapore.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that the government is studying proposals to participate in refinery and storage projects outside Iraq to select the best options.

To move forward with storing crude oil in Egypt, Iraq needs to complete the Basra-Haditha pipeline project, which would then extend out toward the Jordanian port of Aqaba and finally to the city of Arish in the northeastern Sinai Peninsula, according to al-Rikabi.

In September 2025, Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has signed two agreements with OQ, formerly known as Oman Oil Company, and its subsidiary, Oman Tank Terminal Company (OTTCO).

The first agreement establishes a strategic partnership to develop an integrated project to store Iraqi crude oil in the Special Economic Zone at Duqm (SEZD), the largest special economic zone in the Middle East and North Africa.

The second agreement outlines OQ’s responsibility to market Iraqi crude oil in global markets. The deal aims to leverage the administrative and commercial strengths of both parties to enhance the trading value of Iraqi crude oil internationally.

The proposals are part of the Iraqi government’s effort to bypass the Strait of Hormuz—the main route for the country’s oil exports—where maritime shipping has been facing difficulties since the start of the military conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran.

Since the outbreak of the war on February 28 and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq’s seaborne oil exports collapsed to unprecedented levels.

Iraq’s oil exports fell to approximately 550,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, and 98,000 barrels per day in May, before gradually rising to 2.16 million barrels per day in August.

World.title: International coalition halts financial aid to Peshmerga
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US-led international coalition has officially halted financial aid to Iraqi Kurdistan’s Peshmerga forces following the expiration of a four-year agreement.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and the United States Department of Defense inked an agreement that extended from September 21, 2022, until September 21, 2026.

On Thursday, the troops received their final allowance for August and September 2026.

According to the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs, Bakhtiar Sadiq, the financial aid under the initial agreement was planned to steadily reduce by 25 percent each year until reaching a complete halt.

This cash halt aligns with the overall conclusion of the international coalition’s military operations in Iraq, with a full stoppage of combat and training responsibilities expected by September 30, 2026.

Additionally, the proposed US Counter-ISIS Train and Equip Fund (CTEF) plan for 2027 includes no support for the Peshmerga.

The international coalition has tied its financial assistance to necessary reforms and the unification of the Peshmerga forces, particularly the integration of politically separated units. Earlier in September, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) publicly announced that the unification process was complete.

To address the newly established funding imbalance, the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs has formally requested the federal government in Baghdad to adjust Peshmerga salaries to align them permanently with federal Iraqi military and security forces.

MUMBAI: Supreme Court on Monday stays the bail granted recently by Bombay high court to Shiv Sena municipal corporator Ramesh Mhatre,73, in a case of assault on civic hospital doctors and warned that members of the medical fraternity cannot be assaulted at will in such a manner.The SC directed him to surrender within three days.A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta were hearing a bail cancellation plea of The Maharashtra government which challenge the HC order ofThe bench orally cited the general and larger implications an assault on doctors in the medical fraternity. âMedical fraternity serves the people. They cannot be attacked in this manner,â the bench said.Appearing for Mhatre, senior counsel Siddharth Dave said for bail cancellation a higher standard was required. He pointed out that trial was underway before a Magistrate with two prosecution witnesses having deposed and a woman doctor to depose on October 3.Mhatre cooperated with the probe and trial the SC was informed.The maximum sentence under the law is five yearsâ imprisonment for the main offence in the case and there was no obstruction caused in the trial caused, Mhatreâs counsel also submitted.While acknowledging the concerns raised by the bench, the counsel submitted that as a âcriminal caseâ evidence had to form the basis of the outcome.The State had referred to Mhatreâs antecedents while seeking cancellation of his bail.Dave, submitted that Mhatre had been acquitted in 18 of the 19 cases cited against him. âCall for the records of those cases also,â the Court immediately said.The SC had on September 7 concerns over the cases of assaults on doctors and hospital staff in Maharashtra and said they cannot be treated as routine law-and-order.The Bombay HC bench led by then Acting Chief Justice RV Ghuge had taken the matter suo motu observing the seriousness of the assaults. And on July 27 in its initial order come down on Mhatre and the police and Justice Ghuge had noted that Mhatre was arrested 48 hours after the alleged assault. âWhy do you (Mhatre) behave like this? Why beat the public? They are your voters. Surprising that a person who goes to voters and says âvote for me, I want to serve youâ. ..after winning, starts beating people,â he said while hearing pleas filed by the corporator and others seeking bail on any stringent condition HC deemed fit. âEven in public life, you are for the public, are here for the public.âOn August 7 the Bombay HC had fast tracked their trial and granted bail to Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and three others accused behind bars in the July 6 assault on doctors including a woman doctor at a municipal hospital in Dombivli, but all four were to remain outside Maharashtra till the criminal trial begins.The HC had also framed a time-line for probe and prosecution to proceed swiftly and the time to be spent outside Maharashtra for all four would likely be a month.The endevour should be to complete trial in 3 months once charge is framed, the HC said.The ACJ Ghuge dictating the order in open court had said, âIn a democracy an elected representative is by the people and for the people. If the elected representative is accused of assaulting his own voters, such a situation is bound to dent the fabric of democracy in this country and erode public confidence.ââPolice arrested Mhatre on July 8 for allegedly slapping and punching a doctor and assaulting a resident medical officer. A local court granted him bail on July 14, while he was in a hospital. He was released but on July 18 the HC took up the matter suo motu and staying the bail order for all four, directed Mhatre to surrender. He did on July 19.

World.title: Stone pelting, tear gas and clashes with police: What is happening in Ujjain
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tensions rose in Ujjain on Monday as protesters clashed with police during demonstrations over development work in the city. Police were deployed in large numbers around the Shahi Masjid Complex as sporadic protests and

were reported in the area.

The clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the Shahi Masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028, with authorities planning a major infrastructure overhaul ahead of the religious gathering.

Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred when a large group of people clashed with them at the spot where a portion of Shahi Masjid was planned to be demolished.

Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel has been deployed at the spot.

SP Pradeep Sharma says, "...all communities and sections of society are continuously extending their cooperation and support in their respective areas. Even today, the demolition work, initiated by the mosque committee itself, is underway at the Shahi Masjid. As a precautionary measure, a full security perimeter has been established, and entry is prohibited for everyone.





However, certain miscreants attempted to create a disturbance and resorted to stone-pelting.

The police personnel present at the scene responded by using tear gas and mild force to disperse the crowd. Leaders from the Muslim community are also issuing video messages urging calm... The situation is now fully under control. The demolition work by the mosque committee is continuing steadily..."

"We had anticipated this and conducted thorough briefings and multiple meetings to discuss every aspect.

It is precisely because of this planning that we cleared the entire Chhatri Chowk area; there is no crowd here now, and a global security perimeter is in place. Some police personnel sustained minor injuries during the stone-pelting incident, but they remain alert and ready for duty," he said.

The officer futher said: "We utilized tear gas to manage the situation. The entire area is being monitored via CCTV and drones.

We have also been keeping a close watch on social media. Individuals who came from outside the district to incite trouble were detained by the police at the border late last night and have been taken into custody at various police stations. We will now identify the perpetrators using CCTV and drone footage and register FIRs against those found involved.

An attempt to block the road was also made by some women; however, after being counseled and shown video footage of the situation, they withdrew the blockade.

The road is open. I appeal to everyone to please cooperate; if anyone engages in such activities, strict action will be taken against them. As you can all see, this entire undertaking is being carried out by the committee itself, with everyone's consent."

What happened at the site

Protesters tried to move through narrow lanes towards the area, with some women seen being pushed forward as the crowd attempted to proceed. Stones were also thrown at police personnel deployed to maintain order.

The situation remained tense as security forces stayed at the spot to prevent further escalation.

Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi, meanwhile, criticised the demolition and urged the Madhya Pradesh government to take public sentiment into account.

"The administrative efforts to demolish the Ujjain Shahi Masjid under the pretext of road widening should be a bit more sensitive. Demolishing a 600-year-old heritage site just for road widening and development in the name of progress is the height of hatred.

It has come to my notice that when the matter is pending in court, what message does the administration intend to send by repeatedly laying siege to the masjid? Thousands of youth in Ujjain are continuously raising their voices on this issue.

My request to the Ujjain administration is to respect public sentiments and acquire the necessary land for road widening from the other side. Demolishing such a historically significant heritage site cannot be considered a normal event under any circumstances," the Congress MP said.

Road widening for Simhastha

The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain. Authorities have identified 272 structures for demolition as preparations intensify for the 2028 Simhastha gathering.

Earlier, chief minister Mohan Yadav had participated in demolition work at his ancestral home. He said giving up the property had been emotionally difficult but was necessary for the wider development project.

"This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands.

It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.

Yadav said his decision was also intended to encourage other residents affected by the project to cooperate with the administration.

"The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.

Ujjain prepares for 2028 gathering

Ujjain Municipal Corporation chairperson Kalawati Yadav said preparations for Simhastha include several major infrastructure projects. The event is held once every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River and is expected to draw millions of devotees.

"In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.

The road-widening project is part of the wider redevelopment plan aimed at improving Ujjain's infrastructure and handling the expected influx of pilgrims during the 2028 Simhastha Mela.

World.title: 'Medical fraternity cannot be touched': SC cancels Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre's bail in doctor assault case
World.content:
The

has cancelled the bail granted by the Bombay High Court to

corporator Ramesh Mhatre, who is accused of assaulting a doctor at a civic hospital. The court also stayed the High Court order granting him bail on a plea filed by the Maharashtra government.

While cancelling Mhatreâs bail, the Supreme Court said the message should go âloud and clearâ that the medical fraternity cannot be touched.

A court in Maharashtra had framed charges against Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and four others over the assault of doctors, including a female doctor, and nurses at Dombivliâs Shastri Nagar Municipal Hospital following a dispute over the treatment of a pregnant woman on July 6.

Mhatre, along with Pramod Nikam, Ramesh Pawar, Akshay Karande and Sadhana Karande, appeared before Fast-Track Court Judge N P Vasade two days after police filed a 1,832-page chargesheet in the case.

The accused have been charged under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to assault and causing hurt, assaulting or obstructing a public servant, unlawful assembly and rioting, common intention, criminal intimidation and intentional insult, besides offences relating to the dignity or modesty of a woman.

They have also been booked under Sections 3 and 4 of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act and Sections 37(1)(3) and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act for allegedly violating orders imposed to maintain public order.

Mhatre had been staying in Goa after the Bombay High Court granted him conditional bail in August. The High Court had directed him to remain outside Maharashtra until the chargesheet was filed and ordered that the trial be fast-tracked for completion within three months.

After the chargesheet was filed, the condition ceased to operate, following which Mhatre returned to his residence and appeared before the court earlier this month.

World.title: SIR row: Nadda backs EC, sends message to Rahul Gandhi and opposition
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister

on Monday attacked the opposition and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha

over the SIR row surrounding the

, saying, ârepeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truthâ.

Nadda also targeted Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal,

Samajwadi Party

chief Akhilesh Yadav and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, accusing them of attempting to âmalign and weakenâ the country's autonomous and constitutional institutions.

Speaking to reporters, Nadda took a direct aim at the

Congress

leader saying, âRahul Gandhi, listen carefully: repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth; the truth cannot be defeated.â

âFor Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal, Akhilesh Yadav, and Mamata Banerjee, the sole agenda has become to malign and weaken the nation's autonomous and constitutional institutions. This is the same 'toolkit mentality' that hatches a new conspiracy every morning to stall the country's development: level allegations, disrupt the national atmosphere, and flee. This has become the opposition's modus operandi,â he said.





âThey care nothing for national security, public welfare, or the country's honor and prestige. Their only objective is to seize power, not to serve the people, but to nurture dynastic politics and reap personal benefits... The public has taught a befitting lesson to the forces seeking to create instability in the country in the past, and in the future too; every delusion and conspiracy of theirs will be shattered in the court of the people,â he added.

Nadda further accused the opposition of continuing to raise allegations despite the Election Commissionâs responses, saying it was attempting to create confusion and disrupt the atmosphere in the country.

âToday, as the nation realizes the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India) through the tireless efforts of its 1.4 billion citizens, and as Indiaâs influence resonates across the global stage, the Congress and the entire 'INDI Alliance' are, unfortunately, frustrated and despondent at this progress..."

Nadda said.

"Lacking policies and a vision, they are now devising new ploys to spread confusion and anarchy across the country. We all witnessed the uproar created nationwide just a few days ago over a fabricated story. Now, even after the Election Commission has exposed every lie they propagated, they are once again attempting to vitiate the atmosphere,â Nadda added.

He alleged that Rahul and Kejriwal âmake allegations and walk away; they have nothing to do with public interest.â

The Union minister further accused the opposition of attempting to create confusion and disturb the atmosphere in the country despite lacking âintent and visionâ.

âWe saw a few days ago how an attempt was made to disturb the atmosphere across the country on the basis of a fabricated news report. Now, even after all members of the Election Commission have responded to their allegations, they are once again engaged in efforts to vitiate the atmosphere in the country,â Nadda said.

Nadda also contrasted the

BJP

's approach to power with that of the opposition, saying, âFor BJP, power is a means to serve the interests of 140 crore people.â

He said the BJP's objective was to serve citizens and fulfil its commitment to Antyodaya, while accusing the Opposition of seeking power for dynastic politics and its own interests.

Kharge demands CEC's resignation

Nadda's remarks came after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and other leaders demanded the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that he was propagating the BJP's philosophy.

âThey will say like this only, but their own people have exposed them, and their own people are telling. Even a Chief Secretary of Kerala says, our CEC himself told him to contest the election. It means that a person who is in the highest position is propagating the BJPâs philosophy, and he has become a BJP worker. So it is clear. There is nothing. He should resign. If he has got any little moral right, he should resign from that post.

And afterwards, we have to take action against him, even after resignation,â Kharge said.

âI have called a working committee meeting for tomorrow, and there we'll discuss; all the working committee members will give their suggestions. And we are going to fight seriously. This issue concerns the entire country, the existence of our democracy, and the country's survival. That's why we are very serious about this issue.

We'll fight, and we'll see that,â he added.

Rahul Gandhi's allegations over SIR

The political row comes amid opposition criticism of the Election Commission's handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Rahul Gandhi had earlier alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were âall riggedâ and demanded the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.

He also accused the CEC of âmatch-fixing electionsâ, citing a news channel report claiming that Kumar had approached former Kerala chief secretary Jiji Thomson to contest the 2026 Assembly elections on a BJP ticket.

The Election Commission, meanwhile, clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary that had drawn scrutiny related to the functioning of an officer on deputation to the poll body and not to any policy matter.

The row also follows an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and orders related to SIR and other electoral matters.

The reported objections included issues concerning Form 6, voter deletions and access to electoral-roll databases.

The poll body rejected the suggestion that these objections amounted to institutional dissent over final decisions, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process.

Opposition parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT), have demanded Kumar's resignation.

World.title: Satya Niketan PG collapse: Owner seeks bail citing medical condition; court lists hearing for Sept 30
World.content:
Earlier this month, a five-storey PG accommodation collapsed suddenly near Delhi's Satya Niketan.

Owners failed to take safety precautions

NEW DELHI: Delhiâs Satya Niketan's owner on Monday has sought regular bail, citing his age and medical condition, with the Patiala House Court issuing notice on the plea.The court has also sought a medical report from the jail authorities before taking up the matter on September 30, news agency ANI reported.Owner Hari Ram Gupta is an accused in the September 6 collapse of the five-storey PG building in Satya Niketan that killed seven people. His earlier bail plea was rejected by the court, which observed that the investigation was still at an initial stage and the chargesheet had not yet been filed.The court also took note of the deaths, injuries and the fact that one victim was still critical at the time.In a status report filed before the Delhi High Court earlier, Delhi Police said the building owners failed to take adequate safety precautions during construction and repair work, allegedly creating a situation that endangered the lives of PG residents.Police said the building owner Urmila Gupta, her husband Hari Ram Gupta and their son Mahesh Gupta jointly managed the property. The police report also alleged that the premises were being used commercially without obtaining the required land-use conversion permission.Meanwhile, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has launched a major enforcement drive following the collapse.According to a compliance affidavit filed before the Delhi High Court, MCD demolished 543 properties and sealed 178 others for unauthorised construction between September 6 and September 23. It also issued 354 show-cause notices, including 205 sealing notices, and passed 98 demolition orders during the 17-day period.MCD said Property No. 14 in Satya Niketan, which collapsed, had never had a sanctioned building plan approved by the civic body.

World.title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief

and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.

Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victimsâ names redacted.

The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case.

The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a âmanifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on recordâ.

The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on âarchaic and stereotypical assumptionsâ about the âexpectedâ behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.





The case stems from an FIR filed by

following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singhâs tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.

Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.

The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.
